clean_body: Why I'm going all in for Winn Decker in House District 37 | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more Why I'm going all in for Winn Decker in House District 37 | | | Oct 13 | | | | | | | | | | | | I'm on the ballot this year, but nobody's running against me. So I asked myself a simple question: where can I help flip one seat before November 3rd? My answer is a state House race in southern Wake County. If you only read only one line, read this one: chip in and split a contribution of $25 or $50 with Winn Decker. Here's why this race matters so much. Gerrymandering is why so few seats are in play I know what gerrymandering does. It ended my time in Congress. It's the same story in the state House. In 2024, Democratic candidates for the NC House won 51.2% of the vote statewide. Republicans won 47.5%. But Republicans walked away with 71 of 120 seats (59%). That's not an accident. That's Republican gerrymandering. | | ---|---|--- When the lines are drawn that way, most districts are decided before anybody votes. Only a handful of seats are actually up for grabs. That's exactly why the very few competitive districts matter so much. The math on the NC House Republicans hold 71 seats. Democrats hold 47, and there are 2 independents who used to be Democrats. It takes 61 for a majority. That means Democrats need 12 more seats. That's a tall order. But you don't win a majority by only playing in the easy seats. You win it in places like House District 37, where Republican Erin Pare has won by single digits every time since 2020. Why this seat? In 2024, Pare beat Safiyah Jackson 51.4% to 45.3%. That's just a few thousand votes in a district of over 100,000 people. We crunched the numbers, and on the same ballot, voters in that district gave Jeff Jackson and Rachel Hunt about 52% of the vote. Southern Wake voters are open to Democrats. They just need a reason. | | ---|---|--- Even the conservative John Locke Foundation now rates this district . And things are moving our way in Southern Wake. Last November, Fuquay-Varina elected Democrat Bill Harris as mayor over the Republican incumbent. Holly Springs did the same with Mike Kondratick. I know these precincts well. I beat Bo Hines in 2022 in a district that covered these same neighborhoods. These are the independent-minded voters who sent me to Congress. Erin Par e's record | | ---|---|--- This isn't about Erin Pare as a person. It's about how she votes. And she votes with the MAGA Republican leadership over and over again. She voted to gerrymander our mapsagain. Last October, as part of Donald Trump's push to redraw maps across the country, Republicans redrew our congressional map in the middle of the decade. The senator who drew it said the goal was simple: one more Republican seat. Pare voted yes. She voted to take control of our elections board away from the governor. In December 2024, Pare voted to override Governor Cooper's veto of Senate Bill 382, which handed control of the State Board of Elections to the newly elected Republican state auditor. She voted to ban most abortions after 12 weeks. In 2023, every Republican in the House voted to override Governor Cooper's veto, Pare included. One Republican vote against, and it would have failed. She voted to let Duke Energy raise your rates. Last summer, Pare voted to override Governor Stein's veto of Senate Bill 266, which lets Duke charge customers for new power plants before they're even built. Winn Decker will fight for our public schools. He's the son of two public school teachers. Support Winn Decker for District 37 | | ---|---|--- When I take office as your District Attorney in January, I'll be running the most understaffed prosecutor's office in North Carolina. The General Assembly funds 45 prosecutors in Wake County. The state's own formula says we need 70. This year's budget added new prosecutors all over the state, and Wake County got zero. That means victims will have to wait years instead of months for justice, and repeat offenders will stay out on the streets much longer. We'll all be less safe as a result. Here's what gets me. Erin Pare is one of the chairs of the House Appropriations Committee, one of the people who actually writes the state budget. She's one of only two Republicans in the House from Wake County. She took my call on this, and I appreciate that. But Wake still got nothing. If one of the top budget writers in the House can't get funding for her own county's prosecutors, then what's the point of keeping her there? I know one thing for sure, Winn Decker will fight for public safety in Wake County. What changes if we flip the House? A Democratic House can't do everything on its own. Republicans will probably still run the Senate. But a Democratic majority means bad bills are DOA in the House. No more gerrymandered maps (which the governor can't veto). No more veto overrides on abortion, elections, or the environment. That's real power, and it runs through seats like this one. Why your money matters here As of the last public reports on June 30th, Pare had raised about $363,000. Winn had raised about $173,000. She outraised him more than 2 to 1. | | ---|---|--- In a congressional race, $50 is a drop in the bucket. In a state House race that could be decided by a few hundred votes it's mail, digital ads, and money to support volunteers knocking doors in Holly Springs and Fuquay-Varina. In a district this close, a few hundred bucks could be the difference. Here 's my ask Chip in $25, $50, or whatever you can for my campaign and Winn's. Our goal is $5,000 by Election Day, and I'll share updates as we get closer. If you're in southern Wake County, support Winn. If you're not, this is one of the best places in North Carolina for your money to make a real difference. Let's go win this one. Wiley PS: Want to meet the guy leading the fight to flip the House? Robert Reives, the Democratic Leader in the NC House, is coming to my home in Cary on Thursday, October 22nd. That's the fourth public poll in the last three weeks with us ahead. A few months ago, plenty of people didn't think we'd be anywhere near this close to flipping Texas.

But we can’t waste a second celebrating. One point is well within the margin of error, and 5% of voters are still undecided. This race is a true toss-up, and what happens in the next few days will determine how it ends.

So far in this race, Abbott has outspent us 10 to 1, putting most of a $106 million war chest into ads, and we are still tied. That’s remarkable. It means that he hasn’t been able to buy an insurmountable lead in this race, and your support has kept us competitive.

But he still has plenty of money left, and that’s a problem. The latest campaign finance reports just came out:

Cash on hand: TX-GOV
🔴 Abbott — $17.3 million
🔵 Hinojosa — $4.1 million

He has more than four times as much cash on hand as we do, and he's going to spend it all. Early voting starts on October 19. Between now and then, the undecided voters who will decide this race are going to see a lot of Greg Abbott ads, and I need to make sure they hear from us too.

**[We've never needed you more than in this moment — when your donation can have the biggest impact. Can you chip in to my campaign and Equal Opportunity Now before early voting starts to help us stay competitive in the final weeks of this race?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141311230/653139581/1593610140?refcode=261013_gina_yougov&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhZjI5ZWIxMC0xNGM3LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=vXLTgypKgGrMPodscEXQ2NJA9li4-NOIPxfQtznW4eU=)**

The Times was also honest about what still stands in our way. Texas has 20 separate media markets, and national donors routinely pass the state over because reaching all of them is so expensive. And one in five Texas voters still doesn't know who I am. Here's what the last three months have taught us: the more Texans get to know me, the more this race moves. **Every one of those voters is someone we can reach, but only if we have the resources to do it.** Abbott has raised more than $106 million in this race, and he's going to keep spending it in the final month to drag this race back his way. # [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=1079%2E127862%2EHHHc8H)
Folks,
Listen, I'll keep this part quick. Below is a memo my team sent to reporters, allies, and supporters about where this race stands. I wanted you to see it too, because you're one of the folks who got us here.
The short version: **we're tied or leading despite being outspent 10-to-1, and the forecasters are moving this race in our direction.** But that only holds if we can keep pace on the airwaves through Election Day.
[_**Before you read more, can you chip in $5 to help us finish strong and flip Nevada blue?**_](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261013_2_ak.M6Ge6o&amount=5&refcode=em20261013-1072&t=3&akid=1079%2E127862%2EHHHc8H)
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261013_2_ak.M6Ge6o&amount=5&refcode=em20261013-1072&t=4&akid=1079%2E127862%2EHHHc8H)**
* * *
**TO:** Interested Parties **FROM:** Team Ford **SUBJECT:** Race Raters Shift NV-GOV in Ford's Favor as His Momentum Grows Two recent polls of the Nevada governor's race tell the same story: the race is a dead heat, and AG Aaron Ford has the edge heading into November. Public Policy Polling has it tied 45-45, and Emerson College shows Ford leading 44-42. For a sitting governor with universal name ID and a months-long head start on the airwaves, those numbers should be alarming. **The Polls Show a Tied Race with Lombardo Well Under 50%** Despite millions spent on negative ads against AG Ford, Emerson shows _Ford still holds a net-positive favorability_ (41-38). Lombardo, meanwhile, has a job approval of just +1. It’s clear that Nevadans don't think Lombardo is up for the job. Poll after poll this year has Lombardo stuck in the low-to-mid 40s. An incumbent who can't clear 45 percent with universal name ID has no room left to grow. **Those Polls Were Taken at Ford's Weakest Moment** When those polls were fielded, Lombardo and his allies had already spent more than $20 million. Team Ford had spent barely a _tenth_ of that. Voters had heard only one side of the argument, and the race was still tied. That's already changing. When voters hear positive information about both candidates, the race moves to Ford +5. All that Lombardo's spending advantage bought him was a temporary tie. Nate Silver and Sabato's Crystal Ball have both moved the race from Lean Republican to Toss-Up, joining the Cook Political Report. _The three leading national forecasters now agree: Governor Lombardo is no longer the favorite_. **Outlook: The Final Stretch** AG Ford is tied or leading despite being outspent 10-to-1; the national environment is moving toward Democrats, and everyone has taken notice. This race is winnable and trending in Ford's direction. _If we can capture and maintain a surge of grassroots fundraising momentum, Aaron Ford will be Nevada's next Governor_.
---
* * *
That last line says it all: **if we have the resources to reach voters, we can flip Nevada blue.** That's why I need your support right now.
[_**Can you chip in $5 to make sure we have what it takes to win?**_](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261013_2_ak.M6Ge6o&amount=5&refcode=em20261013-1072&t=5&akid=1079%2E127862%2EHHHc8H)

Thank you,
Aaron

Here's why protecting New Mexico's sacred lands is so important to me:

FIRST: I learned from a young age that we all have a responsibility to care for our planet. I grew up fishing with my dad and running through the New Mexico desert with my cousins. Those experiences gave me a deep appreciation for our state’s natural wonders and the places where my ancestors built their lives in the high desert.

THEN: That love for New Mexico’s land and water is what led me to Congress, where I fought to protect the places that are part of who we are. And it’s what I carried with me to the Department of the Interior, where I worked to protect more land and water than any administration in our nation’s history.

Then they asked Big Tech for help.| | | No longer want to receive these emails? | | | | | Friend, In August, the Republicans' own Senate campaign committee wrote a memo about Jon Husted. "More than any other thing in this race," it said, "data centers are the anchor hanging around Husted's neck." They didn't send it to voters. They sent it to the AI companies, asking them to help fix what the memo called a toxic brand. | | | | Here's why it's an anchor. Before Husted was appointed to the Senate, he was Ohio's lieutenant governor, and he helped bring a wave of data centers into the state with big tax breaks attached. Local reporters who checked found Sherrod Brown's ads on this are accurate. Data centers eat enormous amounts of power. In Columbus, the typical home electric bill jumped $27 a month this summer alone, and the Washington Post tied that increase to data center growth. So out of state tech companies got the tax breaks. Ohio families got the electric bill. Sherrod Brown grew up in Mansfield watching corporations lobby for tax breaks and trade deals that shipped Ohio jobs overseas. He has spent his whole career on the other side of that fight. He and his wife drive Jeeps built by union workers in Toledo. We think the choice here is about as clear as it gets. Chip in what you can. | | | | | | | | | | A new Suffolk and USA Today poll has Brown ahead 47 to 44, and early voting is already open in Ohio. Meet Mark Harris:
**Mark Harris is a father, grandfather, pastor, and now a sitting member of Congress who has spent his life in service to his faith, his family, and the people of North Carolina.

Born and raised in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, and a graduate of R.J. Reynolds High School, Mark earned a Bachelor of Science in Political Science from Appalachian State University. Not long before marrying his college sweetheart, Beth, he felt a calling to ministry, going on to earn his Master of Divinity and Doctor of Ministry in Christian Leadership from Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary.

Mark spent decades in pastoral ministry across North Carolina and Georgia, leading congregations at Center Grove Baptist in Clemmons and Curtis Baptist in Augusta before becoming Senior Pastor of First Baptist Charlotte, where he served for more than a decade and guided the church through difficult economic times without taking on debt.

Mark now represents the people of North Carolina's 8th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives, where he serves on the Agriculture, Education and Workforce, and Judiciary Committees, fighting every day for pro-family values, lower taxes, and a government that actually listens to the people it serves.

Mark and Beth have three adult children and eleven grandchildren, and call North Carolina home.

Now, Mark is running for reelection because North Carolina deserves a fighter in Washington who will never stop standing up for faith, family, and freedom. **

**Tuesday, October 13, 2026 -**_****_
_**Yemen** : Saudi-led coalition threatens Sana'a oil site strikes; Ansarallah warns it will hit Aramco in retaliation. Riyadh airport still closed after Ansarallah attacks. Iran offers to mediate Saudi-Ansarallah talks. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is reportedly seeking Saudi approval to join war against Ansarallah; Riyadh opposes move._
_**Palestine** : Israeli forces storm medical complex in Ramallah, raid prominent rights groups. Israeli strike kills Palestinian in Gaza City as four-year-old dies of earlier injuries. Israeli forces and settlers attack olive harvesters across the occupied West Bank. Israel demolishes Palestinian homes inside of Israel a day after displacing 300 residents. Netanyahu orders prosecution of soldiers interviewed in NAZA._
_**Iran** : U.S. President Donald Trump dismisses reports of Chinese and Russian assistance to Iran. International Monetary Fund forecasts economic contraction in Middle East and Central Asia. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham blames Iran for alleged plot targeting U.S.-used airbase. Attacks on ships near Strait of Hormuz reach highest intensity since war began._
_**Lebanon:** Israeli warplanes launch airstrikes across southern Lebanon despite ceasefire. EU to establish mission to train Lebanese military and security forces. 13-year-old killed, 24 wounded by unexploded munition._
_**U.S.** : Texas Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton celebrated New Year's in Dubai with two indicted fugitives. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani orders first NYPD use-of-force review in a decade. Federal agents raid Ilhan Omar's D.C. home in immigration probe. ICE agents ran over fleeing man in Texas, surveillance video shows. Judge orders Trump administration to pull taxpayer-funded promotional ad. Justice Department opens antitrust probe of TV networks over Trump pool blackout. Trump asks U.S. ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign. Shawn Fain wins second term as United Auto Workers president. Elon Musk pours $276 million into Republican midterm effort. Pro-AI super PAC network routes millions through Nevada shell companies._
_**International:** Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Russia violated Trump's "energy ceasefire," vows to respond if attacks continue. NATO warns of counter-attack if alliance is attacked. At least 139 migrants dead, 84 missing after boat capsizes off Djibouti, UN's International Organization for Migration says. China sanctions Paraguay's communications minister and Belize's foreign minister over Taiwan ties. Dozens of gold miners killed in airstrike near Sudan-Egypt border. Cuba denies connection to biodiesel shipments seized in U.S. blockade. Spanish PM acknowledges Moroccan naval incursion, calls it an "isolated" incident. Eritrea and Ethiopia trade accusations of aggression, both appeal to UN for assistance. Gunmen kill at least 20 in Nigeria convoy ambush. Rahul Gandhi leads march to India's Supreme Court demanding election chief's resignation; 30,000+ police block the route. North Korea test-fires multiple ballistic missiles, one flies over 900 km._

* * *
# Yemen
* **Saudi-led coalition threatens Sana 'a oil site strikes; Ansarallah warns it will hit Aramco in retaliation:**
* **Sana 'a:** Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Maliki announced plans for a "special operation" in the Ansarallah-held capital, and [issued](https://substack.com/redirect/6bbbc8b9-9459-4390-884c-a474767d67f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a displacement order near the Yemen Petroleum Company's central Al-Sabaha station.
* Any Saudi-led strikes on the capital would be met with a "harsh and painful response" in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, Ansarallah military spokesperson Yahya Saree [warned](https://substack.com/redirect/b3d71d68-b4c4-4a7e-8014-083c22f23862?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Saree specifically [listed](https://substack.com/redirect/0dcfb3c9-b5b2-4a6a-bc72-44cbd8b6ffe2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the retaliatory targets as: the Dammam headquarters of Aramco, the national petroleum and natural gas company of Saudi Arabia; Khalid Airport in Riyadh; and Aramco's refinery in Riyadh.
* **Taiz:** Ansarallah attacks on Taiz reportedly killed five and wounded 17, according to the Yemeni Network for Rights and Freedoms. The attacks reportedly damaged several homes, Al-Safwa Hospital, and Al-Saeed Mosque. Yemen's Saudi-backed forces reported nine airstrikes targeting Ansarallah positions--five in Dhubab district and four in Al-Misrakh.
* Shortages of medicine, fuel, and medical supplies threaten approximately 1,110 kidney failure patients and more than 190 intensive care patients, Taiz's local health office warned.
* **Hodeidah:** Three airstrikes, including two on Kamaran Island and one in Al-Qanawis district were reported by Ansarallah-run Al Masirah TV, without immediate reports of casualties.
* **Saada:** Saree claimed the group shot down a Saudi Wing Loong II armed reconnaissance drone while it was conducting "hostile missions."
* **Riyadh airport still closed after Ansarallah attacks:** Operations are [still suspended](https://substack.com/redirect/6c2dbdf7-031e-4d85-a5ab-18cbffe6ab13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at Saudi Arabia's King Khalid International Airport following a series of Ansarallah attacks over the weekend that killed 14 people and injured at least 320. The closure was extended until October 17, affecting nearly 700 flights per day, according to Flightradar24.
* On Saturday, an Ansarallah attack struck a passenger terminal, killing 13 and injuring 309, while a separate projectile hit Terminal 4 on Sunday, killing one and injuring 11 others.
* Qatar Airways, Etihad, IndiGo, Air France-KLM, Lufthansa, and Air India have all cancelled flights to Riyadh. Cathay Pacific and Delta have postponed planned Riyadh services until 2027.
* **Iran offers to mediate Saudi-Ansarallah talks:** Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi [offered](https://substack.com/redirect/5248731d-7d68-4f8d-aff9-e6d3d2fe4ca5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to broker talks between Saudi Arabia and Ansarallah, in a call Sunday with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan.
* Iran was ready to help start a dialogue and reach a political solution, Araghchi reportedly said. He warned that "insisting on a military approach and disregarding a political solution would only further complicate the situation."
* Riyadh hasn't publicly responded to the offer. The Saudi Foreign Ministry said the two discussed "the recent escalation in the region and the efforts being made to address it," and that Araghchi initiated the call.
* **Netanyahu is reportedly seeking Saudi approval to join war against Ansarallah; Riyadh opposes move:** Netanyahu is [seeking](https://substack.com/redirect/b53b2792-5813-4be6-b08a-5d266cd4a524?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Saudi approval, through U.S. mediation, for Israel to join the fight against Ansarallah, Haaretz reported, but Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman opposes the move.
* The crown prince fears a domestic backlash if Israel enters the fight, according to Haaretz, while Netanyahu is hoping to strengthen ties with Riyadh and advance normalization. Saudi officials have said normalization depends on a path to a Palestinian state.
* Last month, Lebanon's Al-Akhbar reported that he had offered "Israel's services" in a "comprehensive war" against Ansarallah.

# Palestine
* **Israeli forces storm medical complex in Ramallah, raid prominent rights groups:** Israeli forces [raided](https://substack.com/redirect/15079653-6bbc-46d6-a77e-aadbede5c1d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the offices of prominent Palestinian rights groups--the Addameer Prisoner Support and Human Rights Association and the Union of Palestinian Women's Committees--in central Ramallah on Tuesday, and stormed the courtyard of the Palestine Medical Complex.
* Israeli forces confiscated equipment and files and arrested at least one employee from Addameer. Video obtained by Drop Site News shows the employee, who is seen on video being made to kneel outside the building with his hands behind his head in front of an Israeli army vehicle.
* Troops stormed the Palestine Medical Complex, the largest government medical facility in the West Bank, deploying snipers at its entrances and preventing entry or exit.
* Israeli forces [shot and critically wounded](https://substack.com/redirect/f705848a-967e-4f6b-9555-cde1dd26b24b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Palestinian man and injured a 14-year-old boy during the raids, and injured two journalists covering the raids.
* **Israeli strike kills Palestinian in Gaza City as four-year-old dies of earlier injuries:** One Palestinian was killed and several others wounded Tuesday when an Israeli drone [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/d5c578a1-675a-4fe5-9069-487b2fc784ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a vehicle in the Tuffah neighborhood, northeast of Gaza City, according to WAFA. Two Palestinians were also wounded by Israeli gunfire in the Al-Amal neighborhood and near Hamad City, north of Khan Younis.
* Earlier Tuesday, a four-year-old Palestinian boy died of wounds sustained in an Israeli strike on Al-Zawayda in central Gaza nearly three weeks ago.
* **Killed and wounded in Gaza:** Over the past 24 hours, six Palestinians were killed--three in new Israeli attacks and three due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks--and seven injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. One body was recovered from beneath the rubble.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,389 killed, with 175,423 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,498 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,306, while 838 bodies have been recovered.
* **Israeli forces and settlers attack olive harvesters across the occupied West Bank:**

* "If they are, it's at a very low level, but I don't believe they are at all," Trump [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/180d1020-08d5-4e70-a7ab-f906afa367c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Truth Social. Moscow and Beijing have denied the reports.
* At a campaign rally, Trump suggested the U.S. may have gone too far in targeting Iran's leadership, saying Washington is struggling to identify officials with whom to negotiate.
* "We might have gone too far with the leaders because we don't know who the hell we're dealing with any more," Trump said at a campaign rally in Youngstown, Ohio. "Nobody wants to be the president of Iran," he claimed.
* **IMF forecasts economic contraction in Middle East and Central Asia:** The International Monetary Fund (IMF) [projected](https://substack.com/redirect/8bad6002-19f8-4912-bdea-546ad4e09191?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Tuesday that the Middle East and Central Asia economy will shrink by 0.3% in 2026, a sharp downgrade from the 1.9% growth forecast in April, citing prolonged disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
* Kuwait is expected to suffer the steepest contraction at 16.7%, followed by Iraq (16%), Qatar (15.6%), Bahrain (11.3%), Iran (7.6%) and Saudi Arabia (3.3%).
* The region is the only one globally projected to experience contraction this year; global GDP is forecast to expand by 3.1%.
* **UK PM blames Iran for alleged plot targeting U.S.-used airbase:** A suspected plot targeting RAF Fairford, a British airbase used by the U.S. military in its war against Iran, was "almost certainly" directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), British Prime Minister Andy Burnham [said](https://substack.com/redirect/666123af-c76a-4ca1-91ea-8230890aa4cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Monday.
* The UK announced sanctions on two Iranian nationals over alleged "hostile activity," with Burnham pledging further measures.

The ministry accused Britain of relying on vague language without presenting evidence.
* **Attacks on ships near Strait of Hormuz reach highest intensity since war began:** Missile and drone attacks on shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz [reached](https://substack.com/redirect/f24c47f7-e6d1-410b-babd-73a32cbc98dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) their highest intensity since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began seven months ago, according to the Financial Times. Six vessels were attacked on Sunday alone, while 24 ships were hit in the two weeks ending October 11.
* Oil shipments through Hormuz fell to just 2.9 million barrels on October 11, the lowest daily volume this month, according to Kpler.
* The escalation comes amid increased Iranian attacks on vessels transiting through the southern route, as well as U.S. military operations to enforce its naval blockade of Iran.
* On Saturday, a U.S. fighter jet disabled the cargo ship Ocean Molica in the Gulf of Oman for trying to break the U.S. naval blockade of Iran, CENTCOM said.

* **Gunmen kill at least 20 in Nigeria convoy ambush** : Gunmen [ambushed](https://substack.com/redirect/2adba559-fdad-44e5-9174-5e7bbc0091d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a convoy of traders traveling under military escort in Zamfara state on Saturday, killing at least 20 people. A local resident who helped retrieve the bodies told Reuters the dead included four soldiers, three policemen, a civil defense corps officer and 12 civilians. A military source also confirmed the attack, saying that 19 people were wounded.
* On Saturday, Nigerian airstrikes in the northeastern state of Borno killed over 40 militants of the Islamic State West Africa Province. A military spokesperson claimed that the group was planning an attack on the military.
* **Rahul Gandhi leads march to India 's Supreme Court demanding election chief's resignation; 30,000+ police block the route: **Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi [led thousands](https://substack.com/redirect/4e75f20e-258f-44d9-b889-fb22ceead479?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of protesters on a truck-led march toward the Supreme Court in New Delhi on Monday, demanding the resignation of Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
* Drop Site News contributors Biplob Kumar Das and Fatima Khan reported on the Indian government's crackdown on protesters. "In almost 50 years of being in India, I have never seen such use of force to quell protests," one demonstrator said. **Read the story[here](https://substack.com/redirect/7a7c08e6-0c3c-4815-a89f-d8894a1aa595?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* **North Korea test-fires multiple ballistic missiles, one flies over 900 km** : South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said North Korea [launched](https://substack.com/redirect/c0e1840e-eb43-4ab8-9707-fdbd4056d12f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) multiple ballistic missiles Monday, and that one flew more than 900 km.
* The launch comes days after South Korean President Lee Jae Myung oversaw South Korea's first test-firing of a hypersonic missile on Thursday. Earlier this month, North Korea tested its own hypersonic, intermediate-range missiles.

Photo by Mohammed Huwais / AFP via Getty Images. Tuesday, October 13, 2026 -** Yemen : Saudi-led coalition threatens Sana'a oil site strikes; Ansarallah warns it will hit Aramco in retaliation. Riyadh airport still closed after Ansarallah attacks. Iran offers to mediate Saudi-Ansarallah talks. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is reportedly seeking Saudi approval to join war against Ansarallah; Riyadh opposes move. Palestine : Israeli forces storm medical complex in Ramallah, raid prominent rights groups. Israeli strike kills Palestinian in Gaza City as four-year-old dies of earlier injuries. Israeli forces and settlers attack olive harvesters across the occupied West Bank. Israel demolishes Palestinian homes inside of Israel a day after displacing 300 residents. Netanyahu orders prosecution of soldiers interviewed in NAZA. Iran : U.S. President Donald Trump dismisses reports of Chinese and Russian assistance to Iran. International Monetary Fund forecasts economic contraction in Middle East and Central Asia. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham blames Iran for alleged plot targeting U.S.-used airbase. Attacks on ships near Strait of Hormuz reach highest intensity since war began. Lebanon: Israeli warplanes launch airstrikes across southern Lebanon despite ceasefire. EU to establish mission to train Lebanese military and security forces. 13-year-old killed, 24 wounded by unexploded munition. U.S. : Texas Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton celebrated New Year's in Dubai with two indicted fugitives. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani orders first NYPD use-of-force review in a decade. Federal agents raid Ilhan Omar's D.C. home in immigration probe. ICE agents ran over fleeing man in Texas, surveillance video shows. Judge orders Trump administration to pull taxpayer-funded promotional ad. Justice Department opens antitrust probe of TV networks over Trump pool blackout. Trump asks U.S. ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign. Shawn Fain wins second term as United Auto Workers president. Elon Musk pours $276 million into Republican midterm effort. Pro-AI super PAC network routes millions through Nevada shell companies. International: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Russia violated Trump's "energy ceasefire," vows to respond if attacks continue. NATO warns of counter-attack if alliance is attacked. At least 139 migrants dead, 84 missing after boat capsizes off Djibouti, UN's International Organization for Migration says. China sanctions Paraguay's communications minister and Belize's foreign minister over Taiwan ties. Dozens of gold miners killed in airstrike near Sudan-Egypt border. Cuba denies connection to biodiesel shipments seized in U.S. blockade. Spanish PM acknowledges Moroccan naval incursion, calls it an "isolated" incident. Eritrea and Ethiopia trade accusations of aggression, both appeal to UN for assistance. Gunmen kill at least 20 in Nigeria convoy ambush. Rahul Gandhi leads march to India's Supreme Court demanding election chief's resignation; 30,000+ police block the route. North Korea test-fires multiple ballistic missiles, one flies over 900 km. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Yemen Saudi-led coalition threatens Sana 'a oil site strikes; Ansarallah warns it will hit Aramco in retaliation: Sana 'a: Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Maliki announced plans for a "special operation" in the Ansarallah-held capital, and a displacement order near the Yemen Petroleum Company's central Al-Sabaha station. Any Saudi-led strikes on the capital would be met with a "harsh and painful response" in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, Ansarallah military spokesperson Yahya Saree . Saree specifically the retaliatory targets as: the Dammam headquarters of Aramco, the national petroleum and natural gas company of Saudi Arabia; Khalid Airport in Riyadh; and Aramco's refinery in Riyadh. Taiz: Ansarallah attacks on Taiz reportedly killed five and wounded 17, according to the Yemeni Network for Rights and Freedoms. The attacks reportedly damaged several homes, Al-Safwa Hospital, and Al-Saeed Mosque. Yemen's Saudi-backed forces reported nine airstrikes targeting Ansarallah positions--five in Dhubab district and four in Al-Misrakh. Shortages of medicine, fuel, and medical supplies threaten approximately 1,110 kidney failure patients and more than 190 intensive care patients, Taiz's local health office warned. Hodeidah: Three airstrikes, including two on Kamaran Island and one in Al-Qanawis district were reported by Ansarallah-run Al Masirah TV, without immediate reports of casualties. Saada: Saree claimed the group shot down a Saudi Wing Loong II armed reconnaissance drone while it was conducting "hostile missions." Riyadh airport still closed after Ansarallah attacks: Operations are at Saudi Arabia's King Khalid International Airport following a series of Ansarallah attacks over the weekend that killed 14 people and injured at least 320. The closure was extended until October 17, affecting nearly 700 flights per day, according to Flightradar24. On Saturday, an Ansarallah attack struck a passenger terminal, killing 13 and injuring 309, while a separate projectile hit Terminal 4 on Sunday, killing one and injuring 11 others. Qatar Airways, Etihad, IndiGo, Air France-KLM, Lufthansa, and Air India have all cancelled flights to Riyadh. Cathay Pacific and Delta have postponed planned Riyadh services until 2027. Iran offers to mediate Saudi-Ansarallah talks: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi to broker talks between Saudi Arabia and Ansarallah, in a call Sunday with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan. Iran was ready to help start a dialogue and reach a political solution, Araghchi reportedly said. He warned that "insisting on a military approach and disregarding a political solution would only further complicate the situation." Riyadh hasn't publicly responded to the offer. The Saudi Foreign Ministry said the two discussed "the recent escalation in the region and the efforts being made to address it," and that Araghchi initiated the call. Netanyahu is reportedly seeking Saudi approval to join war against Ansarallah; Riyadh opposes move: Netanyahu is Saudi approval, through U.S. mediation, for Israel to join the fight against Ansarallah, Haaretz reported, but Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman opposes the move. The crown prince fears a domestic backlash if Israel enters the fight, according to Haaretz, while Netanyahu is hoping to strengthen ties with Riyadh and advance normalization. Saudi officials have said normalization depends on a path to a Palestinian state. Last month, Lebanon's Al-Akhbar reported that he had offered "Israel's services" in a "comprehensive war" against Ansarallah. Palestine Israeli forces storm medical complex in Ramallah, raid prominent rights groups: Israeli forces the offices of prominent Palestinian rights groups--the Addameer Prisoner Support and Human Rights Association and the Union of Palestinian Women's Committees--in central Ramallah on Tuesday, and stormed the courtyard of the Palestine Medical Complex. Israeli forces confiscated equipment and files and arrested at least one employee from Addameer. Video obtained by Drop Site News shows the employee, who is seen on video being made to kneel outside the building with his hands behind his head in front of an Israeli army vehicle. Troops stormed the Palestine Medical Complex, the largest government medical facility in the West Bank, deploying snipers at its entrances and preventing entry or exit. Israeli forces a Palestinian man and injured a 14-year-old boy during the raids, and injured two journalists covering the raids. Israeli strike kills Palestinian in Gaza City as four-year-old dies of earlier injuries: One Palestinian was killed and several others wounded Tuesday when an Israeli drone a vehicle in the Tuffah neighborhood, northeast of Gaza City, according to WAFA. Two Palestinians were also wounded by Israeli gunfire in the Al-Amal neighborhood and near Hamad City, north of Khan Younis. Earlier Tuesday, a four-year-old Palestinian boy died of wounds sustained in an Israeli strike on Al-Zawayda in central Gaza nearly three weeks ago. Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, six Palestinians were killed--three in new Israeli attacks and three due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks--and seven injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. One body was recovered from beneath the rubble. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,389 killed, with 175,423 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,498 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,306, while 838 bodies have been recovered. Israeli forces and settlers attack olive harvesters across the occupied West Bank: Ramallah: Dozens of Israeli settlers blocked Palestinians farmers from reaching their olive groves in Turmus Ayya, Ramallah, on Tuesday, WAFA reported, while settlers stole olives in Atara. Tulkarm: Armed settlers olive harvesters in Beit Lid, beating and injuring two women, including an elderly woman struck in the head. Settlers also forced farmers from their olive groves in Wadi Al-Jameh and the Ramin plain at gunpoint. Nablus: Settlers disguised in Israeli military uniforms a Palestinian family inside their home in Talfit, leaving several injured. In Beit Imrin, armed settlers forced olive harvesters from their land in the Al-Naqab area. Salfit: Israeli forces a farmer harvesting olives north of Salfit, fired tear gas toward other farmers, and forced them to leave. Hebron: Settlers olive harvesters in Masafer Yatta, stole crops, damaged farmland and fences, and smashed the windows of a vehicle transporting students to Al-Fakhit school. Israeli forces demolished an agricultural room and water tank and uprooted fruit trees in Khirbet Soba. In Idhna, Israeli forces detained four journalists covering settler attacks on olive harvesters. Israel demolishes Palestinian homes inside of Israel a day after displacing 300 residents: Israeli authorities homes and agricultural structures made of metal sheeting in the southern part of Rahat in the Naqab on Tuesday, according to Arab48. The homes housed dozens of people. On Monday, Israeli authorities destroyed all homes in the village of Al-Dahiya, north of Rahat, displacing approximately 300 Palestinians of the Abu Wadi family. Netanyahu orders prosecution of soldiers interviewed in NAZA: Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu has the country's authorities to uncover the identities of the Israeli soldiers and officers interviewed in the documentary "NAZA" and prosecute them. Netanyahu demanded the Israeli attorney general, the military chief of staff, and the head of Shin Bet "act urgently to uncover the identity of all those who are involved or appear in the libel film" and called for "the opening of a criminal investigation and prosecution." The documentary by filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor details Israel's mass killing of civilians in Gaza. Netanyahu has also said he would seek new laws allowing Israel to strip citizenship from people who "smear" Israeli soldiers as part of a campaign targeting Abraham and Szor. Iran Trump dismisses reports of Chinese and Russian assistance to Iran: President Donald Trump said Monday he does not believe China or Russia are helping Iran in its war with the United States, dismissing reports they have provided intelligence and military assistance. "If they are, it's at a very low level, but I don't believe they are at all," Trump on Truth Social. "They have too much to lose, and we would know about it, and know about it very fast!" CNN that Chinese entities supplied satellite imagery of a U.S. base in Jordan before an Iranian attack that killed three American troops in July, as well as allegations that Russia shared intelligence on U.S. warships and aircraft. Moscow and Beijing have denied the reports. At a campaign rally, Trump suggested the U.S. may have gone too far in targeting Iran's leadership, saying Washington is struggling to identify officials with whom to negotiate. "We might have gone too far with the leaders because we don't know who the hell we're dealing with any more," Trump said at a campaign rally in Youngstown, Ohio. "Nobody wants to be the president of Iran," he claimed. IMF forecasts economic contraction in Middle East and Central Asia: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) Tuesday that the Middle East and Central Asia economy will shrink by 0.3% in 2026, a sharp downgrade from the 1.9% growth forecast in April, citing prolonged disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Kuwait is expected to suffer the steepest contraction at 16.7%, followed by Iraq (16%), Qatar (15.6%), Bahrain (11.3%), Iran (7.6%) and Saudi Arabia (3.3%). The region is the only one globally projected to experience contraction this year; global GDP is forecast to expand by 3.1%. UK PM blames Iran for alleged plot targeting U.S.-used airbase: A suspected plot targeting RAF Fairford, a British airbase used by the U.S. military in its war against Iran, was "almost certainly" directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), British Prime Minister Andy Burnham Monday. The UK announced sanctions on two Iranian nationals over alleged "hostile activity," with Burnham pledging further measures. Iran's Foreign Ministry the allegations, calling them an "ugly conspiracy" aimed at advancing an anti-Iran campaign and deflecting responsibility for Britain's role in the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. The ministry accused Britain of relying on vague language without presenting evidence. Attacks on ships near Strait of Hormuz reach highest intensity since war began: Missile and drone attacks on shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz their highest intensity since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began seven months ago, according to the Financial Times. Six vessels were attacked on Sunday alone, while 24 ships were hit in the two weeks ending October 11. Oil shipments through Hormuz fell to just 2.9 million barrels on October 11, the lowest daily volume this month, according to Kpler. The escalation comes amid increased Iranian attacks on vessels transiting through the southern route, as well as U.S. military operations to enforce its naval blockade of Iran. On Saturday, a U.S. fighter jet disabled the cargo ship Ocean Molica in the Gulf of Oman for trying to break the U.S. naval blockade of Iran, CENTCOM said. Lebanon Israeli warplanes launch airstrikes across southern Lebanon despite ceasefire: Israeli warplanes in Wadi Al-Salouqi near the town of Shaqra in Bint Jbeil district on Tuesday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. Israeli forces carried out an airstrike on Kfar Tebnit in Nabatieh district, followed by another strike on Wadi Al-Hujeir in Marjayoun district. EU to establish mission to train Lebanese military and security forces: More than ten European Union foreign ministers Monday to establish a new mission in Lebanon to advise and train the Lebanese Armed Forces and Internal Security Forces, with an initial three-year mandate. The EU is making an effort to strengthen Lebanese security forces and free up the army to focus on disarming Hezbollah, as part of the framework agreement signed between the Lebanese government and Israel. 13-year-old killed, 24 wounded by unexploded munition: A 13-year-old Israeli student was killed and 24 others wounded Monday when an unexploded cluster submunition during a school hiking trip in the Ramim Ridge area of northern Israel, near the Lebanese border, The Times of Israel reported. Students had found the munition, authorities said, picking it up and potentially placing it in a bag before the explosion. U.S. News Ken Paxton celebrated New Year 's in Dubai with two indicted fugitives: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton , the Republican nominee for Senate, rang in 2025 on a Dubai balcony with girlfriend Tracy Duhon and two Americans who the United States after being indicted on federal health care fraud charges, The Wall Street Journal reported on Monday. Anosh Ahmed and Sameer Suhail are accused of embezzling $15 million from a Chicago hospital where Ahmed was the CFO; Ahmed is also implicated in a separate $195 million scheme involving fraudulent COVID-19 tests. He donated $190,000 to Paxton, including $25,000 days after his indictment. Both men have since returned to the U.S. to face charges. Paxton also campaign money from staff or political arms of five organizations with interests in matters his office weighed in on, the Washington Post reported. Executives at slot-machine-style game maker Pace-O-Matic, for example, gave more than $100,000 while his office reviewed what counts as gambling. Texas Tech regents chair Cody Campbell gave $247,300 to Paxton's fundraising committee the day before Paxton threatened the Big 12 with a lawsuit over a disciplined Texas Tech player. Zohran Mamdani orders first NYPD use-of-force review in a decade : New York City MayorZohran Mamdani the first review of the New York Police Department's use of force in a decade, alongside reforms including $2.6 million in new funding for the Office of the Inspector General and a system to ensure disciplinary hearings finish before accused officers retire. Reported use-of-force incidents tripled from 4,087 in 2016 to 12,348 in 2025 even as shootings and murders hit record lows. Mamdani-endorsed congressional candidates Claire Valdez and Darializa Avila Chevalier have called for disbanding the department's Strategic Response Group. The group was controversially deployed at protests last week, following ICE's October 8 shooting of Oscar Belgal in Marble Hill. City Hall said the review was planned before the Marble Hill shooting. Federal agents raid Ilhan Omar 's D.C. home in immigration probe: Homeland Security Investigations agents the Washington home of Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) before dawn on Monday under a judge-signed warrant tied to an ongoing criminal investigation, the Justice Department said. Omar is being targeted based on immigration paperwork filed in 1995 when Omar entered the United States as a 12-year-old refugee from Somalia in 1995. Omar became a U.S. citizen in 2000 when she was 17 years old. President Donald Trump reporters he had "nothing to do with" the search, after weeks of attacks in which he urged her deportation. Omar called the raid an attempt to "weaponize law enforcement" against political enemies, and House Democrats condemned the incursion as "deeply disturbing." ICE agents ran over fleeing man in Texas, surveillance video shows : An unmarked SUV ICE agents struck Miguel Parra-Hernandez in a west Harris County, Texas, shopping center parking lot on Saturday, as agents pursued another man they were trying to arrest, according to video footage obtained by the local ABC affiliate. ICE claimed Parra-Hernandez ran in front of the vehicle, but the footage appears to show the SUV veering through empty parking spaces before hitting him. Parra-Hernandez was hospitalized and was reportedly in stable condition as of Sunday. Judge orders Trump administration to pull taxpayer-funded promotional ads : U.S. District Judge Jennifer Rochon in New York on Sunday night President Donald Trump's administration to cancel any remaining television ads paid for with $20 million in Department of Homeland Security funds. The ads, which began airing in late September, glorify Trump and echo his midterm messaging, with one touting the capture of Venezuelan leader Nicol as Maduro. Justice Department opens antitrust probe of TV networks over Trump pool blackout : The Justice Department is whether ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox News violated antitrust law when they jointly suspended pooled coverage of President Donald Trump last month after he barred CNN from the White House, sending the networks letters on Friday demanding communications about the pool and CNN's lost access, The New York Times reported. Trump asks Guilfoyle to resign: The U.S. ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, has been to resign from her post amid allegations of improper conduct, White House press secretary Katie Zacharia said Tuesday, according to the AP. President Donald Trump, who appointed Guilfoyle, reporters on Monday he is "looking at" firing her, saying "we're not happy," after businessman Eric Deters alleged she asked him to wire $100,000 to cover her American Express bill in exchange for help with the administration ahead of her 2025 Senate confirmation. The Wall Street Journal, which broke the Deters story, also reported that Guilfoyle boasted in audio recordings about Greek businessmen paying for her travel and encouraged foreign governments to do business with one of them. Shawn Fain wins second term as United Auto Workers president : United Auto Workers President Shawn Fain won reelection with 68% of the vote against five challengers, according to unofficial tallies, with his nearest rival, Vice President Rich Boyer , taking 14%; challenged ballots remain to be counted, and results are not yet certified. Fain's United UAW slate also won the secretary-treasurer and all three vice president posts and will hold every seat on the union's International Executive Board but one. Members interviewed credited the contracts won since the 2023 Stand Up Strike against Ford, General Motors, and Stellantis. Read more on Fain's election at Labor Notes, . Elon Musk pours $276 million into Republican midterm effort: Elon Musk has more than $276 million to Republican groups and his own super PAC since July, making him by far the largest known donor of the midterms, according to figures provided to The New York Times ahead of a federal filing deadline on Thursday. The total includes $158 million to the Senate Leadership Fund, one of the largest political donations in American history, which preceded that group's $149 million ad campaign for Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, plus more than $76 million to his America PAC, which has deployed thousands of paid canvassers and spent over a third of its disclosed money on the Texas Senate race. Pro-AI super PAC network routes millions through Nevada shell companies : Super PACs in the Leading the Future network, which has raised more than $140 million from backers including Marc Andreessen , Ben Horowitz and OpenAI President Greg Brockman , have paid tens of millions of dollars to four Nevada companies whose listed addresses include a post office box, a mail center and a Staples store, Wired on Tuesday, indicating they are shells used to hide strategists and vendors working with the coalition in potential violation of federal law. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Zelenskyy says Russia violated Trump 's "energy ceasefire," vows to respond if attacks continue: Speaking by video to the Warsaw Security Forum on Monday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy there have already been "Russian violations of the energy ceasefire announced by President Trump" over the weekend, including strikes on several energy facilities, among them a power plant in Kharkiv. He said Ukraine was "horribly surprised" and urged the U.S. to "make sure Russians respect it," adding, "If Russia does not agree to an energy ceasefire, we will respond." Trump announced the truce Sunday, two days after declaring a temporary easing of U.S. sanctions on Russian diesel, which angered European allies and Kyiv. Zelenskyy initially said the announcement was "news to him," per Axios, and said a ceasefire was needed "in reality, not just on Truth Social." A day earlier he had said Ukraine would halt attacks on Russian refineries if Moscow stopped hitting Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said talks on a possible energy ceasefire are ongoing but rejected Zelenskyy's proposal for a 60-day truce to allow elections, saying "we do not want a ceasefire" but "long-term peace." NATO warns of counter-attack if alliance is attacked : U.S. Air Force Gen. Alexus Grynkewich, NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Europe, the Warsaw Security Forum that "we will block [any] initial attack" on the alliance. He also said NATO's response would target not only the attacking force but "anything and everything that supports, sustains and controls that force." The comments come amid Russian threats over access to the Kaliningrad exclave. At least 139 migrants dead, 84 missing after boat capsizes off Djibouti, IOM says : At least 139 people, including 15 children, after a boat carrying 305 migrants capsized off Djibouti, the International Organization for Migration said Sunday. The boat was traveling from Djibouti to Yemen when it sank Thursday night or Friday morning. The vessel sank soon after embarking, close to shore, "mainly because it was overcrowded," said IOM's chief of mission in Djibouti. The recovered dead include nine girls and six boys. At least 84 people remain missing. More than 80 survivors are Ethiopian nationals. It is one of the deadliest shipwrecks recorded on the route from the Horn of Africa to the Arabian Peninsula. The toll is likely to rise. China sanctions Paraguay 's communications minister and Belize's foreign minister over Taiwan ties: China's Foreign Ministry announced Monday that it was Paraguayan Communications Minister Gustavo Villate and Belizean Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca, citing their participation in "Taiwan separatist activities." China accused the two officials of "egregious actions and statements" that damage China's "core interests." Paraguay and Belize are two of Taiwan's 12 formal diplomatic partners. Chinese sanctions will freeze the ministers' assets in China, deny their entry visas to Hong Kong and Macau, and bar Chinese organizations and individuals from transactions or cooperation with them. Dozens of gold miners killed in airstrike near Sudan-Egypt border : Warplanes an open-air gold mine in Sudan's Red Sea State, about 25 miles from the Egyptian border, on Saturday, killing dozens of workers, according to Sudanese rights groups, graphic video footage and eyewitnesses interviewed by The New York Times. The strikes killed an estimated 72 people, according to the rights group Emergency Lawyers. Two eyewitnesses told the Times that at least 65 were killed and 120 were wounded. The strike hit an area controlled by the Sudanese Armed Forces largely untouched by the war. Sudanese media and several rights groups blamed Egypt, a staunch ally of Sudan's army, for the attacks. Video footage appeared to show an unexploded Egyptian NASR 400 bomb, former U.S. Army ordnance technician Trevor Ball told the Times. Egypt's military spokesman said its forces were fighting the third phase of "a major campaign to combat illegal gold prospecting in the Eastern Desert," but insisted they acted inside Egypt's borders. Two Egyptian citizens were and a third wounded Monday when a gunman opened fire on them south of Khartoum, Egypt's foreign ministry said. The shooter reportedly belonged to the Joint Force allied with the Sudanese army and opened fire in retaliation. Cuba denies connection to biodiesel shipments seized in U.S. blockade : Following the U.S.'s seizure of almost $3 million of biodiesel bound for Cuba, a senior Cuban official denied that the state had any links to the shipments. "There was no contract of any kind" with the sanctioned Cuban state energy trader ENETEC, Cuban Minister of Energy and Mines Vicente de la O Levy Reuters on Monday. He added, "No Cuban state-owned company has managed to secure a fuel contract, whether for small or large quantities." As part of its blockade on Cuba, the U.S. has seized 90 shipments of what it calls "illegal" oil bound for the island nation. The U.S. has allowed Cuban companies to import fuel since early this year, but it bars oil shipments to the communist government. "The amount entering the country doesn't even cover 3% of its fuel needs," De la O Levy said. Spanish PM acknowledges Moroccan naval incursion, calls it an "isolated" incident: Moroccan naval vessels entered Spanish waters near Ceuta without permission after the mass-migrant crossing in July, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez Monday. "Between two neighboring countries, such isolated incidents do occur," he added. "Those were intense days, but cooperation between the navies remains smooth, regardless of that incident." Sanchez did not mention details reported earlier by El Pais. At least one frigate and several patrol boats of the Royal Moroccan Navy sailed through Spanish waters without seeking authorization, the Spanish newspaper reported on Monday, citing anonymous sources. A Spanish frigate had to intercept and repel them. More than 72,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Ceuta at the end of July. Most, but not all, of the migrants who crossed into Ceuta were expelled or voluntarily returned to Morocco weeks afterward. Eritrea and Ethiopia trade accusations of aggression, both appeal to UN for assistance : Eritrea UN Security Council for "deterrent measures" against Ethiopia on Saturday, accusing the state of making a "declaration of war" He asked the council to "forcefully condemn Ethiopia's deplorable declaration of war against Eritrea." On Friday, Ethiopia told the UN Security Council that Eritrean troops advanced up to 37 miles into Tigray, and that it was prepared to defend itself. Gunmen kill at least 20 in Nigeria convoy ambush : Gunmen a convoy of traders traveling under military escort in Zamfara state on Saturday, killing at least 20 people. A local resident who helped retrieve the bodies told Reuters the dead included four soldiers, three policemen, a civil defense corps officer and 12 civilians. A military source also confirmed the attack, saying that 19 people were wounded. On Saturday, Nigerian airstrikes in the northeastern state of Borno killed over 40 militants of the Islamic State West Africa Province. A military spokesperson claimed that the group was planning an attack on the military. Rahul Gandhi leads march to India 's Supreme Court demanding election chief's resignation; 30,000+ police block the route: Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi of protesters on a truck-led march toward the Supreme Court in New Delhi on Monday, demanding the resignation of Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Drop Site News contributors Biplob Kumar Das and Fatima Khan reported on the Indian government's crackdown on protesters. "In almost 50 years of being in India, I have never seen such use of force to quell protests," one demonstrator said. Read the story. The launch comes days after South Korean President Lee Jae Myung oversaw South Korea's first test-firing of a hypersonic missile on Thursday. | Shawn Oliver Shines in Only LG Debate. The Massachusetts Republican Party released the following statement from Chairwoman Amy Carnevale.
Shawn Oliver delivered a strong, steady performance in today's Lieutenant Governor debate that reminded voters why he's the right partner on the Republican ticket this November. He spoke with the plainspoken conviction of someone who has lived the issues facing Massachusetts families, as a New Bedford city councilor, corrections officer, husband, father, and grandfather who has seen firsthand what Beacon Hill's policies are doing to working people and local communities.
Oliver stayed focused on the priorities that matter most to Massachusetts residents: affordability, accountability, public safety, and giving cities and towns a real voice. He made a clear case that the status quo under the current administration has left too many families struggling and too many communities overlooked.
While the debate highlighted real differences in approach and priorities, Oliver debated with composure and clarity. The Republican ticket is unified and ready. Shawn Oliver showed today that he is prepared to serve as a strong lieutenant governor.
We are proud to stand with Mike Minogue and Shawn Oliver as we make the case to voters over the next three weeks. The choice is clear, and today's debate only reinforced it.

People often ask...how did I get that name?

| [](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmcmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW10cG9zaXRpb249MyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNjEwMTNfRFUtVEIuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDU1ODUxLTIwNjgmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTIwMjYxMDEzX0RVLVRCLjExMDExN190MjA1NTg1MS0yMDY4In0/G2y3ClN-n0CPY6yDPmWgxg)
---
That’s a picture of me from when I flew H-46 and H-3 helicopters in the U.S. Navy. If you look to my left, you can see my call sign...**Blossom.**
People often ask...how did I get that name?
Well, my roommate in flight school and I went on a bit of a “girl power” kick one day and bought old bathtub non-skid flower stickers from the store, cut out that flower shape in reflective tape from our squadron, and stuck those reflective flowers on our helmets.
There is very little room for making a Navy flight suit more “feminine,” but on cruise we were able to be a little more creative and came to love those girly flowers on our helmets.
Although the helicopter community doesn’t use call signs as much as some of the fixed wing squadrons, the “Blossom” stuck and was painted on the side of a CH-46 for part of my first cruise. Made for a great photo and story!
It was my experience in the Navy that helped instill in me the importance of service.
Far too often, our elected officials today forget that their job is to SERVE. They think it is their job to tell everyone what to do and why everyone else is wrong....but that’s not service.
As a Navy veteran and nurse practitioner, I got so frustrated and decided to run for Congress because I wanted to actually SERVE my country and my community.
**While for some it is all about power, for me it is all about service.**
Sadly, this has made me some enemies in Washington.
No one is going to buy me off or tell me what to do...I’m going to keep serving the people I represent, not serve some “master” in Washington, D.C.
If you are also tired of leaders who care more about power than service, [I’m asking you to send me some help today.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmcmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW10cG9zaXRpb249MyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNjEwMTNfRFUtVEIuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDU1ODUxLTIwNjgmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTIwMjYxMDEzX0RVLVRCLjExMDExN190MjA1NTg1MS0yMDY4In0/e04BRxHLt1qI9eWzzkUg-Q)
Because I’m a veteran and not a career politician, I need all the help I can get to support my fight against the Democrats.
---
| [RUSH SUPPORT TO JEN](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmcmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW10cG9zaXRpb249MyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNjEwMTNfRFUtVEIuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDU1ODUxLTIwNjgmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTIwMjYxMDEzX0RVLVRCLjExMDExN190MjA1NTg1MS0yMDY4In0/lx-HvM_QLEM6fVhssM_axQ)
---
I know this was a longer message than you are probably used to getting, but I want you to know where I’m coming from and why I need your help. Whether it’s $100 or just $10, anything you can contribute will help this Navy veteran keep fighting back business as usual in D.C.
It’s time we support leaders who truly want to serve our country, and that’s what I promise to always do...are you with me, Peter?
With the courage to fight,

| **Governor Scott Releases “My Commitment to You”**
**_Governor Highlights Plans to Put
Vermont on a Stronger Path_**
Montpelier, Vt – Governor Phil Scott today released a new 60-second video, _“My Commitment to You,”_ highlighting his priorities for the next two years.

[](https://us.list-manage.com/aPqna4z1MKh?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c)

In the new video, Governor Scott reflects on the challenges Vermonters have faced, the progress made through hard work and determination, and the opportunity to build a stronger future with more good jobs, more families, and thriving communities.

**“Vermonters have been through a lot, and we’ve accomplished some tough things together. But there’s more work to do. We need to build more homes, strengthen schools and hospitals, lower costs, and give working families and small businesses a better chance to succeed,” Governor Scott said.**

**“I have the experience, determination, and real plans to make progress. And if there is enough support in the Legislature, I know we can get it done,” he added.**

The video also acknowledges the challenges Washington will present over the next two years, and emphasizes the Governor’s commitment to steady leadership that always puts Vermonters first.

**“There’s going to be plenty of noise and division coming out of Washington, and I’ll continue to work with Democratic and Republican governors from around the country to protect Vermont and the rights of all Americans. We also must move forward with the work we need to do here at home to put Vermont on a stronger path,” the Governor said.**

**“Together, and with a Legislature that agrees, we will grow Vermont’s economy and make it more affordable for everyone. That’s my commitment to you.”**

_**Help us spread this new video far and wide with a small dollar contribution of $10, $14, $25 or $50 today by clicking the following the contribution link below.**_

| | | | | |
🗳️ October 13 Weekly Update
The campaign season is moving quickly, and we have been busy getting out the vote. Please let me know if you’d like to [help us](https://us.list-manage.com/tueJy6sSPZ8?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211) in this final stretch. Early voting began last week, and if you vote by mail, your ballot should have arrived by now. I took advantage of early voting on the very first day at ASU West. If you live in Maricopa County, you can find your nearest voting location [**HERE**](https://us.list-manage.com/149NMxUiDAP?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211).Thank you to everyone who has reached out to let me know you have already cast your vote, or to ask questions about the ballot measures. It has truly been an honor to serve you in the Arizona State Senate since July 2023, and I hope to earn the opportunity to continue serving you for another two-year term.Our campaign has made significant investments in direct mail, digital outreach, and voter contact efforts to ensure we are reaching every likely targeted voter in Legislative District 2. If you are able, I would be grateful for your support with a contribution [**HERE**](https://us.list-manage.com/19mAYn31GFq?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211).Legislative District 2 remains one of this state’s most competitive legislative districts, with an R+1 voter registration advantage. This race is expected to be extremely close, and every vote and every dollar truly matters. While we've built a strong grassroots get out to vote campaign, our opponents continue to receive substantial financial support from out-of-state big labor groups seeking to influence the outcome of this race. For us to maintain control of our slim Republican majority in the State Senate, I need to win this race. With your help, we can. We cannot afford to let up in these final weeks. Your [contribution](https://us.list-manage.com/umYZBJokCN_?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211) will help us expand our voter outreach, strengthen our get-out-the-vote efforts, and ensure we can respond effectively to misleading attacks and misinformation. Whether it's $25, $50, $100, or any amount you're comfortable giving, your investment will help us finish strong and continue delivering results for our community.**If you have already donated, thank you. If you've been considering**[**contributing**](https://us.list-manage.com/GC9gdADZ8kt?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211)**, now is the time. Together, we can keep Legislative District 2 moving forward.**
🏛️ Legislative Representation at Community EventsLater today, I will attend the Arizona Chamber of Commerce's annual Manufacturer of the Year Awards, honoring leaders in Arizona's manufacturing sector. Tomorrow, I will represent the Republican legislative caucus at the Ivory Prize Summit at Arizona State University, where housing affordability and innovation will be among the key topics discussed.

## ✍️ All Hands-on Deck
A huge thank you to our dedicated postcard-writing volunteers. Every postcard targeting mail-in voters has been mailed, and 95 percent of the postcards targeting in-person voters have already gone out. Your efforts are making a difference. THANK YOU!
📋 What's on Your Ballot?As I mentioned in previous email updates, Arizona voters will be deciding several ballot measures this November. You should have received the official publicity pamphlet and other official voter guides in the mail.If you misplaced your voter guide, you can review the statewide ballot measures [**HERE**](https://us.list-manage.com/lst3T8EyJo_?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211).
🎓 Protecting Our Educational OptionsLast week, I had the opportunity to represent Arizona on a "Freedom Revolution" panel at the Power of Innovation Summit: The Power of Freedom alongside Iowa Governor Kim Reynolds and other education leaders from across the country.It is vital that the nationwide school choice movement remains strong, so every child can succeed, regardless of where they live. | | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

Case File No DRT-ED-HANEDA · Special File · Built for People
Airports, Factories and Warehouses Were Built for Humans. That’s Exactly Why Humanoid Robots Are Moving In.
Japan Airlines is putting humanoid robots to work at Tokyo’s Haneda Airport. BMW’s robot helped build 30,000 cars. Tesla turned its Fremont car line into a robot line. Every one of these machines has to see the world the way we do, and that’s where the quiet money is.
Threat level 3/5 — Guarded
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
Here’s why humanoid robots suddenly make sense. Every airport, factory and warehouse on earth was designed around people: our height, our hands, our way of walking through doors and up stairs. Rebuilding all of it for machines would cost a fortune. Building machines that fit into the world as it is turns out to be cheaper.
The evidence board
| | The Robots Are Already at Work
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the airport.** In May 2026, Japan Airlines’ ground handling unit began a roughly three-year humanoid robot program at Haneda Airport. The robots start by moving cargo containers. The plan is to expand to baggage loading and cabin cleaning.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the factory.** At BMW’s plant in South Carolina, a humanoid robot loaded about 90,000 parts and helped build more than 30,000 cars over an 11-month program, working full 10-hour shifts by the end.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the scale-up.** Tesla ended the Model S and Model X and converted that space at its Fremont factory into a robot line designed for up to 1 million units a year.
| OUR THEORY
---
Airlines are among the most safety-obsessed businesses on earth. When one of them puts humanoids next to its ground crews, it means the technology has moved from science project to real work.
The detail most people miss
| | Every Robot Has to See
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
A humanoid working on an airport ramp or a factory floor has to recognize bags, containers, people and obstacles in real time. Industry executives say customers are putting as many as six to 12 cameras on each humanoid, and the newest robots even have cameras in their palms.
Why it matters to you
| | Where the Money Flows
---|---
| →| **Every robot needs vision.** Whoever wins the robot race, each unit needs cameras and the AI to interpret them.
---|---
| →| **Volume multiplies.** Millions of robots times several cameras each adds up to a huge new market.
---|---
| →| **The supplier is often overlooked.** Investors chase the famous robot makers while the suppliers quietly book the orders.
---|---
| ClassificationExperimental phase: over
---
Airports, car plants and now dedicated robot factories. Humanoids are going to work in the places built for us, and the technology that lets them see is one of the few things every single one of them needs.

subject: Who's paying for this? You are, Peter.
body:
Our tax dollars should go to healthcare, education, and housing. Not ICE. | | | Peter, Congress handed over more than $100 billion of OUR tax dollars to ICE. And what is it getting us? Grainy security footage of traumatized children watching immigration agents brutalize and arrest their parents. ## **The 13-Day Vanishing Act: How James Talarico Bungled the Flu**
In the middle of a high-stakes campaign, momentum is everything. When candidates disappear, voters start asking questions - and when the candidate's explanation doesn't line up, those questions turn into severe political liability.
Enter Texas Democrat Senate nominee James Talarico.
After returning from a late-September campaign trip to New York City, Talarico essentially vanished off the campaign grid for nearly two weeks. When pressed on his whereabouts, his team cited a case of the flu. But as the days dragged on without a video message, a quick phone call, or a simple "proof of life" post, speculation spread rapidly across social media.
