Yesterday, federal agents raided Congresswoman Ilhan Omar's home. The pretext? A bullshit conspiracy theory that she married her brother, one they have zero evidence for, and a search for immigration paperwork that was filled out by her father and probably doesn't even exist.
Donald Trump has threatened for months to abuse the power of the federal government to go after Omar. Now he's done it.
* * *
**Today 's rant is sponsored by Ground News.**
I've been paying more attention to how differently the same story gets covered depending on where you read it--especially lately, when everything feels optimized for speed and outrage instead of context.
Take this one--over 200 news outlets picked up reports about Donald Trump's potential misuse of tax-payer funds on a personally beneficial ad campaign.
**PBS News Hour** says _Legal experts said the ads might even violate federal statutes, including a law against congressionally appropriated funds being used for "publicity or propaganda" and one limiting the partisan political activities of government employees._
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d0da390b-3f75-4529-b41c-efbb878d600a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Patriot Newsfeed** states _Administrations from both parties have utilized public service announcements to clarify policy and advocate for the nation 's direction._
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d0da390b-3f75-4529-b41c-efbb878d600a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Same story--completely different narratives.

That's why I use Ground News. It pulls together 50,000+ sources so you can compare coverage side by side, see political bias, who owns the sources you're reading, how reliable they are and understand how framing changes the story.

See how the left and right cover the same story, what each side emphasizes or leaves out, and discover overlooked stories in the Blindspot Feed, which surfaces coverage disproportionately reported by either side.

I've been a paying user since before they ever sponsored Endless Urgency. I use it because it makes it a lot harder to be misled. They're completely subscriber funded so there are no corporate interests pushing a narrative on what you see.

See the full picture, instead of just one angle with Ground News. * * *
This didn't come out of nowhere. Trump has spent the better part of the last year demagoguing the Somali community in Minnesota over fraud allegations. That's incredibly rich coming from a man whose family is, by far, the most corrupt group of people to ever rule in America. I've argued before that this is the 2026 version of "the Haitian migrants are eating the dogs and cats." It's a convenient excuse for Trump to demagogue immigrants and people of color, as he loves to do, especially in the middle of an election.
You can feel however you want about Ilhan Omar. That's your business. But you should be alarmed by what's happening to her, because it follows a pattern inside the MAGA movement that I know intimately.
It goes like this. They decide they don't like somebody. Maybe that person is standing in their way, or maybe there's just something to gain by going after them. So they turn to the fringe of the internet, people like Laura Loomer, to cook up a conspiracy theory. They manufacture fake reporting. They lie, they cheat, they steal. Then they fire up the MAGA media machine and point it at their target.
Eventually they create the conditions where enough people believe something happened, and because that something "happened," the federal government now has to step in.
I know because they did it to me. They decided, out of thin air, that I was somehow involved in Donald Trump's fraud case. It wasn't rooted in anything real. They doctored a bunch of evidence that didn't even make sense and just ran with it. It was total bullshit. But it didn't matter, because it ended with the House Judiciary Committee and Trump's DOJ investigating my company over nothing. And make no mistake about what it actually was: a fishing expedition to go after my clients. It cost me time, energy, and hundreds of thousands of dollars to defend my business. All because they could. Because they didn't like me, and they didn't like my business partner.
Now they're running the same play on James Talarico. Talarico, a man with type 1 diabetes, got the flu, which can put you down for quite a while and he needed to take a week off to rest. Republicans, by way of weird, crazy online influencers like Spencer Pratt and Nick Sortor, spun that into a conspiracy theory that engulfed the entire MAGA movement on X for the last. They went so far as to doctor a fake phone call with a mental institution claiming Talarico had checked himself in, with no evidence whatsoever. They ended up looking like idiots.

My team and I use it because it helps cut through the noise.

[ Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/d0da390b-3f75-4529-b41c-efbb878d600a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
It's all staggeringly weird, disgusting shit. These people do not live in the same reality as the rest of us. They concoct their own reality to back up their lies, and way too many people believe them, with plenty of help from Russian bot farms along the way.
And it shows you just how desperate they are. According to the polling, the Republican base has never been more depressed. They can't get their people to show up for anything anymore. So they're throwing red meat. And what's redder meat than a Somali-American congresswoman the MAGA base already hates, one they've spent a decade demagoguing and calling corrupt and crooked? They'll invent whatever justification they need and abuse whatever power they have to get their voters off the couch.
They're going to keep doing it. It's going to get more dangerous, and more people are going to get hurt.
We have to take these people seriously for the threat they pose, and we have to actually stop them.
The level of criminality, abuse of power, corruption, and cravenness we're living through in Washington right now is unprecedented. That means the accountability will have to be unprecedented too. That will require our next generation of Democratic leaders to make a lot of very uncomfortable decisions. If they aren't prepared to make them, they shouldn't be running for leadership in the first place.
Our country should be better than this. Right now, we're not. And this is not sustainable.

body:
Are you able to join me?

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/01d44afb985f/join-me-rep-diana-degette-for-lunch-in-ca-17667075?e=feea60f246)

### Dear Peter,

I wanted to ensure you saw the below invite for my annual Fall Luncheon. This November’s midterm elections are the best opportunity Democrats have to put a check on Trump’s disastrous policy agenda. My House Democratic colleagues and I have been working tirelessly to support candidates running in purple seats - right here in California and throughout the country. But we can't do it without your help.

Every phone call, door knock, or contribution gets us closer to winning back control of Congress. **Will you join me by RSVPing below to my annual Fall Luncheon on Thursday, October 22nd in Daly City from 12:00-1:30pm?** Any level of support will allow me to help California Democrats who are running to flip red districts into blue seats next Congress.
---
| [RSVP HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/VVJdM94Tula?e=feea60f246&c2id=eff6f64158732e8851993770f57c9616)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/MNDepa0daob?e=feea60f246&c2id=eff6f64158732e8851993770f57c9616)
| [RSVP HERE ](https://us.list-manage.com/oggGH2P0yJQ?e=feea60f246&c2id=eff6f64158732e8851993770f57c9616)
---
| |

Prop 50 provided House Democrats with five pick up opportunities in California. We must win these five seats so we can regain a majority, conduct oversight into Trump’s corrupt self-dealing, overturn the draconian Medicaid cuts in Republican’s One Big Ugly Bill, and create an economy that works for everyone. But in order to do that, it will take all of us.
---
| [CLICK HERE TO JOIN ME](https://us.list-manage.com/qmyY4ZaC2OM?e=feea60f246&c2id=eff6f64158732e8851993770f57c9616)
---
| |

During the first two years of Trump’s second term, my House Democratic colleagues and I fought hard against extreme Republican budget bills that gutted crucial safety net programs, pushed back against Trump’s inhumane immigration enforcement, and voted multiple times to halt U.S. military intervention in Iran.

With your help, Democrats can take back the House and expand our opposition to the extreme MAGA movement. On day one, we will take action to defend our democratic institutions, ensure our federal budget is responsibly balanced, and protect our nation from authoritarianism. More than ever, we need a strong unified Democratic majority so future generations may inherit a democratic republic.

We have 21 days remaining until the midterm elections. 21 days to fight for our future. I hope you’ll join me in this fight by RSVPing below. I’ll see you on October 22nd.

For more info contact Carol Ong at [ong102825@aol.com](mailto:ong102825@aol.com).
---
| [RSVP HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/3DliU4TMQi2?e=feea60f246&c2id=eff6f64158732e8851993770f57c9616)

name: Barlow For Wyo
subject: Barlow For Wyoming Newsletter
body:
EARLY VOTING IS OPEN!
| | | | | | [ ](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M4V0BEM3YVDR32RCEXYJAVXN_0)
---
| **Welcome to the Barlow for Wyoming Newsletter. Your hub for latest news, information and upcoming events.**
---
|
---
| | |
---
| **EARLY VOTING IS OPEN!**
---
| Hi Friends,Early voting began last week, and Wyoming voters are already casting ballots. Please consider getting out and voting early!Despite our success in the primary, there is still a lot on the line. People who have never set foot in Wyoming want to decide what Wyoming becomes. I believe our future should be decided by the people who call Wyoming home. We want local control of our land, schools, healthcare, and way of life. We have shown that citizens WILL push back against the misleading forces that have flooded our state for too long. Please vote in the general election; it's important.Kelly and I spent last week on the trail with people working every day to make our future better. From healthcare and business to community service and the next generation of Wyoming leaders, we heard ideas and saw people putting them to work. Thank you to everyone who welcomed us and took the time to [visit. Read](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M4V0BEM3YVDR32RCEXYJAVXN_1) more about our visits below.At the Wyoming Primary Care Symposium, we shared an update on our Healthcare Strike Team and the ideas coming in from across the state. Our team is working through ideas from more than 100 survey responses and over 300 people who answered the call to participate. Five priorities are taking shape: strengthening primary care and our healthcare workforce, rural access, affordability, mental health and substance abuse care, and maternal health. I am grateful to the Mental Health PAC for recognizing my work to sustain funding for 988, access to care, and suicide prevention education for all of Wyoming. World Mental Health Day also reminded us that looking out for one another includes helping people get the care they need.That’s what I’ll fight for as governor, and it’s why every early vote matters.On Wednesday, Oct 14, at 7:00 pm, the Governor's Debate, sponsored by PBS, Cowboy State Daily, and Wyoming Public Media, will air on Wyoming PBS. If you are in the Riverton area, consider attending in person at the Riverton High School Auditorium. There are true differences of opinion to be discussed on what Wyoming needs and can afford, from property taxes to healthcare to education. Please tune in and get informed. Link [HERE](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M4V0BEM3YVDR32RCEXYJAVXN_2). Already voted? Thank you. Now forward this to three friends and make sure they’ve voted too. Thank you for helping us push through to November 3rd!Eric
---
|
---
| **IN CASE YOU MISSED IT**
---
| **VIDEO MESSAGING** We have most of the videos we have created posted on our Barlow for Wyoming YouTube page, which should make it easy for you to access and share them. You can access the page [here](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M4V0BEM3YVDR32RCEXYJAVXN_3)[
](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M4V0BEM3YVDR32RCEXYJAVXN_4)

---
|
---
| | | **REVISIT THE BARLOW FOR GOVERNOR WEBSITE!** [The Facts](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M4V0BEM3YVDR32RCEXYJAVXN_6)[Positions](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M4V0BEM3YVDR32RCEXYJAVXN_7)[Healthcare Strike Team](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M4V0BEM3YVDR32RCEXYJAVXN_8)
---
| | |
---
| | [ SUPPORT ERIC! ](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M4V0BEM3YVDR32RCEXYJAVXN_9)
---
| **IN THE NEWS**
---
| | | **COWBOY STATE DAILY RADIO**[ Cowboy State Daily Show With Jake](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M4V0BEM3YVDR32RCEXYJAVXN_10)**WYOMING NEWS**[Barlow Talks Workforce, Healthcare, Youth Retention in Rock Springs](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M4V0BEM3YVDR32RCEXYJAVXN_11)
---
| **WYOMING PUBLIC RADIO**[ Interview With Eric Barlow, Republican Party Candidate For Governor](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M4V0BEM3YVDR32RCEXYJAVXN_12)**COWBOY STATE DAILY**[ Tom Lubnau: Setting Barlow’s Record Straight](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M4V0BEM3YVDR32RCEXYJAVXN_13)
---
|
---
| |
---
| October 14, 9:00 - 10:00 am, Tour, Wyoming Catholic College, 306 Main Street, LanderOctober 14, 11:30 am - 12:30 pm, Lander Senior Center, 205 S. 10th Street, LanderOctober 14, 7:00 - 8:00 pm, Wyoming PBS General Election Gubernatorial Debate, Riverton High School Auditorium, 2001 W Sunset Drive, Riverton, or watch [HERE](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M4V0BEM3YVDR32RCEXYJAVXN_14).October 16, 5:30 - 8:30 pm, University of Wyoming Cowboy Joe Annual Fundraiser, War Memorial Fieldhouse, LaramieOctober 17, 11:30 - 5:30 pm, UW Tailgate and Football, University of Wyoming vs Northern IL, War Memorial Stadium, LaramieOctober 23, 8:00 - 9:00 am, Tour, HF Sinclair, 300 Morrie Avenue, CheyenneOctober 23, 12:00 - 1:00 pm, UW School of Energy Resources; Distinguished Speaker Presentation & Luncheon, Engineering Education and Research Building Atrium, 1114 E Bradley Street, LaramieOctober 23, 2:00 - 3:00 pm, Wyoming Women's History House Celebration, 317 S 2nd Street, LaramieOctober 23, 3:00 - 5:00 pm, Wyoming Wrestling Cornhole Tournament, UW Indoor Practice Facility, LaramieOctober 23, 5:00 - 10:00 pm, UW Tailgate and Football, University of Wyoming vs. Air Force, War Memorial Stadium, Laramie
---
| **On The Trail**
---
|
---
| |
---
| **GILLETTE** Kelly and I attended Dancing with the Gillette Stars and were glad to be there for such a special evening. It is much easier to be an attendee than a performer!It was great to see some well-deserved recognition, including The Heart of the YES House Award presented to Angela Dragseth and the Wandler Award presented to Barbara Harden, one of the original visionaries behind YES House.A great community event that supports youth in Campbell County - and this year was especially meaningful as YES House Foundation celebrated 25 years and YES House marked 50 years of service.
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| **CASPER** I joined primary care providers in Casper for the Wyoming Primary Care Symposium. These folks work hard to care for their patients, often with too few hands and too many hurdles. We need to make it easier for them to deliver care and for Wyoming people to get it.Our Healthcare Strike Team is working through ideas from more than 100 survey responses and over 300 people who answered the call to participate. Five priorities are taking shape: strengthening primary care and our healthcare workforce, rural access, affordability, mental health and substance abuse care, and maternal health.There’s more work ahead to sort through those ideas and build a practical plan we can begin putting to work on day one. Thank you to the providers sharing their experience and helping us figure out what will work for Wyoming.
---
| |
---
|
---
| | | **GILLETTE** We made it back to the ranch in time to host the current Leadership WY class where they learned about agriculture and a bit about politics.We’ve hosted these classes for a lot of years and enjoy every group.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| **CASPER** A few photos from our Casper meet and greet at Cygnet, courtesy of Hank Hoversland. It was great to thank our Natrona County volunteers and supporters and meet some new folks along the way.Thank you to James and Beth Worthen, Shane and Joann True, and John Robitaille for making the evening possible!
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| **CASPER** Kelly and I toured two Wyoming businesses putting our state’s talent and resources to work. At Scottsdale Mint and The Wyoming Reserve, we saw how precious metals are manufactured and securely housed. At Mesa Solutions, we learned how this veteran-owned business designs and services generators for high-energy industries around the world.Thank you to Dave McMaster at Scottsdale Mint and Cruz Cabral at Mesa Solutions for hosting us and sharing their work!
---
|
---
| | | **NATRONA** Kelly and I spent yesterday morning learning more about the services and partnerships supporting residents across Natrona County and beyond.At Central Wyoming Counseling Center, we heard about the important mental and behavioral health services available to Wyoming residents and families, including the center’s recent expansion into Fremont County. A special thank you to Jim Cowser for hosting our tour and sharing more about the center’s work.We also met with the Natrona Council for Safety and Justice Leadership Committee, a countywide collaboration of nonprofit and government agencies working to ensure some of Natrona County’s most vulnerable residents are safe, supported and connected with the care they need.Thank you to everyone who took time to visit with us!
---
| | |
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| **CHEYENNE** We had a great turnout at last night’s meet and greet, and we’re grateful to everyone who joined us and showed their support.A special thank you to Toni Thomson, Rita Meyer and Laura Lewis for hosting, and to The Grazing Cowboy for providing an amazing charcuterie spread. It was a wonderful evening spent with good friends and great conversation!
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
| | [ VOLUNTEER ](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M4V0BEM3YVDR32RCEXYJAVXN_15)
---
| Wyoming’s strength has always come from neighbors pitching in. Join the Barlow For Wyoming team of volunteers who are helping share his message across our state. **🤠 Ride with us — sign up to volunteer!**
---

Three new commercials, a UAW endorsement, fresh-off-the-press postcards, and a mission for you!

Hi friend,

We're just three weeks away from Election Day, and Maria's message is reaching more people across Northeast Ohio.
This week, we're excited to share **three important developments** from the campaign!

**Lights. Camera. Maria!**
It's official! Maria's first campaign commercials are here, and we're excited for you to see them!
We've spent months traveling across Northeast Ohio, listening to voters, and talking about the issues that matter most. Now we're taking those conversations to the screen.

From the rising cost of living to the chaos in Washington, Maria isn't afraid to say what needs to be said. And her message is simple: Northeast Ohio deserves a representative who listens, shows up, and fights for the people who live here.Grab some popcorn, hit play, and meet the voice Northeast Ohio needs in Congress!

Click on the video images below to view!

**The United Auto Workers Endorse Maria!**
We're also proud to announce that Maria has received the endorsement of the United Auto Workers (UAW).
This endorsement is especially meaningful to Maria. Her mother was a proud UAW member, and Maria grew up understanding what union membership meant to working families in Northeast Ohio.
Unions helped generations of families secure better wages, safer workplaces, healthcare, and retirement benefits. Maria knows those gains helped build the middle class and strengthen our communities.

| | When doctors told Kulsum Ali to take her husband home to die, she refused to give up. Mir was fighting for his life, and the medical team had lost hope. But Kulsum wasn’t ready to accept that her husband's story was over. Mir’s journey from smoking to vaping ultimately led to a double lung transplant. Today, he is a walking miracle, and Kulsum’s story is a powerful reminder of the dangers of vaping and the importance of standing up for the people we love. On today’s episode of the Moms for America Podcast, Kulsum shares the frightening reality her family faced, the health consequences that changed their lives forever, and why advocating for your loved ones can make all the difference. When doctors have exhausted their options and hope seems out of reach, asking questions, seeking answers, and continuing to fight for the care your family needs matters. Every family deserves to understand the risks, ask difficult questions, and have the courage to speak up when something doesn’t feel right. Full episode available now on [YouTube](https://momsforamerica.us/so/62Q4rddzK/c?w=waV8aX8itnGaIYFFqLbztPhqe6bU_WjWb9Y3GDdVenY.), [Rumble](https://momsforamerica.us/so/62Q4rddzK/c?w=gbHZP0jJLTD31kbBCoJmMEpScwpqokadv1dUOrs8Vo8.), [Spotify](https://momsforamerica.us/so/62Q4rddzK/c?w=wxQlUoTNPILvYUZ6zhGRSTo0OBLwCYlv7VgTLdtkPNs.), and [Apple](https://momsforamerica.us/so/62Q4rddzK/c?w=pTQoGD_fk4WQxerpKAafYQsG9f9CvpC2qWza3-5v6wA.).

Josh Turek here, Dem nominee for Senate in Iowa.
I’ll level with you, Peter:
**Even though this open U.S. Senate seat is rated a Toss-Up, I’m still an underdog.**
A big part of that is money. My Republican opponent Ashley Hinson and her allies just outspent me nearly 2:1 onTV, and their planned spending in Iowa just hit $100 million.
Fortunately, I’ve been defying the odds all my life.
I wasn’t supposed to win my Iowa State House races. I went door to door, crawling up stairs, dragging my wheelchair after me to talk to voters face-to-face.
_That’s how I won a deep-red Trump district.**Twice.**_
If I had time in this campaign to drag myself up to every front porch in Iowa, believe me, I would. But I don’t. The only way we can win is to get our message out to undecided voters across the state. On TV, in mailboxes, and in person.
To do that, we need money. Today. Not in a month or even two weeks. Right now.

| | | | | | | | | | | | Friend, **A Democrat just got demolished on the debate stage, and she did it to herself.** Lt. Gov. John Rodgers had one shot. **One question.** He asked Molly Gray why she never spoke out about the labor violations on her family farm. Why she stayed silent while migrant workers were mistreated on her family's ground. Whether she used her influence to steer the investigation. _**She called it a new low.**_ _**She told him to ask something else.**_ _**She NEVER answered.**_ Play the clip. A Democrat, put on the spot in front of the whole state, and her first instinct was to be offended that anyone dared bring it up. **No explanation. No denial. A dodge.** **That is the modern Democratic Party in 20 seconds. Hard question. Smug answer. Zero accountability. ** Rodgers asked it twice. She still would not say the words. Vermont Democrats are already pretending it did not happen. **We will not.** This clip is a weapon. Help us put this clip in front of every voter we can reach before November 3. Ever since we kicked off this campaign, I’ve shown up to every county and corner of our state. This mattered deeply to me, because we all know actions speak louder than words — and my goal has always been to show you that I’m committed to listening, making policy plans, governing, and being accountable to you, the folks I’m running to serve. That’s why I am heading out on a statewide bus tour this week, meeting Coloradans where they are, and hearing what’s on their minds.
**Folks, the conversations I’ve had on all my trips have reinforced a core truth: here in Colorado, we’re facing a long list of issues.** Too many folks can’t afford their rent, and buying a home is out of reach. All 64 counties are feeling the effects of climate change. Our kids can’t see a future here.
And to top it off, the Trump administration has _repeatedly_ tried to intimidate and bully our state into going along with their lawless agenda.
**These fights aren’t always easy, and these issues can be complex. But to me, they’re more than worth it.**
I’m running for governor because I’m prepared to get to work for all of us, starting on day one. The first step to solving complex problems is showing up and listening — **and on that front, I’m putting the pedal to the metal.**

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

Asking Virginians to re-hire me to the U.S. Senate is a humbling task, and it’s one that I do not take lightly.

But after seeing the damage Trump and his acolytes are doing to this country – and the big challenges facing our Commonwealth and our nation – I couldn’t give up the fight.

**Now, my campaign’s FINAL FEC fundraising deadline before Election Day is in less than 48 hours and I’m asking for your support. Will you chip in to my reelection campaign before midnight tomorrow? Here’s the best link to use:**

_But it’s also about laying out a positive vision for my next term:_

I’m running to **bring down costs** for working families, so a trip to the grocery store or a refuel at the gas pump doesn’t break the bank.

I’m running to **fight for universal health care** coverage in this country so every American has access to a basic standard of care.

I’m running to **build more affordable housing** and make it easier for young people to buy a home and start a family.

And I’m running to put some real checks on Artificial Intelligence – to protect our safety, our communities, and our workforce – while ensuring the United States continues to lead on innovation.

Hi, my name is Julia Letlow. If you don’t know me, I hope to change that right now.

_Can I start from the beginning?_

[I was born in the birthplace of Delta Air Lines and the home of the first Coca-Cola bottling plant – **good ol’ Monroe, Louisiana.**](http://links.conservativeum.com/s/c/-AHWGq8LKSTB54RBVg58r24Cqasrt15UfXYE9tXvEJzzEVS6hEfh_IbpJgO6F7bxWyanS24x4cuFWa7jI2n6zKGLLDfnWU0CNqlZsrd1JWdC2C4ohrS0u1qUgEEQtA9aPyjwbliezwMvoRGt8nkst-F3MzKeU5dH0zarHNr8rbd2FdmaHpLKKoId0l0V10HFo5LEFAU8k5JY6rImXvtl4P9A-8g-dJC4O5DbJXrubdjNPwleYbnvYBlhn4sLQ0Cafs7BXR-npjduiIcyLUoqo_oaBmr5c-VNKjA2yqFq21Xu74kM-AC5ZQ4Js3C6m3EFcSsNdiRyfn4yBUHEuTHa7M7KLpSJCVGHVRZMMmH-ToX2xNSdaVoAp1XF86TbRKyrsDJ_BQR_GivPB9A9QlH4Xp9KpvGVnmOMizkwJxZzkT4N_NGEtdEF38esqf6EbeCBVLQb3nuorFVKIIzg_YA4z6PBtJKcl9fDOX9yks7jP4wYYXN0RZ5CGlljyLnMp__rE39MqL6SZYAO7V3HyR-dDZ0RKs_mnl-_aot29aj9pvvRn-BBGSweAJR7mqti7ZcWNVTiDIB78yjctLh35AumCWmQGxfMeAQVxc9M5srb-L2ViDe82siABGfn3yumBATBD_s93IY-QfuE-qSyxHWaJ1S9vZdFtgCmeqaDVQTBaRTSV_5EfEHVPFl9wOLqmZdWAJRUn84k0eVOb5lmMo92wKoYvpMNaKm8Z3AD6U66_ePDpVX1f710whFCEmJKBhAcHKDk9Tpbj5QjzUHGSPNDsKa56SFbPeCrHR04IW2whQITJDckden5uJxA0nfjYjucdviAimrLsHniMIr7UiYEtove2XE_t0nBcMvZ_vbiSRI4l6l8-ia1RUTjYG4AzQqx7cRk4kkAKCy-ArZPjF0LkBo6duS2N9DL4xY-Fy8i8NxKBunTMs8YnsFf2t1ERCC-sU0nrrqFOk3oF0euXmakJy4DGo_9X-soa6A0_ZdLWNfeF88iCfjcxbIiSOFIRwTyArVxw6VqESggLobmQ5SfWiRI/8gLwhT3vXdRKamDeRPPZi9dKPjBY-XLA/25)

Growing up, I was always the most determined child in the group. My dad still likes to talk about the first time I rode my bike without training wheels – _I was ready to take on the world at just three and a half years old!_

Dear Friend,

You and I live in the greatest country in human history--America. And, in 2026, America will turn 250 years old.

That's a quarter-millennium of liberty and self-government-something worth celebrating. **But recent events have led me to wonder: will young people mark this milestone with gratitude? Indifference? Or something worse?**

**We should celebrate our great country by remembering the people who built it. Our nation 's story began in the colonial period, and the habits and practices established in the 1600s and early 1700s paved the way for the Revolution in 1776. **

The symbol of the American Revolution is the**Betsy Ross Flag,** and I want you to have one. **It 's made in the U.S.A.**--and reminds us of the enduring principles of liberty upon which our nation was founded.

The truth is that too few citizens know the story of America's founding. When you display this flag, you invite others to remember and learn about the founding principles of our nation.

Today, you can claim your flag and support educational outreach efforts that **reach and teach millions of Americans** the truth about our history and our great heritage of liberty.

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Abbott’s underwater
body:
We turned a long shot into a dead heat. Now we need to finish it.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
**A new poll just came out showing me ahead of Greg Abbott, 47% to 45%.**
That’s the fifth poll in the last month to show us leading this race. Not tied. Ahead.
If you’d told me a year ago, when we launched this campaign, that we’d be here, I’m not sure I would have believed you. But here we are, and it’s because of people like you.
[**So I’m asking: will you make your first-ever donation of $15 today to keep this momentum going?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261013_2_poll.DVhyVC&refcode=em20261013-2413&t=1&akid=2413%2E299639%2EqoOekM)
Here’s what the numbers tell me:
Texans know Greg Abbott, and they’re tired of him. 52% of likely voters view him unfavorably, and only 44% favorably. **After more than a decade of corruption that’s left Texas families to fend for themselves, voters across the political spectrum are ready for change.**
And the more Texans get to know me, the more they like what they see. My name ID has jumped to 79% in just the last few weeks, and I’m still viewed favorably by a 12-point margin (45% to 33%), even after Abbott has spent millions attacking me.
Grassroots donations from this team made that possible. [**Will you make your first contribution so we can reach the voters who still don’t know me?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261013_2_poll.DVhyVC&refcode=em20261013-2413&t=3&akid=2413%2E299639%2EqoOekM)
Together, we’ve turned this race from a long shot into a dead heat. A few months ago, people said we’d never get this close to taking Texas back. Now we’re on the edge of making history.
But Abbott knows it too. He’s raised more than $141 million in this campaign and already spent over $120 million of it trying to stop us. He still has $17 million left to spend on false attack ads right as voting begins. **The undecided voters who will decide this race are about to be buried in them, and we need to make sure they hear from us too.**
If you’ve been meaning to give, now is the time. [**Can you make your first gift before early voting starts so we can stay on the air in the final weeks?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261013_2_poll.DVhyVC&refcode=em20261013-2413&t=5&akid=2413%2E299639%2EqoOekM)

Thank you,
Gina

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/rz7iouriMhO?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
|
---
| |
# Three Weeks Until the Election!
---
|
---
| |
We’re three weeks from Election Day, and the energy across Eastern Washington is electric!
From the farms of the Palouse, the neighborhoods of Spokane, and the communities around Pend Oreille County, people are paying attention! They want leadership that puts our district first, protects our freedoms, and keeps fighting for the values that make this place home.
We’ve come a long way. Now it’s about closing strong.
Ballots are arriving in mailboxes across Eastern Washington this week. When yours show up, fill it out and return it as soon as you can. Find your local ballot drop box [here](https://us.list-manage.com/d_Q7iRlOSsP?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238).
Every conversation, every sign in a yard, every ballot returned, and every volunteer hour between now and November 3rd matters. This is the stretch where campaigns are won, by people who show up.
I’m grateful to be in this fight with you. Let’s make these 3 weeks count!
---
|
---
| |
# Last Chance- Join me at the NAACP Forum this Wednesday
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/IAiy9AOnlv7?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
| | Click on the picture to reserve your spot today!
---
| | With Election Day just three weeks away, I hope you’ll join me Wednesday, October 14 at the upcoming NAACP Congressional Forum. It is a valuable opportunity to hear where the candidates stand on issues facing Eastern Washington families and communities.
Your presence makes a difference. It means a lot to me to look out and see familiar faces who care about Eastern Washington.
Mark your calendar, tell a friend, and join us at 6 p.m at the Spokane Downtown Library (906 W Main Ave). Admission is free, reserve your ticket by clicking the picture above!
---
|
---
| |
# Neighbors Talking to Neighbors
---
|
---
| | Over the next three weeks, it will all come down to neighbors talking to neighbors! Our teams have been have been putting up signs across the district and knocking on doors across Eastern Washington. We’ve had many great conversations with other people who care about the direction of our country and want to see us finish strong.
If you have a spot for a sign or a few hours to knock doors with us, we’d love to have you [join](https://us.list-manage.com/60iTQIvo0tL?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238) us. We knock on doors both weekdays and weekends, so let us know times that work for you. Directions and materials provided!
Every conversation and every sign helps us carry this race across the finish line.
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
|
---
| |
# Come Out and Sign Wave!
---
|
---
| | We’re going to be out sign-waving in the final stretch and we need volunteers to join us. It’s an easy way to help: show up, hold a sign, and wave at your neighbors as they drive by! An hour or two makes a difference and keeps our presence visible across Eastern Washington.
If you can join us, sign up [here](https://us.list-manage.com/RNrABZW5_Qf?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238), and someone from our campaign will reach out!
---

People ask me all the time why I left the Republican Party. They expect a simple answer. A single moment. A breaking point. There wasn't one. There were _hundreds._ I grew up believing the GOP stood for something. Fiscal discipline. Strong institutions. A belief that character counted, that the office was bigger than the man who held it. That's the party my parents raised me to respect.That party is gone. What's left is a party that no longer asks whether something is true, only whether it's loyal. A party where senators who once criticized Donald Trump in private now defend him in public because they're afraid of a primary. A party that has traded the Constitution for a cult of personality. I sat in rooms with these people. I watched the transformation happen in real time — principle by principle, surrender by surrender. This is not the party of my father, who believed in hard work and honest leaders. It is not even the party it was ten years ago. **It is Donald Trump's party now, full stop. And it is up to us to stop it from doing any more damage to this country.** That's why Resist Reclaim Rebuild is fighting in the districts where this fight will actually be decided — the battlegrounds where a MAGA rubber stamp can be replaced by someone who still believes in checks and balances. **[Will you chip in $10, $25 or whatever you can today to help Resist Reclaim Rebuild take back these seats?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141330286/653201438/-323302678?refcode=261013_rrr_troye&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMmVkYmZkZWItMmFjNy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=SIq2CmiLYZCiKJyDBzZgYc4W6FXxBSiMf4baDIxzV10=)**

[ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek,

If you’ve turned on your TV lately, you’ve probably seen more than your
fair share of campaign ads – whether that’s from our own campaign, our
opponent’s latest seven-figure ad buy, or any other candidate.

You might think it’s too much — and trust me, there are times when I
agree. But ever since mail-in ballots officially went out, this is the
hard truth every campaign needs to accept:

Every ad we run — or my opponent runs — could be the last one voters see
before they cast their ballot.

Derek, I can’t even
begin to tell you how important it is that we get the last word. That when
voters fill out their ballots, they’re thinking about our accomplishments
— not the far-right’s lies.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/17105?t=1001&akid=616%2E245147%2EkYKFHS ]Here’s the problem: Pennsylvania has eleven separate media markets — so
making sure every voter hears from our campaign as often as possible? The
bills rack up quickly. So please, will you donate as much as you can to
make sure in the minutes before that next voter in Pittsburgh,
Punxsutawney, or Pottsville fills out their ballot, they hear from us?

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your

# [JPMorgan's rare miss opens mixed Q3 for big banks](https://substack.com/redirect/0f520ce8-e679-474a-9eaa-db6209fc0528?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
JPMorgan posted its **[first profit shortfall](https://substack.com/redirect/8348bee0-f83c-45ef-8a88-b6d2c7dcf133?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/8348bee0-f83c-45ef-8a88-b6d2c7dcf133?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)in nearly three years while **[Goldman Sachs](https://substack.com/redirect/4039502d-9436-4113-8835-8fd06e58ffae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/4039502d-9436-4113-8835-8fd06e58ffae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)crushed estimates on equities trading, as[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/814106a4-e6d9-4eb6-8b1e-edc88a0ebd8c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[Wells Fargo](https://substack.com/redirect/814106a4-e6d9-4eb6-8b1e-edc88a0ebd8c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and **[Citigroup](https://substack.com/redirect/20547d30-b683-4dcf-af15-bf5ed070d629?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** delivered split results to start bank earnings season.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fcca9f90-8575-4486-a20b-9a24aae15483?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **JPMorgan profit shortfall:** Reported profit rose 6% to $15.3 billion or $5.57 a share, missing roughly $5.90 expectations, after $658 million in securities losses; revenue climbed 8% to $50.2 billion as the bank raised net interest income guidance excluding markets to $97.5 billion.
* **Goldman equities surge:** Net earnings of $5.29 billion or $17.01 a share beat the $13.50 forecast, with revenue up 23% to $18.7 billion; equities trading revenue jumped 72% to $6.44 billion while fixed income, currencies and commodities slipped 1% to $3.47 billion.
* **Wells and Citi split:** Wells Fargo earned $1.87 a share, beating $1.85, on $21.87 billion revenue that missed, with provisions of $1 billion better than expected; Citigroup reported $2.85 a share and $23.85 billion revenue, its strongest third-quarter revenue in a decade.
* **Dimon risk warning:** Jamie Dimon said large fiscal deficits, sticky inflation, elevated asset prices, rising rates and geopolitical conditions "continue to shift under the surface," adding the forces "may be manageable" but the bank remains prepared for a wide range of outcomes.

# [IMF sees 3.1% growth as AI offsets war risks](https://substack.com/redirect/0f520ce8-e679-474a-9eaa-db6209fc0528?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The IMF **[raised its 2026 global growth forecast](https://substack.com/redirect/5ca61ba5-945b-4e1a-a326-f3d9dfcb9eaa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to 3.1% from 3.0% in July, with AI investment[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/5a15bc32-ed06-4351-8744-e177c1b4086c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[helping offset the Middle East war,](https://substack.com/redirect/5a15bc32-ed06-4351-8744-e177c1b4086c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** but warned resilience is nearing limits and growth is fracturing.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fcca9f90-8575-4486-a20b-9a24aae15483?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Growth and inflation:** Global growth is projected at 3.1% in 2026, down from 3.5% in 2025, then 3.4% in 2027; headline inflation is seen rising to 4.7% this year before easing to 4.1% in 2027, driven by energy costs and the AI boom.
* **Hormuz and AI offsets:** The baseline assumes the Strait of Hormuz reopens in March 2027 with conditions returning to pre-war levels by October 2027; AI demand provides a near-term impulse but adds inflationary pressure and financial fragility.
* **Fractured outlook:** Just 32 economies now account for 95% of global growth, down from 54 in April, with energy importers outside the tech chain facing the toughest conditions and Gulf forecasts downgraded sharply.
* **Yield and debt risks:** The Fund warned government bond yields could spike in a disorderly fashion amid record public debt near post-World War II highs, hedge-fund positions and more frequent fiscal and inflation shocks.

# [Oil slips on Trump's Russian diesel deal as OPEC cuts demand](https://substack.com/redirect/0f520ce8-e679-474a-9eaa-db6209fc0528?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Crude prices fell as prospects of more Russian diesel on world markets **[outweighed Gulf supply fears,](https://substack.com/redirect/13d2c929-c9b6-4efc-9899-23ea5126d228?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/13d2c929-c9b6-4efc-9899-23ea5126d228?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)while OPEC trimmed its 2026 demand-growth forecast to 180,000 barrels a day from 380,000.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fcca9f90-8575-4486-a20b-9a24aae15483?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Price moves:** Brent crude futures declined 1.3% to $105.24 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate fell 0.9% to $92.90 as traders weighed increased Russian supplies against **[Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure.](https://substack.com/redirect/fb917ae5-b9be-495e-91ce-41c1361be9cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* **OPEC demand cut:** OPEC lowered this year's global oil-demand growth projection to 180,000 barrels a day from 380,000 amid escalating Gulf shipping risks and Houthi strikes, while raising next year's forecast to 2.55 million barrels a day from 2.36 million to rebuild inventories.
* **Russian diesel prospect:** Goldman Sachs estimated that an additional 800,000 metric tons of Russian diesel could lower U.S. Gulf Coast and European wholesale diesel prices by $1 to $2 a barrel, though refinery outages limit the overall relief.
* **Gulf risks persist:** Iran-backed Houthi militants attacked King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh over the weekend, causing 12 deaths and more than 300 injuries, keeping supply-disruption concerns elevated.

# [BlackRock turns to Treasurys after six years of avoidance](https://substack.com/redirect/0f520ce8-e679-474a-9eaa-db6209fc0528?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
BlackRock Investment Institute **[downgraded](https://substack.com/redirect/5d30adcd-731b-44de-b096-4e86f9aaf508?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** U.S. equities to neutral and upgraded short-term Treasurys to overweight for the first time in six years, **[citing AI volatility and attractive yields.](https://substack.com/redirect/ba7175ea-b8e8-4442-a6af-ad4a32cfc860?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fcca9f90-8575-4486-a20b-9a24aae15483?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Portfolio shift:** The institute closed a long-held U.S. equity overweight, moving to neutral to manage potential volatility around the AI buildout, while ending a Treasury underweight held for most of the past six years since October 2020.
* **Short-end preference:** Shorter-term Treasurys **[were raised to overweight](https://substack.com/redirect/24152b92-8754-4390-a792-68eddd1a4741?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and longer-dated notes to neutral, with researchers arguing markets have overpriced further Fed tightening and higher yields now provide better compensation for rate risk.
* **Yield backdrop:** The 10-year Treasury yield has climbed roughly 110 basis points this year to around 5.25%, near multi-decade highs, after moving above 5.3% during recent selloffs before easing on strong auctions.
* **AI conviction intact:** Core views on AI transformation remain unchanged, with continued preference for AI-related companies, listed infrastructure and emerging-market equities even as near-term equity risk is trimmed.

# [UnitedHealth raises outlook to $20.50 after earnings beat](https://substack.com/redirect/0f520ce8-e679-474a-9eaa-db6209fc0528?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
UnitedHealth topped third-quarter estimates and lifted its 2026 adjusted profit forecast to at least $20.50 a share from $19.50-$20.00 as medical cost trends improved, supporting the turnaround.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fcca9f90-8575-4486-a20b-9a24aae15483?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Earnings and revenue:** Adjusted earnings reached $4.69 a share, beating the $4.14 estimate, on revenue of $112.7 billion that exceeded expectations; net income was $4.11 billion or $4.56 a share.
* **Medical cost ratio:** The medical cost ratio improved to 88.4% from 89.9% a year earlier and better than the expected 89.9%, though costs remain elevated versus historical norms with inpatient and specialty pharmacy pressures.
* **Guidance raise:** Full-year 2026 adjusted earnings are now seen at least at $20.50 a share, the third upward revision this year, incorporating experience through the third quarter.
* **Turnaround momentum:** CFO Wayne DeVeydt cited ongoing management of high medical costs, with investments in value-based care and AI beginning to take hold, including lower acute hospital admissions and higher home-health use.

# [J&J raises guidance as it eyes orthopedics spinoff](https://substack.com/redirect/0f520ce8-e679-474a-9eaa-db6209fc0528?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Johnson & Johnson beat earnings estimates and raised full-year guidance as pharmaceutical strength offset weaker medical-device results, while management leans toward spinning off the orthopedics unit by mid-2027.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fcca9f90-8575-4486-a20b-9a24aae15483?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Sales and segments:** Third-quarter sales rose 5.9% to $25.4 billion, above estimates, with pharmaceutical revenue up 7.7% to $16.76 billion and medtech up 2.5% to $8.6 billion, missing device expectations.
* **Guidance increase:** The company lifted its full-year reported sales midpoint to about $101.2 billion and its adjusted earnings midpoint to $11.10 a share, reflecting strong operational performance.
* **Spinoff plans:** CFO Joe Wolk said the company is targeting mid-2027 for separating DePuy Synthes and is leaning toward a spinoff rather than a sale, noting "we're not cash strapped" and can wait for an optimal path.
* **Middle East drag:** The regional conflict weighed on medtech sales as budgets in countries such as Kuwait, the UAE and Saudi Arabia shifted toward defense, though it has not yet affected costs.

# [Meta rises as "Muse Wonder" rivals OpenAI and Anthropic](https://substack.com/redirect/0f520ce8-e679-474a-9eaa-db6209fc0528?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Meta introduced Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full as its most capable models yet, with Zuckerberg saying they put the company at the AI frontier and Truist seeing roughly 35% further upside.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fcca9f90-8575-4486-a20b-9a24aae15483?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Model launch:** Muse Wonder, available today via the Meta Model API and Muse Code, and Muse Wonder Full for code subscribers, feature Active Memory and Active Focus for agentic personal and professional tasks after a 14-month AI overhaul.
* **Frontier claims:** The company said the models deliver state-of-the-art performance on complex tasks including coding, finance, law and health, with benchmark results comparable to leading systems from OpenAI and Anthropic.
* **Agent integration:** Muse Wonder will soon power the Muse personal agent, rolling out first to subscribers, as part of the push toward personal superintelligence following the earlier Muse Spark release.
* **Analyst view:** Truist said Meta still has about 35% upside even after the Muse-related rally, citing the model's capabilities and continued growth potential in the AI agent space.

| A long ballot, and where I landed:
Your ballot may have arrived by now, and trust me, it's a long one this year.
Some of that length is by design, of course. Conservative groups like Advance Colorado and Protect Kids Colorado spent the year loading our ballot with measures that carry friendly titles but do ugly work, from forcing local police to cooperate with ICE to protecting a tax code built for the wealthiest people in our state. Their whole plan depends on you skimming the title and guessing.
But I think they're underestimating Denver. In June, this city looked past a lot of expensive advertising and made up its own mind, and we'll do that again in November.
[So here's how I'm voting on all of it, with a short reason for each.](https://cefuo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001L8hLQNqJ6gAyJ7vdofI8hgX1hddDL9HBy5T_Ccsqo1_L5cFzc1bH6N1MyGXzcoWExBn14xSpzSpVJozMQkbHfoItUACLmdWpR08VuUbgG9GWu_4ZahC3BnBnUA3aLaql6KKFk6DX4HfpjLBnx-65Fpf3GRTINo-dY-v57eyD_xNoVGeQKRcy8Zav98xCEvUyy6vNd-gicEHYusYVT3AiKI-_CPCbLkfY30F0GW93UmJkbda0RvnWDA==&c=V9vTRak3kshWyiypPJ6tHN7BJ0-NLdC5rmKtt_yXOEvJYxLAKJ2LBw==&ch=nZIqQFiLF3RGZvbpY5KklrUeTQ8-ftpeUaOnhKjUQUD22L1hyyqTbQ==)

You can mail your ballot back through October 26. Or, you can use a drop box or a vote center any time until 7 p.m. through Election Day, November 3.

If you know someone in Denver who's still working through theirs, please forward this to them.
The people behind these measures have consultants, ad budgets, and a lot of patience. We have volunteers who would rather spend October talking with their neighbors than let any of that go unanswered, and every one of those conversations makes it harder to buy a ballot measure in this state. clean_body: My vote on every measure on the Denver ballot, with one line on why: | | | | | == | A long ballot, and where I landed: Your ballot may have arrived by now, and trust me, it's a long one this year. Some of that length is by design, of course. Conservative groups like Advance Colorado and Protect Kids Colorado spent the year loading our ballot with measures that carry friendly titles but do ugly work, from forcing local police to cooperate with ICE to protecting a tax code built for the wealthiest people in our state. Their whole plan depends on you skimming the title and guessing. But I think they're underestimating Denver. In June, this city looked past a lot of expensive advertising and made up its own mind, and we'll do that again in November. == | == You can mail your ballot back through October 26. Or, you can use a drop box or a vote center any time until 7 p.m. through Election Day, November 3. If you know someone in Denver who's still working through theirs, please forward this to them. The people behind these measures have consultants, ad budgets, and a lot of patience. We have volunteers who would rather spend October talking with their neighbors than let any of that go unanswered, and every one of those conversations makes it harder to buy a ballot measure in this state. == | == | == Vote the whole ballot, and bring someone with you. # **Join Us for Our Monthly Webinar**
---
|
---
| Join Autism Health on **Wednesday, October 21st at 4:30 PM PST / 7:30 PM EST** for an informative webinar on **Building Resilience to Environmental Stressors,** featuring **Dr. Candice Staniek and Murtaza Khan** , as they explore how environmental stressors, including toxins, pollutants, poor nutrition, and chronic stress, can impact our physical and neurological health. Discover practical strategies to strengthen the body's natural defenses, support detoxification pathways, reduce inflammation, and promote overall resilience. Our speakers will also discuss potential solutions for **supporting the body's natural blood filtration and cleansing processes** , improving circulation, and reducing exposure to harmful substances. Whether you're a parent, caregiver, healthcare professional, or simply interested in improving your health, this webinar will provide valuable insights and practical approaches to supporting long-term wellness. **This webinar is FREE, but advance registration is required!** Register using the link below to reserve your spot. We look forward to seeing you!
---
| [REGISTER HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/CNJM3Gl7Nm2?e=3a42edfdc4&c2id=8db3279a53aa0d16c24f727ce5cda332 "REGISTER HERE")
---
|

|
# Save the Date for Our Winter Gala!
---
|
---
| **Join Us for an Unforgettable Evening at the Autism Health Winter Gala** We are thrilled to invite you to the **First Annual Autism Health Winter Gala** , taking place on **Saturday, January 30, 2027** , at the beautiful **Trump National Golf Club in Jupiter, Florida**. This elegant evening will bring together supporters, physicians, researchers, community leaders, and families for a memorable celebration. Guests will enjoy an inspiring evening featuring a VIP reception, dinner, exciting live and silent auctions, and presentations from nationally recognized leaders. We are honored to announce **General Michael Flynn** and **Del Bigtree **as our featured speakers. We have also extended an invitation to **Robert F. Kennedy, Jr.** , whose participation will be confirmed at a later date. Sponsorships are [available HERE!](https://us.list-manage.com/1BAq08h4Ts8?e=3a42edfdc4&c2id=8db3279a53aa0d16c24f727ce5cda332) The Winter Gala is more than a celebration. It is an opportunity to invest in the future of Autism Health. Proceeds from this special event will directly support our mission to provide educational webinars, parent support groups, scholarships for families, research initiatives, biomedical grants, and community programs that improve the lives of individuals with autism and related neurological conditions. **For a limited time only, you can receive 20% off your admission ticket with promo code Gala20. This offer ends November 1st. ** Whether you are a longtime supporter or are just learning about Autism Health, we invite you to join us for an evening of inspiration, generosity, and meaningful connection. Together, we can continue expanding access to education, advancing research, and providing hope to families across the country. **Reserve your seat today using the registration link below. We look forward to celebrating with you in Jupiter, Florida!**
---

# Early Bird Registration for the Autism Health Summit
---
|
---
| The countdown has begun for the **2027 Autism Health Summit** , taking place **April 29 through May 1, 2027** , at **The Legacy Center Resort & Spa** in **San Diego, California**. Join parents, physicians, researchers, healthcare professionals, educators, and advocates from around the world for three inspiring days of education, collaboration, and hope. We're excited to announce that our **headline speakers** include **Del Bigtree** , **Dr. Henry Ealy, and Tyler Hudson** , with many more nationally recognized experts to be announced in the coming months. Attendees will gain valuable insights into the latest research, innovative therapies, integrative medicine, environmental health, and practical strategies to support individuals with autism and related neurological conditions. We're also pleased to offer **Continuing Medical Education (CME)** and **Continuing Education Unit (CEU)** credits for eligible healthcare professionals, making the Autism Health Summit an outstanding opportunity to expand your knowledge while earning valuable continuing education credits. **Now is the best time to register!** Secure your ticket before prices increase and receive **$50 OFF** your registration during the month of **October** by using promo code **AHS50** at checkout. This special offer expires at the end of the month. Whether you're a parent, caregiver, practitioner, educator, therapist, or advocate, the Autism Health Summit offers an unparalleled opportunity to learn from leading experts, connect with a passionate community, and leave empowered with practical knowledge you can apply immediately. **Reserve your seat today using the registration link below. We look forward to welcoming you to San Diego, April 29 through May 1, 2027!**

| Hey Peter!
Last month Sean Hannity put me on primetime under a banner that said "radicals," and Nancy Mace went online to question whether I'm fit to serve.
I'll leave it to them to explain what's radical about wanting a paycheck that covers the rent, or child care that doesn't swallow half of it. Working people in this district aren't asking for the moon. They want time with their families and some say over their own lives, and they're tired of hearing from people like Hannity that it's too much to ask.
That's the case we'll be making to voters for the next three weeks. Wednesday at midnight is our last FEC deadline before the November election, and what comes in before then helps us make that case to as many people as possible as we go out to support the entire progressive ticket.

Friends, did you see my email yesterday about Russ Vought and the “Project 2025 surprise” Trump is boasting about before the midterms? Here’s the thing about Project 2025 that keeps me up at night: they didn’t get halfway through their blueprint by waiting around. They laid the groundwork early, and the _moment_ Donald Trump returned to office, they used that blueprint to start dismantling our democracy, checking off the destruction as they went. **The fact is that we need an equally coordinated response and proactive plan for OUR vision for the future.** So I want to talk to you about what I’ve been focused on since day one of Trump’s second term — not just fighting back, but building toward what’s next: **Introducing legislation to meet the moment.** Just because our party has been in the minority doesn’t mean Democrats abandon our responsibility to champion legislation that would help people right now. On AI alone, I’ve introduced several bills over the last 21 months, including the _AI Talent Act_ , the _Sectoral AI Governance Act_ , and most recently, the _AI Tax and Work Protection Act_ , which levies a tax on AI companies based on their usage and revenue. I also co-led the bipartisan _ATOMIC_ _Act_ to identify and prevent AI-related nuclear risks before they become actual emergencies. And I’m working on more! **Getting Republicans on the record.** The legislation I’m working on serves a dual purpose: on top of just being worthwhile, it can expose Republican hypocrisy in real time. Bills like the _Protect U.S. National Security Act_ should absolutely have bipartisan support! When Republicans refuse to vote for them — or even to show up for work at all — their claims of supporting foreign assistance go up in smoke. That’s just one example, we are doing this on lots of issues that should be (and used to be) bipartisan. **Focusing on what we want, not just what we don’t.** Fighting back against Trump is non-negotiable at this point, but at the same time, just being anti-Trump is not a platform. We’ve been fighting back against Trump and Republicans’ worst actions while also laying out a proactive, positive vision for our future so that we’ll be ready to hit the ground running as soon as we regain the majority in November. In less than a month, we have a chance to elect a Democratic majority full of leaders who will do exactly that: jump into action, reverse the damage, and fight back with a real strategy of our own. **Will you join me? I’m working towards my last FEC fundraising goal of this election before our filing deadline tomorrow, and reaching it will help us execute all our final plans on the ground.** **[Will you chip in to support this work today? clean_body: | | | | = Friends, did you see my email yesterday about Russ Vought and the “Project 2025 surprise” Trump is boasting about before the midterms? Here’s the thing about Project 2025 that keeps me up at night: they didn’t get halfway through their blueprint by waiting around. They laid the groundwork early, and the moment Donald Trump returned to office, they used that blueprint to start dismantling our democracy, checking off the destruction as they went. The fact is that we need an equally coordinated response and proactive plan for OUR vision for the future. So I want to talk to you about what I’ve been focused on since day one of Trump’s second term — not just fighting back, but building toward what’s next: Introducing legislation to meet the moment. Just because our party has been in the minority doesn’t mean Democrats abandon our responsibility to champion legislation that would help people right now. On AI alone, I’ve introduced several bills over the last 21 months, including the AI Talent Act , the Sectoral AI Governance Act , and most recently, the AI Tax and Work Protection Act , which levies a tax on AI companies based on their usage and revenue. I also co-led the bipartisan ATOMIC Act to identify and prevent AI-related nuclear risks before they become actual emergencies. And I’m working on more! Getting Republicans on the record. The legislation I’m working on serves a dual purpose: on top of just being worthwhile, it can expose Republican hypocrisy in real time. Bills like the Protect U.S. National Security Act should absolutely have bipartisan support! When Republicans refuse to vote for them — or even to show up for work at all — their claims of supporting foreign assistance go up in smoke. That’s just one example, we are doing this on lots of issues that should be (and used to be) bipartisan. Focusing on what we want, not just what we don’t. Fighting back against Trump is non-negotiable at this point, but at the same time, just being anti-Trump is not a platform. We’ve been fighting back against Trump and Republicans’ worst actions while also laying out a proactive, positive vision for our future so that we’ll be ready to hit the ground running as soon as we regain the majority in November. In less than a month, we have a chance to elect a Democratic majority full of leaders who will do exactly that: jump into action, reverse the damage, and fight back with a real strategy of our own. Will you join me? body:

| **IN CASE YOU MISSED IT**
**WCAX: Vermont’s $2.5+ Billion School Costs Squeeze Funding for Other Programs**
A recent WCAX report highlights the massive financial pressure Vermont’s outdated education system is placing on taxpayers and the state’s ability to fund other essential priorities.

**The numbers tell an important story:**
* **$2.5 billion annually** to educate approximately 81,750 students – roughly $1 billion more and about 15,000 fewer students than 20 years ago. And about 30,000 fewer students than about 30 years ago.
* That’s almost $31,000 per student
* **$2.6 billion** in other state tax revenue (non-property tax revenue), directed into the Education Fund in the last three years alone.
* **$200 million** spent from the General Fund to limit property tax increases in the last three years alone.
* **$500 million i** n General Fund or other non-property tax revenue may be required to contain property tax increases.
* Note: these numbers do not tell the whole story. The state spends roughly $250 million out of the general fund every year to finance the Vermont State Teacher’s Retirement System (VSTRS), which are school-born costs. In total, the full education spending amount is closer to $2.8 billion or $34,250 per student.

If spending more guaranteed better outcomes, Vermont would lead the nation. However, we spend the second most per pupil with student outcomes trending downward into the middle of the pack.

Vermont spends a lot – more than it can afford – to maintain a system that must be reformed, if we want the best schools with the best outcomes in America. And if we want to invest in other priorities.

The WCAX report features Vermont Tax Commissioner Bill Shouldice, who explains how rising education system costs have left fewer and fewer resources available for housing, healthcare, transportation, and other public investments in Vermont.

**The issue is not simply about how much Vermont spends on education. **

It’s also about whether the state can sustain those costs while providing students with the opportunities they deserve and strengthening services Vermonters depend on.

Over the years, Governor Scott repeatedly raised alarms – and proposed real plans that would get better results. This incredibly important effort finally moved forward in the Legislature, with the bipartisan passage of Act 73 to establish a better framework and funding formula for education – and to bring down property tax burdens.

The Governor’s plan strengthens communities and grows local economies by improving educational opportunities and outcomes throughout the state, with a sustainable financing system that Vermont’s taxpayers can afford.

**View the full WCAX story here** : [https://www.wcax.com/2026/10/07/vermonts-25-billion-school-costs-squeeze-funding-other-programs/ ](https://us.list-manage.com/GAiewr22eev?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c)
_Source: WCAX-TV, October 7, 2026_

---
| | **Tales From the Trail:** With just three weeks left to election day, Team Knickerbocker is more motivated than ever to win this race! This past week we participated in five candidate panels, a VA Town Hall with Common Defense and the Buckeye Veterans Coalition, and had multiple campaign meet and greets.
Last Sunday, Team Knickerbocker attended Omega Baptist and saw familiar faces and met new friends. Kristina can’t wait to come back as Congresswoman Knickerbocker! Thank you, Pastor Ward and Omega, for welcoming us into worship. We need someone in Congress that doesn’t just listen to the Word, but lives it - that’s **KK!** On Tuesday morning, we hosted a group focused on climate change. Together, we discussed some of their legislative priorities for the upcoming term and some longer-term plans to address climate challenges. As a neuro-oncologist nurse practitioner, Kristina understands the health impacts that come from environmental factors, from air pollution and extreme heat to exposure to toxic chemicals, and the role they can play in serious illnesses like cancer. We need a fighter in Congress to make it happen against corporate lobbyists - that’s **KK!** That evening we attended the League of Women Voters candidate meet and greet and a Town Hall hosted by Common Defense and the Buckeye Veterans Coalition about the state of the VA. The Dayton VA experienced a number of staff cuts due to the DOGE early retirements. Rather than backfilling those positions the VA permanently cut those positions leading to shortages in medical staff. In addition, veteran disability rating rules have been under attack in the first two years of this administration. They are willing to start new wars while cutting benefits from those permanently wounded by previous ones! We need to elect a veteran and medical professional who has actually lived these experiences and can help the veterans in our district - that’s **KK!**
On Wednesday, we stopped by four different events around the district in Greene and Montgomery County. Not sure what “No Show” Mike was up to; he wasn’t at any of them. We were welcomed with loud cheers at the Team Kettering meeting. We promise friends, more yard signs are coming! This is what our congress person should be doing. Showing up! We can be busy and present, and Team Knickerbocker has proven that throughout this cycle. We need a congressperson willing to listen to the people - that’s **KK!**
On Saturday, Team Knickerbocker hung out at the Yellow Springs Street Fair and on Sunday we attended Gurdwara with the Dayton Sikh community. This administration has been actively discriminating against the Sikh community with racist post from the [Department of Homeland](https://us.list-manage.com/tj9fhOV_DS6?e=36314ef925&c2id=95485440be040823d6a7108ee922ec5d) Security Facebook page. This is abhorrent behavior and should never be accepted. We need someone in Congress who fights for all Americans - that’s **KK!**
To end our Sunday, we were hosted by artist and business owners at their home to enjoy an assortment of food from their home-made wood fire stove! Thank you to all of the friends who came out and enjoyed a beautiful Ohio evening with us and thank you to the hosts for a lovely meal. Next week is just as busy! We can’t wait to see you all at the GOTV rally tomorrow! Come vote at the Montgomery BOE with Team Knickerbocker at 4:00PM and then meet at the rally when the polls close.
Links for things you may need around election time:[Butler County Board of Elections](https://us.list-manage.com/p5wfDcpotZk?e=36314ef925&c2id=95485440be040823d6a7108ee922ec5d) [Greene County Board of Elections](https://us.list-manage.com/8ejwAn3h2EE?e=36314ef925&c2id=95485440be040823d6a7108ee922ec5d) [Montgomery County Board of Elections ](https://us.list-manage.com/137WoGczkB2?e=36314ef925&c2id=95485440be040823d6a7108ee922ec5d)[BCDP ](https://us.list-manage.com/1AMeEDy2awV?e=36314ef925&c2id=95485440be040823d6a7108ee922ec5d)[GCDP ](https://us.list-manage.com/tPgoaJLqgXr?e=36314ef925&c2id=95485440be040823d6a7108ee922ec5d)[MCDP ](https://us.list-manage.com/gU53a5WL2Pj?e=36314ef925&c2id=95485440be040823d6a7108ee922ec5d)
If you have read this far & know the reference to “that’s KK”, come find Jordan from Team Knickerbocker at the GOTV Rally tomorrow for a special prize!

| | | Peter, As we enter the final few months of the year, people across Oregon and the country are waking up to changes in Oregon Health Plan (OHP), Oregon’s Medicaid program, and SNAP that could affect their ability to afford groceries, see a doctor, or get the critical care they need. These cuts are part of Republicans’ Big Ugly Bill, which slashed funding for Medicaid and SNAP and will continue to be implemented in stages over the next few years. For families, children, older adults, and people with disabilities who depend on these programs, these cuts aren't abstract. They mean harder choices between groceries, medication, rent, and care. **If you or someone you know has been affected by these changes, you can check your OHP status or reapply for SNAP **[**here**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141334187/653213033/-1078352051?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMDk5MDQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNjMwNWYyNzEtMzNjNy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=VbnT3WMMmFmJQp_VK9exclU9qVVc9-f5KV890M13cg8=&emci=b959604e-2cc7-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=6305f271-33c7-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=9506338)**.** I became a physician because I wanted to care for people when they need it most. I will not stand by while Republicans make that care harder to afford. The cruel cuts to Medicaid and SNAP are a slap in the face when our President is building extravagant ballrooms and sending us into unnecessary wars. **We should be making it easier for people to get healthy, put food on the table, and live with dignity. Not harder.** **[If you’re with me, will you chip in today to help us keep fighting for the communities who need us most?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141334188/653213034/-870868562?refcode=x_261013_medicaidsnap_act&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMDk5MDQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNjMwNWYyNzEtMzNjNy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=VbnT3WMMmFmJQp_VK9exclU9qVVc9-f5KV890M13cg8=)**
