---|---|---
Salma Abdel Hadi (left) inside her tent speaking to journalist Rasha Abou Jalal (right) in the Nuseirat refugee camp in central the Gaza Strip on September 25, 2026. Photo by Saida Al-Torkmani.
GAZA CITY--Standing before the rubble of the Palace of Justice in central Gaza, Salma Abdel Hadi was overwhelmed by a profound sense of helplessness. Since her husband's killing last year, the 38-year-old mother of six has been unable to secure inheritance rights for herself and her children to help provide food and clothing in the midst of a genocide.
The Israeli military deliberately destroyed the Palace of Justice in Al-Zahra City early in the war, rigging the court complex with explosives and [demolishing](https://substack.com/redirect/185eecb4-7c70-466b-b357-2365730398c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the entire structure on December 4, 2023. Abdel Hadi's husband was killed in an Israeli airstrike in August 2025, leaving her alone to raise and feed their children in the Nuseirat refugee camp--and with no functioning court system, accessing any of her late husband's money or property has been all but impossible.
"My children need their rights more than ever," Abdel Hadi told Drop Site News, clasping her hands together in anguish. "But today I find myself facing a question to which I have no answer: How can I protect my children's right to inherit from their father if the place that is supposed to provide me with a document proving that right has been reduced to rubble?"
In the three years of Israel's genocide in Gaza, the military has systematically destroyed most of the enclave, including residential neighborhoods, hospitals, schools and universities, bakeries, water systems, electrical grids, along with most of Gaza's governmental, judicial, and bureaucratic infrastructure. The lack of a functioning judicial system in Gaza has particularly affected Palestinian women, who face a series of seemingly insurmountable legal and bureaucratic obstacles to secure legal rights like inheritance, divorce, alimony, property rights, and more.
Abdel Hadi said she is entitled to an inheritance of approximately $5,000 held in her late husband's bank account, yet she cannot access the funds without an inheritance certificate issued by the court. The delays in establishing inheritance rights from her husband for herself and her children also allowed members of his family to take control of some of his property. "My husband's brother seized my husband's car without any legal right, and I was unable to recover it through the judicial process because the courts are not functioning," she said.
She estimates recovering ownership of the car and selling it could fetch as much as $20,000. For a family that has lost its breadwinner and sole source of income, the funds are critical and could make it possible to move out of the tent where they are living and into a rented home, afford more food, and even set aside whatever they can for the children's future.
Abdel Hadi also needs official documentation in order to obtain any assistance or financial rights connected to their father, and prevent their property from being disposed of without legal oversight. Aside from the car, the family owns a 300-meter plot of land located near the Nuseirat camp where Abdel Hadi has pitched a tent. In the absence of any documents, Abdel Hadi is unable as a widow to safeguard her own social and economic rights or those of her children.
"I want to get my children out of the tents and provide them with a home where we can live, food to satisfy their hunger, and savings that will help them continue their education when they reach university age," Abdel Hadi said.
In Gaza, the Sharia court is the authority that handles divorce, alimony, custody, and guardianship cases, and issues documents establishing inheritance, widowhood, death, and marriage. When these procedures are suspended or become inaccessible, legal rights become pending claims that are difficult to prove or enforce. Women in Gaza are bearing the brunt of Israel's attack on the court system, particularly widows, divorced women, and women caring for minors. The war has killed husbands and breadwinners, separated families, and destroyed marriage documents and other files. In this vacuum, women find themselves forced to negotiate with other parties and bargain over their rights.
[A December 2025 report](https://substack.com/redirect/5b4e3740-8aaa-4332-9aba-85863402dac8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the Palestinian Centre for Human Rights found that "the suspension of Sharia courts and the halt in receiving new cases as a result of the Israeli attack have devastating effects on the situation of women in the Gaza Strip, in the absence of any institutional alternatives capable of addressing personal status cases. Women have become unable to pursue cases involving separation, alimony or custody, leaving them in a legally suspended and unstable situation."
The report noted that these circumstances have "exacerbated women's psychological, social and economic suffering, made them more vulnerable to marginalization and exploitation, and even pushed many of them to relinquish their rights involuntarily as a result of the lack of avenues for legal redress and the collapse of the formal protection system." It added, "women have paid the highest price for the disruption of the judiciary, losing their Sharia, economic and social rights and being subjected to continuous legal and psychological injustice in the absence of institutional protection and support."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7ce7b3fe-70b0-42af-becf-aae9779066eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Aida Hamid (center in red) sits on the coast in Gaza City on September 26. Photo by Rasha Abou Jalal.
In August 2023, two months before Israel's genocidal assault began, Aida Hamid's husband left her. He offered to grant her a divorce in exchange for her giving up her financial rights, including her deferred dowry, and other rights she was legally entitled to.
"I refused to give up my Sharia rights in order to obtain the divorce so I decided to file a lawsuit that would guarantee me a divorce while preserving my legal rights," Hamid, 32, told Drop Site. "However, the outbreak of war, the destruction of the courts and the disruption of judicial work left my case unresolved and suspended."
Without any recourse in court, Hamid, who lives in Gaza City, has been left in limbo. Not only has she been denied financial rights, such as a deferred dowry and alimony, which she estimates at some 7,000 Jordanian dinars (about $9,900), she has remained legally married, preventing her from finding a new partner and marrying again.
"More than three years have passed without my case being resolved, leaving me trapped in an unresolved social and legal situation," she said. "I have been abandoned by my husband, and I do not have a court ruling ending the marriage, which has turned my life into complete chaos."
Financial rights are more than just abstract legal entitlements for Hamid, but instead are a vital resource that would help her secure basic needs and cost of living as the genocide enters its fourth year.
"Receiving my deferred dowry and alimony would grant me a degree of financial independence and reduce my dependence on others for my living expenses, especially since I have been living in a state of legal and social limbo for over three years due to the courts being closed," Halid said.
Mohammad Shehadeh, a lawyer who specializes in civil and Sharia cases, told Drop Site that the effective incapacitation of the Sharia judiciary in Gaza has "disrupted the lives of thousands of women and left them facing a legal and social vacuum that threatens their rights and the rights of their children."
Widows need a series of documents to establish their rights, such as proof of the husband's death or filing a missing person claim, followed by obtaining an inheritance certificate and proof of widowhood, and guardianship or legal authority over any children.
"When the court is absent or the document is lost, the rights of women and children are no longer protected by law, but instead become vulnerable to family pressure, seizure or forced relinquishment," Shehadeh said. He added that child custody cases are becoming increasingly complicated, particularly when a husband is killed or goes missing, leading to disputes between the wife and the husband's relatives over the care of the children and the management of their inheritance. Abandoned women also face difficulties obtaining rulings on separation and divorce, alimony, child custody or visitation rights. Existing judgments are also difficult to enforce with no authority capable of compelling payments or handing over documents.
There may also be unforeseen long term consequences of a nonfunctioning judiciary that are not immediately apparent, Shehadeh warned. "A judicial file that is lost today may turn tomorrow into a prolonged dispute over a home, land, inheritance or custody, and proving the right may become more difficult as time passes," he said, adding that some women may be compelled to accept unfair settlements or relinquish their rights in exchange for a quick resolution to a legal issue.
As with much else in Gaza, the damage to the Sharia judicial system in Israel's assault has been devastating. Around half of all court premises have been completely destroyed, according to Dr. Omar Nofal, the head of the Sharia Court of Appeal in Gaza. Three of 30 judges have been killed along with 20 judicial staff members. A large part of the courts' paper archives, including historical records and documents, has been burned or destroyed.
And as with nearly all Palestinians in Gaza, most judicial staff have been displaced, forcing them to work from their places of shelter or temporary locations, turning even simple bureaucratic procedures into an ordeal.
"We established three temporary locations in the Gaza Strip that operate as courts, though their role is limited to receiving and registering lawsuits," Nofal said. "Because of the difficult circumstances resulting from the war, judges have completed only a very small fraction of these cases, while most cases have yet to be heard. Some of them have been registered for more than a year without being considered."
Nofal also stressed that women face particular obstacles in cases involving separation or divorce, spousal and child alimony, custody, guardianship, and inheritance.
"When documents are lost or access to the court becomes impossible, the children's money and the family's rights remain suspended, and the woman may be forced to relinquish her rights," Nofal said. He also highlighted that even if women obtain court rulings establishing their rights, they face major obstacles in securing those rights in practice.
"Even if a woman obtains a court ruling establishing her right--for example, if a divorced woman obtains her right to alimony or custody of her children--there are no executive bodies to enforce the court order because the Israeli army is pursuing the police authorities in Gaza," he said.
Police authorities in Gaza that are responsible for law enforcement have been targeted by Israel in repeated attacks. Between January and August 2026, the UN recorded at least 18 Israeli attacks against police personnel in Gaza, resulting in the killing of at least 77 Palestinians, including 57 police personnel, six children and four women. The attacks have targeted police headquarters, posts, and vehicles, and appear to be escalating, with six of them being carried out since June.
On August 19, an Israeli airstrike targeted a temporary municipal police headquarters in Gaza City, killing eight police officers, including Fatena Al-Sahhar, the head of the Women's Police in Gaza Governorate, as well as a 13-year-old girl.
"Under international humanitarian law, police personnel are civilians protected against attacks. Targeting them is a war crime," the UN said in a statement.
One year into the so-called "ceasefire," Israel continues to violate the agreement on a daily basis, continuing its attacks on Palestinians and preventing any reconstruction, including of Gaza's social, governmental, and judicial institutions.
"With the absence of the judiciary, I have been left without a ruling to end my marriage and without any means of claiming my rights," Abdel Hadi said. "I feel as though my life has completely stopped along with the suspension of the courts' work."

Please consider becoming a paid subscriber or making a . | | ---|---|--- Salma Abdel Hadi (left) inside her tent speaking to journalist Rasha Abou Jalal (right) in the Nuseirat refugee camp in central the Gaza Strip on September 25, 2026. Photo by Saida Al-Torkmani. GAZA CITY--Standing before the rubble of the Palace of Justice in central Gaza, Salma Abdel Hadi was overwhelmed by a profound sense of helplessness. Since her husband's killing last year, the 38-year-old mother of six has been unable to secure inheritance rights for herself and her children to help provide food and clothing in the midst of a genocide. The Israeli military deliberately destroyed the Palace of Justice in Al-Zahra City early in the war, rigging the court complex with explosives and the entire structure on December 4, 2023. Abdel Hadi's husband was killed in an Israeli airstrike in August 2025, leaving her alone to raise and feed their children in the Nuseirat refugee camp--and with no functioning court system, accessing any of her late husband's money or property has been all but impossible. "My children need their rights more than ever," Abdel Hadi told Drop Site News, clasping her hands together in anguish. "But today I find myself facing a question to which I have no answer: How can I protect my children's right to inherit from their father if the place that is supposed to provide me with a document proving that right has been reduced to rubble?" In the three years of Israel's genocide in Gaza, the military has systematically destroyed most of the enclave, including residential neighborhoods, hospitals, schools and universities, bakeries, water systems, electrical grids, along with most of Gaza's governmental, judicial, and bureaucratic infrastructure. The lack of a functioning judicial system in Gaza has particularly affected Palestinian women, who face a series of seemingly insurmountable legal and bureaucratic obstacles to secure legal rights like inheritance, divorce, alimony, property rights, and more. Abdel Hadi said she is entitled to an inheritance of approximately $5,000 held in her late husband's bank account, yet she cannot access the funds without an inheritance certificate issued by the court. The delays in establishing inheritance rights from her husband for herself and her children also allowed members of his family to take control of some of his property. "My husband's brother seized my husband's car without any legal right, and I was unable to recover it through the judicial process because the courts are not functioning," she said. She estimates recovering ownership of the car and selling it could fetch as much as $20,000. For a family that has lost its breadwinner and sole source of income, the funds are critical and could make it possible to move out of the tent where they are living and into a rented home, afford more food, and even set aside whatever they can for the children's future. Abdel Hadi also needs official documentation in order to obtain any assistance or financial rights connected to their father, and prevent their property from being disposed of without legal oversight. Aside from the car, the family owns a 300-meter plot of land located near the Nuseirat camp where Abdel Hadi has pitched a tent. In the absence of any documents, Abdel Hadi is unable as a widow to safeguard her own social and economic rights or those of her children. "I want to get my children out of the tents and provide them with a home where we can live, food to satisfy their hunger, and savings that will help them continue their education when they reach university age," Abdel Hadi said. In Gaza, the Sharia court is the authority that handles divorce, alimony, custody, and guardianship cases, and issues documents establishing inheritance, widowhood, death, and marriage. When these procedures are suspended or become inaccessible, legal rights become pending claims that are difficult to prove or enforce. Women in Gaza are bearing the brunt of Israel's attack on the court system, particularly widows, divorced women, and women caring for minors. The war has killed husbands and breadwinners, separated families, and destroyed marriage documents and other files. In this vacuum, women find themselves forced to negotiate with other parties and bargain over their rights. by the Palestinian Centre for Human Rights found that "the suspension of Sharia courts and the halt in receiving new cases as a result of the Israeli attack have devastating effects on the situation of women in the Gaza Strip, in the absence of any institutional alternatives capable of addressing personal status cases. Women have become unable to pursue cases involving separation, alimony or custody, leaving them in a legally suspended and unstable situation." The report noted that these circumstances have "exacerbated women's psychological, social and economic suffering, made them more vulnerable to marginalization and exploitation, and even pushed many of them to relinquish their rights involuntarily as a result of the lack of avenues for legal redress and the collapse of the formal protection system." It added, "women have paid the highest price for the disruption of the judiciary, losing their Sharia, economic and social rights and being subjected to continuous legal and psychological injustice in the absence of institutional protection and support." | | ---|---|--- Aida Hamid (center in red) sits on the coast in Gaza City on September 26. Photo by Rasha Abou Jalal. In August 2023, two months before Israel's genocidal assault began, Aida Hamid's husband left her. He offered to grant her a divorce in exchange for her giving up her financial rights, including her deferred dowry, and other rights she was legally entitled to. "I refused to give up my Sharia rights in order to obtain the divorce so I decided to file a lawsuit that would guarantee me a divorce while preserving my legal rights," Hamid, 32, told Drop Site. "However, the outbreak of war, the destruction of the courts and the disruption of judicial work left my case unresolved and suspended." Without any recourse in court, Hamid, who lives in Gaza City, has been left in limbo. Not only has she been denied financial rights, such as a deferred dowry and alimony, which she estimates at some 7,000 Jordanian dinars (about $9,900), she has remained legally married, preventing her from finding a new partner and marrying again. "More than three years have passed without my case being resolved, leaving me trapped in an unresolved social and legal situation," she said. "I have been abandoned by my husband, and I do not have a court ruling ending the marriage, which has turned my life into complete chaos." Financial rights are more than just abstract legal entitlements for Hamid, but instead are a vital resource that would help her secure basic needs and cost of living as the genocide enters its fourth year. "Receiving my deferred dowry and alimony would grant me a degree of financial independence and reduce my dependence on others for my living expenses, especially since I have been living in a state of legal and social limbo for over three years due to the courts being closed," Halid said. Mohammad Shehadeh, a lawyer who specializes in civil and Sharia cases, told Drop Site that the effective incapacitation of the Sharia judiciary in Gaza has "disrupted the lives of thousands of women and left them facing a legal and social vacuum that threatens their rights and the rights of their children." Widows need a series of documents to establish their rights, such as proof of the husband's death or filing a missing person claim, followed by obtaining an inheritance certificate and proof of widowhood, and guardianship or legal authority over any children. "When the court is absent or the document is lost, the rights of women and children are no longer protected by law, but instead become vulnerable to family pressure, seizure or forced relinquishment," Shehadeh said. He added that child custody cases are becoming increasingly complicated, particularly when a husband is killed or goes missing, leading to disputes between the wife and the husband's relatives over the care of the children and the management of their inheritance. Abandoned women also face difficulties obtaining rulings on separation and divorce, alimony, child custody or visitation rights. Existing judgments are also difficult to enforce with no authority capable of compelling payments or handing over documents. There may also be unforeseen long term consequences of a nonfunctioning judiciary that are not immediately apparent, Shehadeh warned. "A judicial file that is lost today may turn tomorrow into a prolonged dispute over a home, land, inheritance or custody, and proving the right may become more difficult as time passes," he said, adding that some women may be compelled to accept unfair settlements or relinquish their rights in exchange for a quick resolution to a legal issue. As with much else in Gaza, the damage to the Sharia judicial system in Israel's assault has been devastating. Around half of all court premises have been completely destroyed, according to Dr. Omar Nofal, the head of the Sharia Court of Appeal in Gaza. Three of 30 judges have been killed along with 20 judicial staff members. A large part of the courts' paper archives, including historical records and documents, has been burned or destroyed. And as with nearly all Palestinians in Gaza, most judicial staff have been displaced, forcing them to work from their places of shelter or temporary locations, turning even simple bureaucratic procedures into an ordeal. "We established three temporary locations in the Gaza Strip that operate as courts, though their role is limited to receiving and registering lawsuits," Nofal said. "Because of the difficult circumstances resulting from the war, judges have completed only a very small fraction of these cases, while most cases have yet to be heard. Some of them have been registered for more than a year without being considered." Nofal also stressed that women face particular obstacles in cases involving separation or divorce, spousal and child alimony, custody, guardianship, and inheritance. "When documents are lost or access to the court becomes impossible, the children's money and the family's rights remain suspended, and the woman may be forced to relinquish her rights," Nofal said. He also highlighted that even if women obtain court rulings establishing their rights, they face major obstacles in securing those rights in practice. "Even if a woman obtains a court ruling establishing her right--for example, if a divorced woman obtains her right to alimony or custody of her children--there are no executive bodies to enforce the court order because the Israeli army is pursuing the police authorities in Gaza," he said. Police authorities in Gaza that are responsible for law enforcement have been targeted by Israel in repeated attacks. Between January and August 2026, the UN recorded at least 18 Israeli attacks against police personnel in Gaza, resulting in the killing of at least 77 Palestinians, including 57 police personnel, six children and four women. The attacks have targeted police headquarters, posts, and vehicles, and appear to be escalating, with six of them being carried out since June. On August 19, an Israeli airstrike targeted a temporary municipal police headquarters in Gaza City, killing eight police officers, including Fatena Al-Sahhar, the head of the Women's Police in Gaza Governorate, as well as a 13-year-old girl. "Under international humanitarian law, police personnel are civilians protected against attacks. Targeting them is a war crime," the UN said in a statement. One year into the so-called "ceasefire," Israel continues to violate the agreement on a daily basis, continuing its attacks on Palestinians and preventing any reconstruction, including of Gaza's social, governmental, and judicial institutions. "With the absence of the judiciary, I have been left without a ruling to end my marriage and without any means of claiming my rights," Abdel Hadi said. "I feel as though my life has completely stopped along with the suspension of the courts' work." | A guest post by| I am Rasha Abu Jalal, a journalist from Gaza Strip. With Election Day just around the corner, my team and I have some difficult decisions coming up, and we could really use a hand, particularly right now.
Tomorrow marks our final FEC fundraising deadline of this campaign. And after it passes, we're going to sit down and make plans for the final weeks of this campaign.
**I want to give the green light to the biggest, boldest plans my team can think up. Plans that will reach every corner of the state and get everyone involved and talking to their neighbors.**
_Plans that will win Georgia._
But, running a campaign like that is not easy. Especially when we're facing tens of millions of dollars in outside Republican spending. In order to fully respond to my opponents' attacks and organize relentlessly across the state, we are going to need your help.
This team has never let me down before. In 2021, I won election to the U.S. Senate by just over 1%. It was close! But thanks to you, we had the resources to win. So, ahead of some of the most important budget decisions for our campaign, I'm asking for your help once again:
**[Please, chip in $10 or whatever you can afford to my reelection campaign today. We 'll put every donation right to work building the biggest, boldest campaign we possibly can -- there's too much on the line for anything less than maximum effort.](https://substack.com/redirect/3df1e841-b983-4234-8a1c-93d26237b480?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Thank you so much for your support. Onward!
Jon

name: Cooper, Roy
subject: You’ve distinguished yourself from the crowd
body:
I want to express my profound gratitude for having you by my side.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1612&source=&t=1&akid=4534%2E124072%2E7r9OrS) | | | | | | Peter, I’m not reaching out to everyone today – just a select few, including you.
---
| | My team was going through our supporter records, and yours stood out in the crowd. You’re one of my most attentive grassroots supporters. You’ve been getting these emails for a while now, and we see you're keeping up with the latest on this election. I want you to know that I know how engaged you’ve been with our campaign and how much I appreciate it. [**_Today, I’m asking you to take the next step._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1612&amount=5&t=9&akid=4534%2E124072%2E7r9OrS) **Here’s why:**
---
| | Grassroots fundraising has stalled recently, and it couldn’t come at a worse time. Republican super PACs have poured tens of millions into North Carolina to defeat me, and President Trump and JD Vance have both come to smear my name at rallies alongside my MAGA opponent Michael Whatley.
---
| | We need to turn this around fast – and the first step is reaching our $3 million goal before our last FEC filing deadline tomorrow at midnight. [**_Will you chip in $5 right now to help us get there in time? The stakes could not be higher._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1612&amount=5&t=10&akid=4534%2E124072%2E7r9OrS)

| | **Unlike my MAGA opponent Michael Whatley, I’m not a Washington DC insider who can rely on his billionaire connections to buy this Senate seat. I’m depending on people like you giving what you can, when you can, at crucial moments like this.**
---
| | _With just over 24 hours left to close the gap, Peter, I need you._

#### **[BDN Does Journalism, Sort Of](https://substack.com/redirect/142c6e41-78d4-4c33-a921-bc39390da407?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The news blog subsidized by Pulse Marketing company caused headaches for State Auditor Matt Dunlap's struggling congressional campaign this morning with the publication of an audio recording in which Dunlap attacked outgoing Democratic U.S. Rep. Jared Golden. Dunlap had already made enemies within Democrat Party ranks by declaring his candidacy when Golden was still a favored-to-win incumbent, but the seemingly off-the-cuff shot at Golden comes across as a misstep for a man who has been in public office for a very long time.
The Golden camp responded via a statement suggesting Dunlap was trying to shift blame for an anticipated election loss. "Usually by this stage of a campaign, a candidate knows who they are running against. Matt Dunlap should know by now he's running against Paul LePage, not me," Golden said. "This comes across as someone scared of losing, and seeding the ground to shift the blame if he does."
#### **[Allegations Against Socialist Lawmaker Deepen as Democrats, Media Ignore Woman in Need](https://substack.com/redirect/0ebeaee7-7272-42a4-a2fd-d2cb2ec02e32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **
A former tenant named Karrah tells Jon Fetherston that Scott Harriman, a state representative and Lewiston city councilor who was her landlord, evicted her after she refused to have sex with him. She also says he drove her to buy drugs more than 50 times.
Harriman denies all of it and has falsely accused The Maine Wire of inventing the story -- which was first disclosed to Lewiston city officials by a third party, according to records obtained by Fetherston. The allegations -- which Karrah repeated on camera -- have not been addressed by Democratic leaders, nor have they been covered by other media outlets.

#### **[With Three Weeks Until Election, Bobby Charles Makes Case for Change, Pledges Day-One Action at Wells Town Hall](https://substack.com/redirect/0db22d02-2c77-48cd-a5a2-ed13b888a0bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
At his Oct. 12 town hall in Wells, the Republican nominee for governor promised a $100,000 homestead property-tax exemption, a day-one executive order keeping biological males out of girls' sports and locker rooms. Charles has two more gubernatorial debates to trigger a break-moment for his underdog candidacy.
#### **[Jonathan Bush Takes'Maine for Keeps' Campaign to Bangor, Targets City Hall Accountability Amid Growing Public Safety Concerns](https://substack.com/redirect/9a5de961-87a4-45d8-b20f-1b46b3017b37?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
At a West Market Square presser on Monday, Jonathan Bush, with GOP Chair Jim Deyermond and Phil Henry alongside, laid out his $100,000 push into the Bangor, Lewiston, and Waterville municipal races, $50,000 of it his own contribution. His pitch: city halls do more to your quality of life than Augusta does, and nobody's watching them.
#### **[White House Asks U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle to Resign](https://substack.com/redirect/ea9193d8-631b-4b2c-93f5-d8b42be97300?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
New Press Secretary Katie Zacharia announced at her first briefing, one day after Trump said "we're not happy." It follows Wall Street Journal reporting that Guilfoyle asked a donor to wire $100,000 to her AmEx so it "won't show up anywhere" on her disclosures. The donor never paid and later called the request "pay to play." Guilfoyle, a former Fox News personality, was previously engaged to Donald Trump, Jr.
#### **[Appeals Court Sides With Aquarium in Lobstermen's Defamation Lawsuit](https://substack.com/redirect/63422926-3e7c-4090-879a-69d92a08d16d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The First Circuit threw out the lobstermen's suit over Monterey Bay Aquarium's 2022 "red list" rating of Maine lobster. The court held that Maine's group-defamation rule protects a statement about an entire industry unless it singles out particular members. So the California aquarium can keep maligning the Maine lobster. Yet another way California is making life worse for Mainers...
#### **[Former Independent York Sheriff's Candidate Appointed as Wells' New Police Chief](https://substack.com/redirect/48b91162-7a66-4030-a932-d3d64f22a353?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Brian Pellerin, chief deputy for the Cumberland County Sheriff, quit the York County sheriff's race on Sept. 23, saying he was taking a "different professional path." Now we know where it leads: he takes over the Wells Police Department on Nov. 10. Pellerin's departure from the York County Sheriff race almost certainly guarantees re-election for Democrat incumbent Sheriff William King, considering he recruited the GOP candidate himself to run as a spoiler in what would have been a competitive three-way race.
#### **[Aquatic Police Operation in Passadumkeag Leads to Arrest of Burglar](https://substack.com/redirect/0497e494-d725-495e-9205-7acad39068fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Penobscot deputies say a 25-year-old Chester man broke into his ex-girlfriend's home despite bail conditions, then hid on an island in the river. It took a drone, a K-9 unit, and a Warden Service boat. He surrendered once the drone showed up.

## Politics to Watch this Week...
**Collins vs. Jackson, Senate debate No. 3** : tonight, **7:00 p.m.** , on WABI (also streaming, and on C-SPAN).
**Governor 's debate (Pingree, Charles, Bennett)**: also tonight, **7:00 p.m.** , on CBS 13 and FOX 23, so pick a channel. They meet again Wed at 8 p.m. on WMTW.
**Thursday, Oct. 15** : the last Collins vs. Jackson debate at 7 p.m., plus the last televised 2nd District debate, LePage vs. Dunlap, at 7 p.m. on WABI/WAGM.
**General Election Day** : **Tue Nov 3**. Candidate and PAC 11-day pre-general reports are due Oct. 23. That deadline will be one of the final, best glimpses at how the money is shaking out in state races.
## Around the Web
**[State says infection control issues at CMMC in Lewiston could jeopardize Medicare agreement](https://substack.com/redirect/4090b919-e08e-4412-971e-9f103ba2199d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** (Sun Journal) In an Oct. 8 notice, CMS told Central Maine Medical Center that "substantial noncompliance remains" on infection control, the physical environment, and governing-body oversight. If those aren't fixed by Jan. 7, 2027, CMS can end the hospital's Medicare agreement. This grew out of the sterile-processing contamination regulators found in August. The hospital's own infection plan had already flagged the problem as "high risk."
**[An underwater AI data center proposal has residents up in arms in Downeast Maine](https://substack.com/redirect/1548b61d-464c-4f0a-9a76-6f115a86ae93?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** (Boston Globe) A Needham developer has applied to FERC for a preliminary permit for a 15-megawatt data center under the water off Eastport, run on the tides. Eastport's city manager calls it "an idea on a bar napkin." The city has a 180-day moratorium on data centers anyway, and a residents' group has formed to fight it.

body:
Hearing from a friend, family member, or neighbor is the best way to get the word out.

| | |
---
---
---
---
Peter, Thank you for everything you’ve done to help elect Rick as Maine’s next Governor. We have **21 days left,** and early voting is already underway. The most valuable way to help is also the simplest: **would you email or text five people and tell them, in your own words, why you’re supporting Rick?** Hearing from a friend, family member, or neighbor is the best way to get the word out. A note from someone they know means more than any ad we could ever run. Please copy and paste the note below, and please add a sentence about why you’re supporting Rick: Dear Friends, Hi, I wanted to personally ask you to vote for Rick Bennett for governor. I’m supporting Rick because [_add one sentence in your own words. It could be as simple as: “I’m supporting Rick because I’m tired of politicians fighting instead of fixing things.”_] Rick is an independent, running because too many Maine families are doing everything right and still falling behind. He’s focused on the basics: a fair shot, a government that tells the truth, and a future our kids can afford. I encourage you to learn more at [BennettForGovernor.com](BennettForGovernor.com), and to join me in voting for Rick. If you can, **send it to five people before 7 p.m. today.** Then reply “DONE” to this email to let me know. You’ll help us track how many Mainers Rick’s supporters are reaching. Thanks for your help,
Kaitlin
---

| | | Today is the last day to register to vote in Oregon's November election. If you're not registered by 11:59 p.m. tonight, you won't get a ballot this year. That means no say in who runs our state, who represents us in Congress, or what happens on the measures that shape our communities. **Registering takes about two minutes at _[oregonvotes.gov](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141335324/653217079/-357076319?refcode=261013-register&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiYmI3YWExYS0zN2M3LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_rLdxS3Fo3VBq37_ks5e-Rk0hBsg-OzyH2QTmagfzZI=&emci=68f16d14-37c7-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=bbb7aa1a-37c7-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=30662126)_. Ballots start going out tomorrow.** As Secretary of State, my job is to make sure every eligible Oregonian can vote and that every vote is counted. Most years, that's hard enough. This year, I'm doing it while the Trump administration tries to make voting by mail harder in every way it can. **Oregon built the best vote-by-mail system in the country, and I'm not going to let anyone take it apart. body:
We can’t take anything for granted.
#
Hi there,
Election Day is 3 weeks away, and while Democrats are overall in a strong position to flip the Senate, there’s some nuance in what we’re seeing.
In several of our Must-Flip races—particularly North Carolina, Ohio, and Texas—Democrats are looking stronger and stronger. But one of our Must-Hold races, Michigan, is looking extremely close.
**Here’s a look at some of the latest polling numbers in all of our Senate targets this cycle:**
[](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2652?t=1&akid=3123%2E1562180%2Ebaw3OL)
[](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2652?t=2&akid=3123%2E1562180%2Ebaw3OL)
To win Senate control, Democrats need to flip four Republican-held seats while holding on to their current seats in three battleground states. And Republicans aren’t making it easy. They’re pouring money into TV ads in many of these races, including more than $326 million spent in Texas alone. We need to make sure Democrats have the resources to respond to attacks and stay competitive.
**So with less than 4 weeks to go, we’re asking you to[donate any amount to our Win The Senate Fund today.](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2652?t=3&akid=3123%2E1562180%2Ebaw3OL)**
**[Donate Now](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2652?t=4&akid=3123%2E1562180%2Ebaw3OL)**
Your donation will be split between each of the candidates listed above, with a portion also going to Swing Left to support our efforts to have Ground Truth deep canvassing conversations in competitive states across the country.
Thank you, as always, for everything you do. Let’s get out there and win some elections!

subject: It’s clear… the Court is for sale
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Demand Justice PAC
body:
[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20261013-61900&t=1001&akid=61900%2E1407376%2E6ZnWBj ]Demand Justice PAC[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20261013-61900&t=1002&akid=61900%2E1407376%2E6ZnWBj ]Demand Justice PAC

Here's
something you don't hear often: Democrats and Republicans agree.

The University of Maryland’s Program for Public Consultation surveyed
voters across 11 Senate battlegrounds and 28 swing House districts about
their thoughts on government, elections, and court reform.^1

The result? In nearly every battleground, both parties came down on the
same side. They want:

* A binding ethics code for the Supreme Court, like the one every
lower-court judge already follows.
* A ban on stock trading for Supreme Court justices, members of
Congress, and the president and vice president.
* An end to Citizens United.

It's not hard to see why. Justices have let billionaires bankroll their
vacations, real estate, and school tuition for their families for decades
while keeping it off disclosures. And the "ethics code" the Supreme Court
wrote for itself has no enforcement at all.

Voters in red and blue districts look at this Court and see the same
thing: a Court for sale.

The only ones standing in the way are the justices cashing in, the
billionaires propping them up, and Donald Trump, who's counting on this
Court to protect him.

Demand Justice PAC is leading the fight to win real reform, hold senators
accountable for the justices they confirm, and ensure the Court protects
the people, not the powerful. But we can't do it without grassroots
support.

name: Ilhan Omar
subject: DHS just raided my house.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261013-1.NA9Fft&refcode=em20261013-6829&t=1001&akid=6829%2E420207%2EUtWQZH ][IMG]

Peter, Donald
Trump’s fascism and abuse of power has now come to my literal front door.

DHS agents just raided and searched my home in the DC area as the latest
step in their ludicrous, partisan investigation into my immigration
status.

I have been in Trump’s crosshairs for years, but now he is escalating in a
desperate attempt to drag me and the entire progressive movement down
ahead of the midterms.

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261013-1.NA9Fft&refcode=em20261013-6829&t=1002&akid=6829%2E420207%2EUtWQZH ]This is a critical moment for our democracy, and we must be decisive.
Please, stand by me and our movement today by rushing a contribution,
split between me and Pramila Jayapal, to help me fight back in the face of
Trump’s abuse of power >>

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261013-1.NA9Fft&refcode=em20261013-6829&t=1003&akid=6829%2E420207%2EUtWQZH ]Rush a Donation

It’s no accident that this raid comes three weeks before an election where
I’m on the ballot.

This is part of the fascist playbook to rile up Trump’s die-hard
supporters and give them a big distraction in advance of the midterms.
With this obviously political investigation, Trump is telling his voters:
‘Ignore the price of gas, ignore the war in Iran, ignore that you’re
losing your healthcare — we want you to get angry about this instead.”

Throughout his presidency, Trump has weaponized the DOJ to target his
political opponents, manufacturing charges that have been roundly
dismissed by court after court. And I’m not even the first member of
Congress to be targeted. The point is to waste everyone’s time and
resources, and generate negative headlines for his opponents.

I will repeat what I have long said: This is a ludicrous investigation,
and Trump’s escalation is only further proof that he is willing to use the
power of the federal government to try to intimidate and silence anyone
who stands up to him. It’s up to us to make sure it doesn’t work.

In just a few weeks we can strike a major blow at Trump’s fascist agenda
and end this era of authoritarianism by taking Congress back from MAGA.
Today, as I stand in the breach of Trump’s endless attacks and immense
power to do harm, I’m asking for your support:

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261013-1.NA9Fft&refcode=em20261013-6829&t=1004&akid=6829%2E420207%2EUtWQZH ]Please, stand with me today by splitting a generous donation between me
and Pramila Jayapal. Your donation will help me not only fight back
against this incredible abuse of power, but continue to organize our
movement for democracy, peace, and affordability ahead of what is shaping
up to be one of the most important elections of our lives.

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261013-1.NA9Fft&amount=3&refcode=em20261013-6829&t=1023&akid=6829%2E420207%2EUtWQZH ]Contribute $3

In solidarity,

Ilhan Omar

Contribute to Pramila Jayapal: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-footer?refcode=em20261013-6829-footer&t=1024&refcode2=6829_420207_UtWQZH&akid=6829%2E420207%2EUtWQZH

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141335470/653217514/-1038038363?refcode=ITT_ATA_EM_FR_Acton_261013_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOGI5Yzk1ZTAtMzdjNy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=TgeOOrpyorup6NrFh6H1tzHJQm5ddZ0K7loFEjZIrlw=&emci=271456ea-74c6-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=8b9c95e0-37c7-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=17458827)
_Hey team, Andy Beshear here. My friend Amy Acton is running for governor of Ohio. We have a real shot at winning this race and flipping the Ohio governorship blue for the first time in almost two decades. I hope you’ll take a minute to read Amy’s message and consider getting involved:_ [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141335471/653217515/1200337883?refcode=ITT_ATA_EM_FR_Acton_261013_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOGI5Yzk1ZTAtMzdjNy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=TgeOOrpyorup6NrFh6H1tzHJQm5ddZ0K7loFEjZIrlw=) I think it was somewhere off Route 7.

I was 12 years old, homeless, and living in a tent. It wasn't easy, but it made me tough.

Peter, by the time I was in middle school, I had been a frequent flier with children’s services. I had lived in over a dozen homes and experienced abuse, hunger, and homelessness.

But I was determined to find a way out. I credit public schools with saving my life. And I worked three jobs in college and medical school to fulfill my dream of becoming a doctor.

**I’m not sharing this story to earn sympathy points. I’m sharing it because these experiences shaped who I am and how I fight.**

They're why I'll never look the other way while Ohio families struggle to afford groceries, healthcare, childcare, or a place to call home. I know what it's like to need someone to fight for you.

That’s why I’m running for governor.

Look, there’s no doubt this will be a tough fight. I’m up against an out-of-touch billionaire who has no idea what it’s like to struggle. He’s spending tens of millions to buy this state for his own selfish gain.

**But I’m ready for a tough fight. And if I learned anything from my childhood, it's that no one gets through anything alone. That’s where you come in, Peter.**

[_**Together, I know we can build a future for Ohio that works for everyone. So if you’re ready to fight for that future and defeat an out-of-touch billionaire, then I’m asking you to split a contribution between me and Andy Beshear’s In This Together PAC today. name: Troy Downing
subject: A look back in time
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Troy Downing for Congress
body:
I don't usually do this

| Peter,**
**I don't usually do this, but I want to show you something personal today.
I dug up a few old photos – one with my siblings and my single mother, one from my time serving in Afghanistan, and one with my family, long before I set foot in politics.
---
[](https://trk.emails.troydowning._8-u_fcXfYyq5tbg)
---
You see, people in Washington think they know my story because they've seen a 30-second ad or interview.
They don't, Peter.
They don't know what it felt like to leave a stable career behind after 9/11, or what it's like to sit in a helicopter over hostile territory, hoping you make it back with the soldier you came for.
I'm sharing these photos because I think you deserve to actually know who’s reaching out with these emails – not just a name on a donation page.
And with the threat of losing our House Majority looming over our heads, I’m counting on every Patriot’s support before November.
[If this story means something to you, I'd be grateful if you could chip in $5, $10, or $15 towards my campaign today.](https://trk.emails.troydowning.-WF45ndz-8mcu3mJDQ5xIA)

**Our pre-election FEC report closes tomorrow night, Wednesday, October 14.** Before it does, I want to show you something about how Suhas Subramanyam votes, and ask for your help.

I want it to show that VA-10 is ready for change, and every dollar you give before the books close counts toward it. ---

As I've been traveling the district, talking to voters, holding events, sending out volunteers, putting up billboards, and so much more, I've had the feeling that _something doesn 't quite add up._
**Where 's Tim?**
I'm not talking about him refusing to hold town halls, debate, or show up at forums or joint interviews. Those failures of basic representation I expected, unfortunately.
But what I didn't expect was for his campaign to be so . . . invisible. We know that Rep. Burchett has raised and spent more money on this campaign than he ever has before. But, on what exactly?
I've seen a few yard signs crop up in the last two weeks. And sure, he's sent some emails trying to portray me as a radical to raise money for his campaign. But Tim has the budget for multiple glossy mailers, both for him and against me. TV ads. Text messages. Paid canvassers. Radio and podcast spots. Billboards.
I've had dozens of people ask me over the past few weeks:
_**Is Tim even campaigning?**_
Maybe it's coming. But just one day before early voting and exactly three weeks before Election Day, I would have expected _something_ of substance by now.
One explanation is that he doesn't think he'll lose, so he's decided he doesn't have to try to earn people's votes or get out his message. That might be part of it.
**But I 've actually started wondering if Tim just doesn't want this anymore. That it's no longer fun for him. That more people are seeing through the alien talk and the Carhartt jacket and the dadgums - and asking why he hasn't done more to improve the lives of the people of East Tennessee.**
He's tied his wagon to an unpopular President he can't break from. He's lost the respect of many people in his community who used to think he was a good man. And he's hoping that if he hangs around Marsha, he'll be handed her Senate seat.
That's why I sent out a press release earlier this month [asking Rep. Burchett to just hold a public town hall](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/42da8683-6734-473e-8085-936f4c499d7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for his constituents, even if he didn't want to debate me.
I've known how steep this climb was since launching this campaign over a year ago. **I did it, knowing the odds, because I believe that things can be better for East Tennessee.**

I know I have to earn every single vote. That I will have to work harder than feels humanly possible. That I will have to show up _everywhere_.
**So, why can 't Representative Burchett be bothered to show up **_**anywhere**_**?**
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/dd90dd2f-8512-4895-9c36-01acfeb6f9ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

**Early Voting: October 14 - October 29**
Early voting starts tomorrow. It helps me more than you can know to show up early, because then I can use all of our resources to get other voters to the polls!
And if you want to help us show up _everywhere_ , we have [volunteer opportunities](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/89392e6c-7bb4-4652-a288-13257774f3a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) just about every single day from here through November 3rd!

# [](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/3095?t=1&akid=5738%2E35263%2EEg9Q9D)
Peter,
As Election Day approaches - here’s one thing I know: Wisconsin knows how to run safe, secure, and fair elections. Donald Trump wants you to believe otherwise.
Now he’s sending the FBI to our state to “investigate” the 2020 election and he continues to double down on his Big Lie. This isn’t about making our elections safer — he’s undermining our elections to avoid accountability.
I’m not going to let that happen. **I’ve introduced a new bill to protect voters from intimidation or interference at polling locations – the Safe Access to the Polls Act.** This legislation would:
* Bar federal funds from being used to send ICE or the National Guard to polls,
* Prohibit set up a checkpoint near polling places,
* Stop anyone from interfering in any way with voters accessing their polling location.

No voter in Wisconsin should ever be intimidated on their way to cast a ballot.
But I can't do this alone. **With 21 days left until Election Day,** we need strong Wisconsin Democrats up and down the ballot who will fight alongside me in the Senate to safeguard our democracy.
That takes resources, and we're running out of time to raise them. **[Please, if you are able, will you make your first donation to put an end to Trump’s authoritative power grab and keep our elections free and fair?](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20261013-safeaccess.qc8iAs&amount=10&refcode=em20261013-5738&t=2&akid=5738%2E35263%2EEg9Q9D)**

| | Friend, Two weeks ago, the White House celebrated a $15 billion steel plant, the largest in American history. The iron ore that the plant would be processing would come from Minnesota’s Iron Range, but the plant, the paychecks, and the future that comes with them are going to Iowa.With that steel mill Iowa gets 6,000 construction jobs and 1,750 permanent jobs all backed by $10 billion in federal financing. And it’s not the first time this has happened this year. In April, [U.S. Steel announced a $1.9 billion facility](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141337794/653225567/-1448859412?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ3MDYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjJhYzZhZDgtM2JjNy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ZAhnymSmmvCVHPXir8BAY3oSnSOPs8HCCTIYgbKOlyc=&emci=f4f359bf-39c7-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=22ac6ad8-3bc7-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=1071883) that would be constructed in Arkansas fed by Minnesota’s iron ore. That’s another 2,000 construction jobs and more than 200 permanent jobs that Minnesota won’t see.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141337795/653225568/618342866?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ3MDYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjJhYzZhZDgtM2JjNy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ZAhnymSmmvCVHPXir8BAY3oSnSOPs8HCCTIYgbKOlyc=&emci=f4f359bf-39c7-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=22ac6ad8-3bc7-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=1071883)
---
So where was Rep. Pete Stauber?When the Iowa plant was announced Pete called it a “missed opportunity” for northern Minnesota, and then blamed everyone in St. Paul. In the very same statement, he thanked the President for his commitment to the steel industry. **He can’t have it both ways. ** When Washington put billions of federal dollars behind this deal, **our representative should have been in the room fighting to bring that mill to the Iron Range.** Northern Minnesota has supplied this country with iron for generations. Our ore built ships, bridges, and the cities that make this country strong. We should not be satisfied with being the place where raw materials come from. **As your Congresswoman, I’ll fight to make sure that when federal dollars back projects built on Minnesota resources, they come with good union jobs here at home. **If you believe that Minnesota deserves more than holes in the ground, vote Trina Swanson on Nov. 3rd.**Team Trina**

clean_body: Where was Pete when steel investments went to other states?| | | | | Friend, Two weeks ago, the White House celebrated a $15 billion steel plant, the largest in American history. The iron ore that the plant would be processing would come from Minnesota’s Iron Range, but the plant, the paychecks, and the future that comes with them are going to Iowa.With that steel mill Iowa gets 6,000 construction jobs and 1,750 permanent jobs all backed by $10 billion in federal financing. And it’s not the first time this has happened this year. In April, that would be constructed in Arkansas fed by Minnesota’s iron ore. That’s another 2,000 construction jobs and more than 200 permanent jobs that Minnesota won’t see. So where was Rep. Pete Stauber?When the Iowa plant was announced Pete called it a “missed opportunity” for northern Minnesota, and then blamed everyone in St. Paul. In the very same statement, he thanked the President for his commitment to the steel industry. He can’t have it both ways. When Washington put billions of federal dollars behind this deal, our representative should have been in the room fighting to bring that mill to the Iron Range. Northern Minnesota has supplied this country with iron for generations. Our ore built ships, bridges, and the cities that make this country strong. We should not be satisfied with being the place where raw materials come from. As your Congresswoman, I’ll fight to make sure that when federal dollars back projects built on Minnesota resources, they come with good union jobs here at home. If you believe that Minnesota deserves more than holes in the ground, vote Trina Swanson on Nov. 3rd.Team Trina = | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|--- Paid for by Trina for Congress Trina for Congress PO Box 1063 Duluth, MN 55810 United States If you believe you received this message in error or wish to no longer receive email from us, please .

Friends,
On Thursday, Lily Tang Williams walks into Keene for the NHPR candidate forum, on stage with Maggie Goodlander.
Keene is one of the most Democratic towns in New Hampshire. It’s their home turf, and they expect the crowd outside, the signs on the street, and the energy in the room to be all theirs.
Let’s show them otherwise.
When Lily pulls up to that forum, she should see a line of red Lily signs along the street and a crowd of Granite State Republicans who drove in to stand with her. That picture goes out with the coverage. It tells voters across the district, and the press in the room, that this race is competitive and that Lily’s supporters show up wherever she goes, even in Keene.
**Sign Wave for Lily Tang Williams**
Thursday, October 15
4:15pm–5:00 PM
Brewbakers Café, [48 Emerald St, Keene](https://us.list-manage.com/1CX4OmNVq6B?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=OQh6XiqBlimRjapc8FoUH6TyewqZxLDuBXYx-pHHnjnuZYZL1D0JX2yACA==)Bring a sign if you have one. We’ll have plenty of extras.
The forum is free and open to the public. Doors open at 5:00 PM, and the forum starts at 6:00 PM sharp.
**Can’t make it to Keene?** Tune in Friday, October 16, at 9 AM or 7 PM on NHPR, and share it with everyone you know.
Questions? Contact Alvin Wang, Lily’s campaign manager, at [(267) 201-6498](tel:\(267\)%20201-6498) or [cm@lily4congress.com](mailto:cm@lily4congress.com).

Where was Pete when steel investments went to other states?| | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141338504/653227965/618342866?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ3MDYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGUzZjMzM2QtM2RjNy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=mtiKKWjJQa1GUV5rK0a3IOvsDtyQ8azizrmnL6B5rK8=&emci=305b52ff-39c7-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=0e3f333d-3dc7-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=1071883)
---
| | Friend, Two weeks ago, the White House celebrated a $15 billion steel plant, the largest in American history. The iron ore that the plant would be processing would come from Minnesota’s Iron Range, but the plant, the paychecks, and the future that comes with them are going to Iowa.With that steel mill Iowa gets 6,000 construction jobs and 1,750 permanent jobs all backed by $10 billion in federal financing. And it’s not the first time this has happened this year. In April, [U.S. Steel announced a $1.9 billion facility](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141338505/653227967/-1448859412?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ3MDYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGUzZjMzM2QtM2RjNy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=mtiKKWjJQa1GUV5rK0a3IOvsDtyQ8azizrmnL6B5rK8=&emci=305b52ff-39c7-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=0e3f333d-3dc7-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=1071883) that would be constructed in Arkansas fed by Minnesota’s iron ore. That’s another 2,000 construction jobs and more than 200 permanent jobs that Minnesota won’t see.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141338507/653227968/618342866?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ3MDYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGUzZjMzM2QtM2RjNy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=mtiKKWjJQa1GUV5rK0a3IOvsDtyQ8azizrmnL6B5rK8=&emci=305b52ff-39c7-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=0e3f333d-3dc7-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=1071883)
---
So where was Rep. Pete Stauber?When the Iowa plant was announced Pete called it a “missed opportunity” for northern Minnesota, and then blamed everyone in St. Paul. In the very same statement, he thanked the President for his commitment to the steel industry. **He can’t have it both ways. ** When Washington put billions of federal dollars behind this deal, **our representative should have been in the room fighting to bring that mill to the Iron Range.** Northern Minnesota has supplied this country with iron for generations. Our ore built ships, bridges, and the cities that make this country strong. We should not be satisfied with being the place where raw materials come from. **As your Congresswoman, I’ll fight to make sure that when federal dollars back projects built on Minnesota resources, they come with good union jobs here at home. **If you believe that Minnesota deserves more than holes in the ground, vote Trina Swanson on Nov. 3rd.**Team Trina**

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: 6 to 1, and still a dead heat
body:
Abbott outspent us 6 to 1. It’s mid-October and this race is still a dead heat.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
**A new poll released today shows me ahead of Greg Abbott, 47% to 45%.**
That makes five polls _in the last month_ with us in the lead. And it’s October 13th.
Let me explain why that matters.
At the end of July, we got our first poll showing this race within a single point. The experts said to enjoy it while it lasted. Once Greg Abbott opened up his war chest, he’d pull away. That’s how it’s always gone in Texas.
Well, he opened it. Abbott has raised more than $141 million and already spent over $120 million of it. From July through September, he outspent us 6 to 1 and blanketed this state with attack ads.
August came, and he didn’t pull away...
September came, and he didn’t pull away...
**Now it’s the middle of October, and this race is still a dead heat, with new polls _still_ being released that show us ahead.**
That’s remarkable, Peter. All that money, and he couldn’t pull away.
That’s because we have something stronger than his millions: people. Nearly 250,000 individual donors have chipped in to this campaign because they’re ready for change. That’s not something Abbott can buy.
His money also can’t buy a single new reason to like him. In today’s poll, 52% of likely voters view him unfavorably, while voters see me favorably by 12 points, even after months of his attacks.
My grandmother had a phrase I come back to in moments like this: _No te dejes._ Don’t back down.
We’re not backing down now. Early voting starts October 19th, less than a week from today.**If we hold this line through Election Day, we can do what everyone said was impossible and win this race.**
If you’ve been waiting for the right moment to make your first contribution, this is it. Early voting starts on the 19th, and Abbott still has $17 million to spend. [**Will you chip in $15 to help us hold this line all the way to Election Day?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1374?c0=em_ms_gh_20261013_4_pollbump.dy8cPf&refcode=em20261013-2418&t=2&akid=2418%2E299639%2ENBZCT0)

Thank you,
Gina

subject: Our tax dollars paid for Trump’s campaign ads

body:
While Trump’s political allies will cover future ads, taxpayers are on the hook for $19 million already spent. Demand repayment. | |
---
Peter, Trump’s administration spent $19 million of our tax dollars on television ads promoting him ahead of the midterm elections. **We’re demanding that every dollar be paid back.** We pay taxes from the wages we work for, while covering rent, groceries, childcare, and healthcare. We have every reason to demand a say in how our tax dollars get spent. Trump’s administration used millions of those dollars to put his face and political message on television. **One of the ads reused material from Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign, this time with a disclaimer saying it was paid for by the U.S. government.** The administration made working people cover the cost of promoting Trump and his agenda. **After public criticism, Trump announced that he would pay for ads through his super PAC. Then the White House clarified that this did not include reimbursement for past spending. **A federal judge has ordered the administration to stop any remaining taxpayer-funded ads, which ended Sunday at midnight. But stopping the ads leaves $19 million of our money unreturned. We need to keep demanding repayment.**
Our communities organize for fully funded schools, accessible healthcare, and homes our families can afford. We know how hard we have to push to get politicians to invest in those needs. Meanwhile, Trump just helped himself to millions of public dollars to promote his own image and agenda.

Friend, I've spent a lot of time on doorsteps across TX-21 lately, and the conversations are remarkably consistent. People are worried about affording everyday life. Groceries, gas, rent, healthcare — all of it costs more, and paychecks aren't keeping up. Folks aren't asking for much. They want to know how they're going to make it to the end of the month. And underneath that, I'm hearing something else: fear. Fear of what this administration will do next. People feel like decisions are being made far away, for someone else's benefit, and they're the ones left to absorb the cost. That's exactly why I'm running. I grew up watching my mom work multiple jobs just to get by. I know what it feels like to wonder how the bills will get paid, and I know people deserve a representative who actually fights for them, not for donors or special interests. [**Our mid-month deadline is coming up, and every dollar we raise before it helps us keep knocking doors, keep listening, and keep fighting for these families. With Election Day right around the corner, we wanted to fill you in on some major updates: Boosting Black Voter Turnout In Texas We're so proud to announce that we launched an ad in Texas to boost Black voter turnout for James Talarico for Senate. | | ---|---|--- We know just how important this race is for Americans, because Texas is the path to taking back a Democratic Senate Majority. With new polls showing Talarico leading Ken Paxton, this is a golden opportunity to flip Texas blue. But that means Donald Trump is doing everything he can to support his MAGA lackey Paxton to further push his extremist agenda. That's why we're laser-focused on boosting Black voter turnout, because we know that encouraging Black voters to the polls is how we claim victory in Texas! But we need your grassroots support if we're going to keep our operations going and keep our ads running. Free Rides to the Polls on Election Day Look, we know that control of Congress could be decided by just a few votes in battleground races across the country. If Democrats stay home, Republicans will retain their grip on power, which would mean two more years of MAGA attacks on our rights and democracy. We refuse to sit idly by and let this happen! That 's why we're offering FREE rides to the polls on Election Day across the country. Because the stakes are too high to let anyone miss their chance to vote because of a missed bus, a long walk, or no car at all. But to make this happen, we need to raise $100,000 for our Rides to the Polls Fund. If we're going to boost Black voter turnout nationwide, it's going to take each and every one of us stepping up right now. If we're going to win and take back control, we must do it together. name: Bethany Mann for Congress
subject: 110,000 voters reached. Help us finish the job.
body:
We've reached more than one in five voters we're working to reach - help us get to the rest before election day!

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/Gqb1Er9SAEU?e=519ef02502&c2id=654d9c3339d5694b9267d382db7ced0e)
| | | | | |

Friend,**THANK YOU, MO-03!**

Because of your support, our campaign has already reached more than **110,000 voters across Missouri's 3rd Congressional District!** That's roughly one in five voters in our district, and we've accomplished it with a fraction of the resources available to my opponent.
[**Now, we're setting a fundraising goal of $12,000 to help us reach the remaining 383,000 voters in MO-03 before Election Day.**](https://us.list-manage.com/17BuQtPZEyL?e=519ef02502&c2id=654d9c3339d5694b9267d382db7ced0e)
That might not sound like a particularly ambitious goal in political fundraising, but my team and I take enormous pride in being careful stewards of the resources you've entrusted to us. We know what we need to get the job done, and we're not interested in spending a dollar more than necessary.
Approximately **96% of our campaign contributions have come from right here in Missouri's 3rd Congressional District,** with most individual donations coming in under $150. That's what a genuinely grassroots campaign looks like. We haven't accepted a dime from corporate PACs or AIPAC, and we aren't about to start.
Yes, that means I've raised significantly less money than my opponent. But it also means that when I go to Washington, I won't owe political favors to wealthy donors or special interests. My responsibility will be to the people of MO-03, fighting for the infrastructure, economic security, and legislation that working families in our communities deserve.
Our campaign works harder and smarter because we understand the sacrifices people are making just to get by. For many Missouri families, the cost of groceries, housing, healthcare, and utilities leaves precious little room for anything else. We know that asking someone to contribute to a political campaign is no small thing, especially in this economy.
That's why we're asking for exactly what we need, and why we're committed to making every contribution count.

[**We've already shown what we can accomplish together with limited resources and a whole lot of determination. Now we need your help to finish what we started.**](https://us.list-manage.com/1A5MVUVegrF?e=519ef02502&c2id=654d9c3339d5694b9267d382db7ced0e)
If you're able to contribute $10, $25, $50, or whatever makes sense for your household, you'll be helping us put this campaign directly in front of more Missouri voters in these final weeks.
And if you've already given, volunteered, shared our message, or simply encouraged someone to learn more about this campaign, please know how much that means to me and my team. You've helped build something extraordinary, and we intend to honor that trust by making every dollar and every remaining day count.
**Let's bring this home for Missouri's 3rd Congressional District!**
With gratitude,Bethany MannCandidate for Congress, MO-03
[**[DONATE TO HELP US REACH EVERY VOTER]**](https://us.list-manage.com/_wTz5LCVZEk?e=519ef02502&c2id=654d9c3339d5694b9267d382db7ced0e)

* * *
Over the weekend, Donald Trump performed one of his most treacherous acts to date. He plunged a dagger into the back of Ukraine, a nation struggling against Russia's invasion. And Trump did it with the braggadocio of a demented lunatic.
Last Friday, Donald Trump announced a "massive" deal to purchase diesel fuel from Russia. The adjective was Trump's own. The consequences, however, belong to all of us. American money will flow to Vladimir Putin, a dictator who has demonstrated repeatedly what he intends to do with the funds: buy weapons, sustain his war machine, and continue to terrorize Ukrainian civilians.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/75606a1a-0516-4b60-b932-3d293416a624?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_The Atlantic_ described the transaction as the most outrageous and heartless Trump betrayal yet, adding that it offers the President, his family, and friends corruption opportunities on a multibillion-dollar scale.
Trump would have us all believe that Russia is not an adversary of the United States, not an enemy of our European allies, and not a menace to the security of NATO. Never mind that Russia has interfered in American elections, is assisting Iran in its conflict with the United States, and keeps threatening NATO countries including Poland and Lithuania. Meanwhile, Russia maintains a strategic partnership with China, a country whose ambitions over Taiwan pose a direct threat to the U.S.
Vladimir Putin is not innocent.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/75606a1a-0516-4b60-b932-3d293416a624?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
He is a ruthless and tyrannical dictator whose government has been rightfully subjected to punishing sanctions intended to deny it access to Western capital. Those sanctions have made Putin's war against Ukraine more difficult to finance. Enter Donald Trump, arriving on Friday afternoon with what amounts to a financial transfusion for Russia.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/b60b2f73-3d07-4e4b-a54d-0dac4044ae26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
###### This data is presented as part of a partnership with Polymarket
So, what is the United States getting in return? A reduction in the cost of diesel? A grateful nod from the Kremlin? Perhaps a few kind words from Moscow's propaganda machine?
Whatever the consideration, it is difficult to imagine a bargain more disadvantageous to American interests.
There is, to begin with, the matter of the law.

Case File No DRT-ED-SUBPRIME · Special File · The Locked Door
In 2007, the Warning Signs Were Locked Funds and Rising Bad Loans. Look What’s Happening in a $3 Trillion Market Now.
Investors have tried to pull billions out of private credit funds this year and been told to wait. Banks have lent nearly $2 trillion into the sector. A Reuters columnist says the alarm bells echo 2007. Most people don’t know their own money may be exposed.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
Most Americans have never heard the term “private credit.” That’s part of the problem. It’s a giant lending market that operates mostly outside the public eye, and it has grown into one of the biggest pools of debt in the financial system. In 2026, it started showing cracks.
The evidence board
| | What the Cracks Look Like
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the size.** Private credit grew from roughly $2 trillion in 2020 to more than $3 trillion by the end of 2025.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the locked doors.** In February, Blue Owl froze withdrawals from one of its retail funds. In March, Apollo and Ares limited how much investors could take out. Bloomberg reported that investors asked for about $13 billion back from more than a dozen funds, and over $4.6 billion was left stuck.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the weak loans.** Loans where borrowers pay interest with more debt instead of cash rose to 8% of private credit, double the share in 2019. Moody’s cut one large fund’s rating to junk.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit D — the link to your bank.** Banks have lent nearly $2 trillion to non-bank lenders, up from $1.5 trillion a year earlier. Pension funds and insurance companies are among the biggest investors in private credit.
| CHATTER
---
Withdrawal requests eased in September, according to recent reports, but the limits are still in place. In 2007, the calm months came before the storm, not after it.
Why it matters to you
| | Where This Could Reach You
---|---
| →| **Your retirement account.** Pension funds increasingly hold private assets, and new federal rules aim to open 401(k)s to them too.
---|---
| →| **Your annuity or insurance policy.** Insurers are some of the largest buyers of private credit.
---|---
| →| **Your bank.** Nearly $2 trillion in bank loans now flows to non-bank lenders.
---|---
Decoder
| | The Headline That Should Worry You
---|---
| | “Private credit alarm bells echo 2007 subprime warnings.”— Reuters column headline, 2026
---|---
What it says
The same warning signs that came before the 2008 crisis are showing up again.
What it means
**Our theory:** the column is careful to say every crisis is different. But the pattern rhymes: fast growth, loose lending, assets that are hard to value, and investors who suddenly can’t get their money out. In 2007, the people who acted on the early warnings protected their wealth. The ones who waited for confirmation got the crisis instead.
| ClassificationPressure building
---
The cracks are already visible: frozen funds, junk ratings, weaker loans. They haven’t become a crisis yet, which is exactly why this is the moment to look closely, not after the headlines turn.

It hides inside pensions, annuities, insurance products and bank balance sheets. The analysts who warned before 2008 say there are specific steps you can take now to protect yourself, and even come out ahead.The time to prepare is before the door locks, not after.

| | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
**October 13, 2026** **WESTFIELD, IN** - Legal counsel for Congresswoman **Victoria Spartz** has sent additional cease-and-desist letters to **J.D. Ford** ’s campaign and the Commonsense Hoosiers PAC, demanding they stop distributing falsified, AI-generated political advertisements that violate Indiana election law. **Ford** ’s latest ad, “The Heist,” uses fabricated AI images to depict **Spartz** committing crimes she never committed.
