Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers and his wife Kristi Rogers at a campaign event in Highland Township, Michigan on October 9, 2026. Photo by Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images.
Mike Rogers and his second wife, Kristi, saw their wealth rise substantially after Rogers was elevated to chair of the House Intelligence Committee in 2011 and lucrative government contracts poured her way, a review of financial disclosures finds.
Rogers was first elected to Congress in 2000, in time to be a major backer of the Iraq war. With a background at the FBI, Rogers was encouraged by Speaker Dennis Hastert to get involved in foreign policy and national security matters. According to the [Rogers Archive at Oakland University,](https://substack.com/redirect/5b119734-5e88-44fe-9ec6-fcb282f12565?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) he made seven trips to Iraq between 2001 and 2005 as a member of Congress. In 2005, he was appointed to the House Intelligence Committee. (Drop Site could not independently verify the number of trips, but taking seven trips to Iraq in the space of four years would be highly unusual for a member of Congress--and trips in 2001 or 2002, before the invasion, are unlikely.)
Kristi Clemens was a top press aide to L. Paul Bremer, who oversaw the U.S. occupation of Iraq as head of the Coalition Provisional Authority. Clemens turned heads in DC in 2006, when, following her role in Iraq, she successfully pitched the major British security contractor Aegis Defence Services to launch an American offshoot. Within three years, she rose to CEO and president. Rogers divorced his wife of 17 years in 2007 and married Clemens in 2010. By 2011, when Mike Rogers assumed his chairmanship, she was vice chair of Aegis LLC US.
After his divorce, according to Rogers's financial disclosures, the congressman had few assets to his name and little wealth. That would soon change.

The Rogers family added at least hundreds of thousands of dollars to their net worth as Rogers was elevated to chair of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence (HPSCI) and Kristi Rogers's private military security company received increasingly large contracts from the U.S. government, according to Rogers's financial disclosures. The couple added millions more after Rogers left the House and began working in the industry he had spent years overseeing.
While Rogers is not required to disclose his spouse's income, their reported "Unearned Income," including multiple investment funds, dividends, and interest income, soared over those years. They also acquired two mortgages in Maryland and Virginia--neither principal residences.

In 2010, Aegis was named one of only eight private military contractors who were qualified to bid on $10 billion of contracts for the State Department's Worldwide Protection (WWP) program. The biggest fish, the Kabul Afghanistan Embassy Security contract, first went to another firm but was re-competed and awarded to Aegis LLC.
Kristi Rogers claimed credit for this in a biography later scrubbed from the website of the law firm Manatt, Phelps & Phillips, which stated she led "a two-year pursuit and capture strategy to win a five-year, $10 billion contract." Mike Rogers was appointed Chairman on January 3, 2011; the contract was awarded to Aegis seven months later, on July 29th, 2011.

## **From Opioids to Intel**
Mike Rogers [spent his first eight years in Congress](https://substack.com/redirect/c74ba701-bea2-4772-b2df-29fb9daf429d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as a lead advocate for the opioid industry in Congress, but as the resulting epidemic surged and his longtime patrons came under federal investigation, he pivoted fully to national security following the Tea Party wave of 2010 that swept Republicans to power.
As chair of HPSCI, Rogers had access to sensitive and top secret intelligence that is unavailable to rank-and-file lawmakers, and the position is one of the most powerful in Washington. (Technically, the Appropriations Committee is supposed to have more power over spending decisions in Congress, but legislation now is generally adopted through a so-called "continuing resolution" or an omnibus spending package, bypassing regular order.)
In 2007, Rogers got into a public battle with then-Rep. Jack Murtha (D-Penn.) when Rogers attempted to defund the National Intelligence Drug Center, based in Murtha's district. Rogers [argued the money](https://substack.com/redirect/fc698106-48d8-4c67-afd5-11d19bde464c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) "takes precious intelligence resources from spies on the ground catching terrorists in places like Fallujah, Iraq, and sends it to bureaucrats in Johnstown, Pennsylvania." Aegis, of course, was a leading provider of security contracting in Iraq at the time.
Rogers and his wife rose in tandem. By her own account in Washington Exec, Kristi Clemens[ in 2006 made a pitch to start the U.S. branch of Aegis Defence Ltd](https://substack.com/redirect/0a360eb0-36fe-4ad0-9074-6e51e80e1988?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), to the company's board, which included a 5-Star UK Colonel and Winston Churchill's grandson. It's not clear whether he and Clemens had met yet. The company made her executive vice president, then president in 2008, chief executive in 2009, president in 2010, and vice chairman in 2011.
Aegis, a UK private military contractor, was founded by Tim Spicer, a controversial figure thanks to three international scandals involving his first company, Sandline. The Nation [reported in 2004](https://substack.com/redirect/01f4bfd8-0bf0-43b6-ac78-495aa4ca1f31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Spicer had been caught "violating a UN Arms embargo in Sierra Leone and unwittingly triggering a coup in Papua New Guinea," prompting its military to arrest Spicer. They found $400,000 in cash on him. It was a surprise to many in Iraq and D.C. that Spicer's new firm, Aegis Defence Services,[ landed a major $293 million Pentagon contract](https://substack.com/redirect/0e73fea6-ec95-405c-94ce-141c0936b915?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2004 to protect U.S. diplomats in Iraq. Five Democratic U.S. senators, led by Ted Kennedy, appealed to Secretary of State Donald Rumsfeld to reconsider the award based on Spicer's scandals, but were rebuffed. By 2007, with Kristi Rogers in place at Aegis U.S.,[ the largest single contract--for $475 million dollars](https://substack.com/redirect/3ec197f1-a1dd-40b5-a3dd-6cc785d68651?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--was awarded to Aegis by the Defense Department; it included supporting the Army Corps of Engineers in reconstruction operations in Iraq.
The 2004 contract made Aegis head of the regional operating centers and later the Contractor Operations Cell (CONOC), responsible for providing situational awareness and coordinating the movements of private security contractors. That put Aegis in charge of coordination of all the other private military contractors in Iraq, earning Aegis's Spicer the moniker of[ "the general in charge of all of the private contractors,"](https://substack.com/redirect/0e73fea6-ec95-405c-94ce-141c0936b915?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Under Aegis ostensible oversight, Blackwater contractors were involved in the 2007 Nisour Square massacre, in which 17 innocent Iraqi civilians were killed. In 2005, [Aegis drew international attention ](https://substack.com/redirect/6b34062d-366b-4ddf-99e2-b57037f568fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)when one of their gunmen posted a video of their vehicle wildly shooting at civilian vehicles en route from the Green Zone to the airport, set to the Elvis song, "Mystery Train." At least one civilian was reported killed.
None of it stopped the company's rise. Aegis was awarded the Armed Contractor Oversight Directorate, or ACOD, contract in 2009 for Afghanistan, which oversees contractors. That produced a glaring conflict of interest--overseeing other contractors while also bidding against them--and one former ACOD whistleblower ordered what's called a "Cure Notice," effectively calling out a conflict-of-interest and demanding it be fixed.
A congressional commission set up to root out waste and fraud in wartime contracting called Kristi Rogers to testify, but she begged off, citing her honeymoon in spring 2010. One commissioner at the hearing noted that he understood her board had advised her not to attend.
That summer, [on June 21, 2010, she testified as Aegis's president.](https://substack.com/redirect/0b6afa8c-a376-42fb-955b-a9c5d341eac4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Commissioner Charles Tiefer put it to her that Aegis personnel "currently operate the CONOC [the center coordinating other armed contractors] in Iraq." "We support it, yes," she said.
Kristi Rogers said the whistleblower who had flagged the conflicts of interest was a "disgruntled former employee," but she admitted the company was forced to terminate its ACOD duties.
Despite the scandals, 20 months later, Aegis landed that $1.017 billion contract to secure the Kabul, Afghanistan Embassy. .
The pursuit of further contracts took Aegis to Libya, where NATO intervention had produced widespread violence with the overthrow of Moamar Gaddafi. Aegis had an intelligence arm called Aegis Advisory Services, in Libya, with a large team in Tripoli that boasted of top security clearance status, and clients which included the world's elite private intelligence group, Stratfor.
In September 2012, a U.S. compound in Benghazi was sacked, killing four Americans: two private contractors, the U.S. ambassador to Libya, and a State Department official. Al Jazeera later reported that Aegis had been bidding for a $5 billion contract to secure all of Libya's porous borders. In 2014, the conservative group Judicial Watch, relying in part on documents published by WikiLeaks, found that Aegis had been heavily active in Libya since early 2011 and that it had assessed Benghazi in the summer before the attack.
## **After Benghazi**
Republicans spent years investigating the lapses and policy decisions that led to the fatal attack, while Kristi Rogers and her company were walled off from the Intelligence Committee, a spokesperson said at the time. Through its spokesperson Susan Phalan, HPSCI announced a "no interaction policy with Mrs. Rogers or any Aegis employee." (The no interaction policy presumably did not apply between husband and wife.)
Judicial Watch's Micah Morrison [was unsparing ](https://substack.com/redirect/e25d47fe-efc1-4375-90ae-13508aacc30d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)in its criticism of Rogers in a report headlined "Unraveling Benghazi: Is Mike Rogers Part of the Problem?":
> Sussing out the White House's response to Benghazi is a critical step in clearing the shadows from the incident, but there are other players in the drama as well, including Rep. Rogers, and possibly also including a private military contracting firm that until recently was run by his wife, Kristi Rogers. Mike and Kristi Rogers are quintessential Washington insiders. A seven-term Republican from Michigan, Mike Rogers climbed the political ladder to become chairman of the Intelligence Committee in January 2011. Kristi Rogers, after years of government service in mid-level administrative positions, moved to the private sector, joining the British-based security contractor Aegis Defense Services to help open its U.S. subsidiary. The newsletter Intelligence Online noted that thanks to Ms. Rogers' efforts, "Aegis won several major contracts with the U.S. administration."
> A spokesperson for the House Intelligence Committee noted that "strictly observed and enforced" policies required "that there should be no interaction with Mrs. Rogers on any matter relating to the official business of the House" and "no interaction between the Committee and any representative of Aegis." There is no evidence of wrong-doing by Rep. Rogers or Aegis. Indeed, the outlines of the story are more suggestive of "right-doing," Washington-style: an insider's game of covert operations and corporate profits played out in the gray areas of law and policy.
That spring--though, as Judicial Watch noted, there was no direct evidence of criminal wrongdoing--Rogers announced he would not be running for re-election, and his wife left Aegis. Rogers went into corporate and cyber security work, and was floated as CIA director in the first Trump administration.
Leading right-wing pollster and operative Dick Morris, who had questioned Mike Rogers's oversight of Benghazi, wanted to make sure that conservatives never forgot about his work. Rogers had fought the formation of a special committee to investigate it, and conservatives believed he was slow-walking the probe to protect his wife's company. "The first to go--and most deserving--is former Congressman and House Intelligence Committee Chairman Mike Rogers," Morris [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/101b6bf8-dfdf-4e1e-a460-78be6993f790?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). "Slated, some say, to be the new director of the CIA, Rogers was a key force in obstructing and delaying the Benghazi investigation in order to shield his wife, Kristi, from scrutiny."
Morris went on: "Aegis had won several major contracts, likely through Mrs. Rogers' influence as the wife of the House Intel Committee. Although not directly responsible for security at Benghazi, her firm had significant responsibilities in the area."
The late Sen. Lindsey Graham called the HPSCI report on Benghazi[ "full of crap,"](https://substack.com/redirect/88592958-976a-4fd2-8845-256d682320c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) while former U.S. Attorney Joe DiGenova [went on WMAL Radio in D.C. ](https://substack.com/redirect/1ffff1ad-1add-4716-982f-dc6c9a88a04a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)during the hearings and accused Mike Rogers of "sabotaging the Benghazi hearings" and went so far as to warn future Republicans to pay attention to the "dishonorable conduct of Mike Rogers."
Judicial Watch's Micah Morrison called the couple the "quintessential Washington insiders." In November 2012, the Rogers family took a six-day, all-expenses-paid trip to Buenos Aires, Argentina, costing its sponsors, the Franklin Center and the Ripon Center, $23,540.
Rogers announced his departure on the Paul W. Smith morning drive show on WJR Radio in Detroit on March 28, 2014, saying that he would finish his term and become a talk radio host on Cumulus Radio, WJR's syndicator. On the show, Rogers said he always believed in "a citizen legislature," that he had a private-sector career before his public service, and that he intended to return to one.
After his years spent regulating the surveillance industry as chair of the Intelligence Committee, Rogers began working with multiple cybersecurity companies.
Rogers ran unsuccessfully for the Michigan Senate in 2024 and is running again in 2026. His Democratic opponent, Abdul El-Sayed, [has repeatedly attacked him](https://substack.com/redirect/760b011e-3757-4a32-b1fd-ca264ffb987c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for making up to $14 million in the private sector from the types of companies he was tasked with regulating.
The Rogers campaign did not respond to requests for comment, but Rogers has previously insisted that his work in Congress and his wife's work as head of Aegis U.S. were kept separate.

(Technically, the Appropriations Committee is supposed to have more power over spending decisions in Congress, but legislation now is generally adopted through a so-called "continuing resolution" or an omnibus spending package, bypassing regular order.) In 2007, Rogers got into a public battle with then-Rep. Jack Murtha (D-Penn.) when Rogers attempted to defund the National Intelligence Drug Center, based in Murtha's district. Rogers "takes precious intelligence resources from spies on the ground catching terrorists in places like Fallujah, Iraq, and sends it to bureaucrats in Johnstown, Pennsylvania." Aegis, of course, was a leading provider of security contracting in Iraq at the time. Rogers and his wife rose in tandem. By her own account in Washington Exec, Kristi Clemens, to the company's board, which included a 5-Star UK Colonel and Winston Churchill's grandson. It's not clear whether he and Clemens had met yet. The company made her executive vice president, then president in 2008, chief executive in 2009, president in 2010, and vice chairman in 2011. Aegis, a UK private military contractor, was founded by Tim Spicer, a controversial figure thanks to three international scandals involving his first company, Sandline. The Nation that Spicer had been caught "violating a UN Arms embargo in Sierra Leone and unwittingly triggering a coup in Papua New Guinea," prompting its military to arrest Spicer. They found $400,000 in cash on him. It was a surprise to many in Iraq and D.C. that Spicer's new firm, Aegis Defence Services, in 2004 to protect U.S. diplomats in Iraq. Five Democratic U.S. senators, led by Ted Kennedy, appealed to Secretary of State Donald Rumsfeld to reconsider the award based on Spicer's scandals, but were rebuffed. By 2007, with Kristi Rogers in place at Aegis U.S., awarded to Aegis by the Defense Department; it included supporting the Army Corps of Engineers in reconstruction operations in Iraq. The 2004 contract made Aegis head of the regional operating centers and later the Contractor Operations Cell (CONOC), responsible for providing situational awareness and coordinating the movements of private security contractors. That put Aegis in charge of coordination of all the other private military contractors in Iraq, earning Aegis's Spicer the moniker of Under Aegis ostensible oversight, Blackwater contractors were involved in the 2007 Nisour Square massacre, in which 17 innocent Iraqi civilians were killed. In 2005, one of their gunmen posted a video of their vehicle wildly shooting at civilian vehicles en route from the Green Zone to the airport, set to the Elvis song, "Mystery Train." At least one civilian was reported killed. None of it stopped the company's rise. Aegis was awarded the Armed Contractor Oversight Directorate, or ACOD, contract in 2009 for Afghanistan, which oversees contractors. That produced a glaring conflict of interest--overseeing other contractors while also bidding against them--and one former ACOD whistleblower ordered what's called a "Cure Notice," effectively calling out a conflict-of-interest and demanding it be fixed. A congressional commission set up to root out waste and fraud in wartime contracting called Kristi Rogers to testify, but she begged off, citing her honeymoon in spring 2010. One commissioner at the hearing noted that he understood her board had advised her not to attend. That summer, Commissioner Charles Tiefer put it to her that Aegis personnel "currently operate the CONOC [the center coordinating other armed contractors] in Iraq." "We support it, yes," she said. Kristi Rogers said the whistleblower who had flagged the conflicts of interest was a "disgruntled former employee," but she admitted the company was forced to terminate its ACOD duties. Despite the scandals, 20 months later, Aegis landed that $1.017 billion contract to secure the Kabul, Afghanistan Embassy. . The pursuit of further contracts took Aegis to Libya, where NATO intervention had produced widespread violence with the overthrow of Moamar Gaddafi. Aegis had an intelligence arm called Aegis Advisory Services, in Libya, with a large team in Tripoli that boasted of top security clearance status, and clients which included the world's elite private intelligence group, Stratfor. In September 2012, a U.S. compound in Benghazi was sacked, killing four Americans: two private contractors, the U.S. ambassador to Libya, and a State Department official. Al Jazeera later reported that Aegis had been bidding for a $5 billion contract to secure all of Libya's porous borders. In 2014, the conservative group Judicial Watch, relying in part on documents published by WikiLeaks, found that Aegis had been heavily active in Libya since early 2011 and that it had assessed Benghazi in the summer before the attack. After Benghazi Republicans spent years investigating the lapses and policy decisions that led to the fatal attack, while Kristi Rogers and her company were walled off from the Intelligence Committee, a spokesperson said at the time. Through its spokesperson Susan Phalan, HPSCI announced a "no interaction policy with Mrs. Rogers or any Aegis employee." (The no interaction policy presumably did not apply between husband and wife.) Judicial Watch's Micah Morrison its criticism of Rogers in a report headlined "Unraveling Benghazi: Is Mike Rogers Part of the Problem?": Sussing out the White House's response to Benghazi is a critical step in clearing the shadows from the incident, but there are other players in the drama as well, including Rep. Rogers, and possibly also including a private military contracting firm that until recently was run by his wife, Kristi Rogers. Mike and Kristi Rogers are quintessential Washington insiders. A seven-term Republican from Michigan, Mike Rogers climbed the political ladder to become chairman of the Intelligence Committee in January 2011. Kristi Rogers, after years of government service in mid-level administrative positions, moved to the private sector, joining the British-based security contractor Aegis Defense Services to help open its U.S. subsidiary. The newsletter Intelligence Online noted that thanks to Ms. Rogers' efforts, "Aegis won several major contracts with the U.S. administration." A spokesperson for the House Intelligence Committee noted that "strictly observed and enforced" policies required "that there should be no interaction with Mrs. Rogers on any matter relating to the official business of the House" and "no interaction between the Committee and any representative of Aegis." There is no evidence of wrong-doing by Rep. Rogers or Aegis. Indeed, the outlines of the story are more suggestive of "right-doing," Washington-style: an insider's game of covert operations and corporate profits played out in the gray areas of law and policy. That spring--though, as Judicial Watch noted, there was no direct evidence of criminal wrongdoing--Rogers announced he would not be running for re-election, and his wife left Aegis. Rogers went into corporate and cyber security work, and was floated as CIA director in the first Trump administration. Leading right-wing pollster and operative Dick Morris, who had questioned Mike Rogers's oversight of Benghazi, wanted to make sure that conservatives never forgot about his work. Rogers had fought the formation of a special committee to investigate it, and conservatives believed he was slow-walking the probe to protect his wife's company. "The first to go--and most deserving--is former Congressman and House Intelligence Committee Chairman Mike Rogers," Morris . "Slated, some say, to be the new director of the CIA, Rogers was a key force in obstructing and delaying the Benghazi investigation in order to shield his wife, Kristi, from scrutiny." Morris went on: "Aegis had won several major contracts, likely through Mrs. Rogers' influence as the wife of the House Intel Committee. Although not directly responsible for security at Benghazi, her firm had significant responsibilities in the area." The late Sen. Lindsey Graham called the HPSCI report on Benghazi while former U.S. Attorney Joe DiGenova the hearings and accused Mike Rogers of "sabotaging the Benghazi hearings" and went so far as to warn future Republicans to pay attention to the "dishonorable conduct of Mike Rogers." Judicial Watch's Micah Morrison called the couple the "quintessential Washington insiders." In November 2012, the Rogers family took a six-day, all-expenses-paid trip to Buenos Aires, Argentina, costing its sponsors, the Franklin Center and the Ripon Center, $23,540. Rogers announced his departure on the Paul W. Smith morning drive show on WJR Radio in Detroit on March 28, 2014, saying that he would finish his term and become a talk radio host on Cumulus Radio, WJR's syndicator. On the show, Rogers said he always believed in "a citizen legislature," that he had a private-sector career before his public service, and that he intended to return to one. After his years spent regulating the surveillance industry as chair of the Intelligence Committee, Rogers began working with multiple cybersecurity companies. Rogers ran unsuccessfully for the Michigan Senate in 2024 and is running again in 2026. His Democratic opponent, Abdul El-Sayed, for making up to $14 million in the private sector from the types of companies he was tasked with regulating. The Rogers campaign did not respond to requests for comment, but Rogers has previously insisted that his work in Congress and his wife's work as head of Aegis U.S. were kept separate. Nancy Skinner is a longtime radio and television commentator and was previously a Democratic candidate for office. She has made small campaign contributions to Abdul El-Sayed 's Senate campaign. A Denver sheriff’s deputy filled out a notification form in late

Streets.

describes him as a suspected Tren de Aragua member who had been in

That form now sits in a congressional report.

PROPOSITION 137 PROMISES MILLIONS FOR COLORADO PUBLIC LANDS, BUT
LAWMAKERS RETAIN FINAL SAY
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

THE COLORADO SUN
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_Proposition 137 promises roughly $175 million a year for land
conservation and wildfire mitigation, but built-in triggers and
legislative discretion mean the money may never actually arrive._

*
A MEASURE DESIGNED TO TURN ITSELF OFF: Proposition 137 includes a
trigger that reduces or eliminates its funding diversion in years when
it would affect the Family Affordability Tax Credit or Earned Income
Tax Credit, and nonpartisan staff already project both credits will be
unavailable in 2027, which a backer concedes was intentional to avoid
conflict.

*
LAWMAKERS HAVE SIGNALED THEY’LL IGNORE IT ANYWAY: Because
Proposition 137 is a statutory measure rather than a constitutional
one, Democrats in the legislature, including House Speaker Julie
McCluskie, have said they retain discretion to redirect the revenue
elsewhere in tight budget years, and Republicans on the Legislative
Council Committee objected when Democrats tried to add that caveat to
the official ballot guide.

*
A COMPETING MEASURE COULD SQUEEZE IT FURTHER: If Proposition NN also
passes, it would let the state keep TABOR surplus dollars for K-12 and
early childhood education instead of refunding them, directly
competing with the surplus funds Proposition 137 depends on and giving
lawmakers another reason to bypass its spending directives.

| | Peter, it ain’t over ‘till it’s over!

**Here’s what’s happening: key House and State Legislature races are dramatically shifting towards Democrats. Red districts that were won by 20 points in 2024 are now _neck and neck._**

The skeptics keep writing us off. They claim Florida is a lost cause, locked up by far-right special interests and Ron DeSantis’s megadonor apparatus. They keep telling us to throw in the towel and focus elsewhere.

I’m not buying it, and I know you aren't either. We just need to make sure voters across Florida stay in this fight, too.

**_[With 21 days until Election Day and a massive number of voters to reach in this final stretch, we need grassroots support to power our organizing teams on the ground. A deep dive into New Hampshire U.S. Senate candidate Chris Pappas's border-security policies reveals that they closely align with Abdul El-Sayed and Hasan Piker, which is no surprise given Pappas' recent refusal to condemn the duo's radical agenda to destroy our country.
Currently a member of the U.S. House of Representatives, Chris Pappas' voting record shows he is an open-border extremist, just like El-Sayed and Piker. On September 11, 2025, of all days, Pappas voted Nay on [H.R. 3486, the Stop Illegal Entry Act](https://substack.com/redirect/053c97d0-d3ea-4dc0-9edd-b78453d77392?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Then in January, Pappas also voted Nay on [H.R. 7147, the DHS Appropriations Act of 2026](https://substack.com/redirect/b64840c1-df10-402b-8620-3f249ac8970b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which was essentially a vote to defund Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ecbdc219-bc6d-48b2-b3ba-72c8b42b4c76?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/94595501-8e7f-4805-ac81-e38d42c957e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Following his no vote on H.R. 7147, Pappas issued a statement on his [official House website](https://substack.com/redirect/66f39f96-7325-4f59-8c78-fb5878082226?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) demanding "guardrails" for ICE:
"Knowing this, I voted against this spending bill because American citizens and taxpayers deserve accountable government and commonsense guardrails for ICE."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/65da7b23-f931-40b5-87bd-2db395ee6b95?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Then, in June, Pappas posted to X his anger centered around the fact that House Republicans voted to fund ICE while also portraying anti-ICE agitators Renee Good and Alex Pretti as victims:

"House Republicans just passed another enormous blank check to ICE -- $70 million. No reforms. No guardrails. No oversight. No accountability for Renee Good and Alex Pretti."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9c279f51-d2bd-4575-806c-672f16ce7d94?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Like El-Sayed and Piker, Pappas has built quite a lengthy list of statements that express disdain for ICE, even praising violent anti-ICE protesters earlier this month during a campaign event with Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), who also wants to abolish ICE. During their event, Pappas stated:
"We still have the power in our hands. Whether it was those protesters down in the town of Merrimack, New Hampshire, who stopped the ICE detention center."

Greg Abbott's latest campaign finance report shows he raised $20 million during this reporting period.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a8d9740c-472e-4538-a9d6-1176f357524e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But there's something else it said: he's bankrolled by billionaire CEOs and data center corporations. A shock to nobody.
While Texans are struggling with sky-high electricity bills and property taxes that have shot up 85% under Abbott's decade-plus long tenure, he's busy lining his pockets and selling Texans out to the highest bidder. The link couldn't be clearer. Kelcy Warren and Thomas Long, co-CEOs of a _major_ energy company, have given $600,000 to Abbott's campaign. They saw record profits after Winter Storm Uri left thousands of Texans without power for _days_. Andrew Schapp, CEO of a data center company has given Abbott $50,000 and is _unaffected_ by Abbott's "audit" of data centers and how they are disrupting Texas communities.
**In the last two filing periods, Abbott has received $5.2 million directly from business entities and at least $6.9 million from oil, gas, energy and utility interests. Just 52 donors accounted for more than 70% of everything Abbott raised.**
Greg Abbott can't work for the people of Texas because he is beholden to special interests. Me on the other hand? I'm proud to say that this campaign is 95% funded by grassroots supporters chipping in what they can because they believe in this campaign.
While Greg Abbott has burned through $146 million in spending against me, five polls in the last month all tell the same story: we're leading in the race for governor. Because Texans are ready for change.
**There 's one fight this year: will Texas be a state that is by and for the people, or is this the billionaires' world and we just live here? If Abbott stays in the Governor's mansion, we already have our answer -- $1 billion scammed out of neighborhood public schools, the highest uninsured rate in the country, and the largest data center in the entire world, right here in our backyard.**
Texans deserve a governor who will secure the American Dream by saving our public schools, putting money back in their pockets, and ending Abbott's decades of corruption -- and come November, I'm ready to deliver.
**[Getting Abbott out of the Governor's mansion won't be easy. It will take all of us stepping up in these final three weeks before Election Day. Will you please keep the momentum on our side by chipping in $5 or more to my campaign today? I'm fighting for the future of Texas and would be honored to have your support.](https://substack.com/redirect/a8d9740c-472e-4538-a9d6-1176f357524e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

This campaign belongs to the people, and that's exactly who I'll answer to.

Creating real change means moving past the political labels.
| | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141343422/653245414/15057203?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk770&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjYxMjYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGNjNzk5N2UtNGFjNy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=l16wmI4h6_PbUpRZi5h0dTZ_AlSV61qDpPcu4o6CevM=)

Friend, there’s one question people ask me at every campaign stop: “Are you liberal or conservative?”
My answer, every time, is “Yes, of course.”
When I say that, people almost always stare at me for a second, and then they blurt out, “No, no, _which are you?_ ”
I get why they’re asking. In these deeply divided times, people put a lot of stock in how we label ourselves politically. If someone identifies as liberal, people think they know what that person stands for. Same if someone defines themselves as conservative. But like I tell the people who ask me which I am: **_I think we can — and must — be both._**
**To be liberal can mean to be generous of spirit, open to reform and able to see things with fresh eyes. To be conservative can mean holding on to values and beliefs that are really important.**
Those are both important perspectives to bring to the table — and I think at some level, we all know we are not 100% one or the other all of the time. Maybe you think of yourself as an incredibly liberal person. I bet you’re still conservative compared to _someone_ you know. And if you identify as deeply conservative — well, I bet you can still think of someone that _you’re_ liberal compared to.
That’s why I don’t focus on the political label. I think what matters far more is whether you stand up for your neighbors and your community. And after talking to thousands of people throughout the state, I think Kansans agree with me. That’s probably why I’ve had more people than I can count come up to me and say, “I’ve never voted for a Democrat, but I’m going to vote for you.”
**Friend, this might not be a typical approach to politics, but I believe it’s resonating with voters. It’s why we’re narrowly leading in the polls and Roger Marshall and his allies are spending big to slow us down. **Maybe I see that more clearly because I’m _not_ a career politician. My focus is and always has been on serving everyone — and the thousands of people I’ve talked to throughout the state seem to resonate with that unifying message.**

clean_body: Creating real change means moving past the political labels. | | | = Friend, there’s one question people ask me at every campaign stop: “Are you liberal or conservative?” My answer, every time, is “Yes, of course.” When I say that, people almost always stare at me for a second, and then they blurt out, “No, no, which are you? ” I get why they’re asking. In these deeply divided times, people put a lot of stock in how we label ourselves politically. If someone identifies as liberal, people think they know what that person stands for. Same if someone defines themselves as conservative. But like I tell the people who ask me which I am: I think we can — and must — be both. To be liberal can mean to be generous of spirit, open to reform and able to see things with fresh eyes. To be conservative can mean holding on to values and beliefs that are really important. Those are both important perspectives to bring to the table — and I think at some level, we all know we are not 100% one or the other all of the time. Maybe you think of yourself as an incredibly liberal person. I bet you’re still conservative compared to someone you know. And if you identify as deeply conservative — well, I bet you can still think of someone that you’re liberal compared to. That’s why I don’t focus on the political label. I think what matters far more is whether you stand up for your neighbors and your community. And after talking to thousands of people throughout the state, I think Kansans agree with me. That’s probably why I’ve had more people than I can count come up to me and say, “I’ve never voted for a Democrat, but I’m going to vote for you.” Friend, this might not be a typical approach to politics, but I believe it’s resonating with voters. It’s why we’re narrowly leading in the polls and Roger Marshall and his allies are spending big to slow us down. I don’t take money from corporate PACs, which means I rely on donations from people like you to fight back.= If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | | = | | = | | = Friend, the extreme political division that’s taken root in this country isn’t serving any of us. We need each other. Our systems only function when we work with each other ... when we fight a bit and argue some, then come up with a compromise that takes into account the concerns of both sides. Maybe I see that more clearly because I’m not a career politician. My focus is and always has been on serving everyone — and the thousands of people I’ve talked to throughout the state seem to resonate with that unifying message. That’s probably why so many people have come up to me and said, “I’ve never voted for a Democrat, but I’m going to vote for you.” It’s probably why I’m leading Roger Marshall in the polls AND why election experts keep upgrading our chances of winning. Because it’s not about the label, friend. It’s about a leader showing up for the people they represent with generosity of spirit, a spirit of reform and a deep loyalty to the values that make this country great. = If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | | = | | = | | = Thank you, Adam Hamilton | Adam Hamilton is a husband, father, pastor and fifth-generation Kansan. Now, he’s running for U.S. Senate as an independent-minded Democrat. Just like you, he’s tired of the chaos and corruption in Washington that is harming our farmers, raising costs at the checkout line and making critical health care services unattainable. He hears your concerns and is ready to get to work for you. subject: I debated an empty podium

We have three weeks. Everything we have built comes down to what happens next.

New national polls show Latino voters are swinging back to Democrats in a big way. About one in seven Latinos who voted for Trump in 2024 now want Democrats in charge.

That is exactly why my campaign is not waiting. We are investing in reaching Latino voters across Wisconsin through digital, Latino radio, and mail, so our community knows their voice matters.

| | | | JoCasta Zamarripa is a lifelong Milwaukeean, a proud daughter of the city’s south side, and a dedicated public servant who’s never stopped fighting for working people. Born and raised in the very neighborhoods she now represents, JoCasta has spent her life pushing for progress that reflects the realities of everyday Wisconsinites.

[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/1D4JHgN9OUh?e=8d919f2092&c2id=0bdcb6d83cbc8b2aaf05afb952b88bb7)

She made history as the first Latina and first openly bi member of both the Wisconsin State Legislature and the Milwaukee Common Council. But JoCasta’s leadership is defined by more than her historic firsts—it's grounded in results. She served ten years in the State Assembly and is now in her second term as Alderperson for Milwaukee’s 8th District, where she’s led major efforts on affordable housing, small business licensing reform, and community development.

In 2025, she was the lead sponsor of the Housing Element Plan, a key step in addressing Milwaukee’s housing crisis by expanding affordable options and preventing displacement. Her approach is practical and persistent—building coalitions, navigating political challenges, and staying rooted in the neighborhoods she serves.

Now, JoCasta is running as a Democrat for Wisconsin Secretary of State to use the platform to fight for what matters: more funding for our schools so families aren’t forced into referenda every election, real housing relief for working people, and affordable child care that lets parents breathe.

Hi team,
There's a clear contrast in this race, and voters are being asked to make a really important choice. I need your help to make sure they know that.
But first, let me show you what I mean with a quick game of Would You Rather?
**Would you rather** your tax dollars go into the pockets of billionaires, or have them invested in our local communities?
**Would you rather** see 30,000 of your neighbors get kicked off their health care, or pay lower premiums and hold insurance companies accountable?
**Would you rather** have a giant data center built in your backyard without your input, or have the ability to say no to Big Tech?
**Would you rather** your representative double their net worth in office, or fight for a congressional stock trading ban?
**Would you rather** have someone in Congress who only cares about their own bottom line, or someone who fights for YOU?
**If you chose the second option for all five of these, I need your help.**
**[Our final FEC pre-election deadline is tomorrow night. Everything we raise before then helps us make sure every voter knows what 's at stake in this race. I need your help to make sure they know that. But first, let me show you what I mean with a quick game of Would You Rather? Would you rather your tax dollars go into the pockets of billionaires, or have them invested in our local communities? Would you rather see 30,000 of your neighbors get kicked off their health care, or pay lower premiums and hold insurance companies accountable? Would you rather have a giant data center built in your backyard without your input, or have the ability to say no to Big Tech? Would you rather your representative double their net worth in office, or fight for a congressional stock trading ban? They are preparing to lay off up to 30% of the entire agency's workforce—firing the very park rangers, ecologists, and wildland firefighters who protect our public lands and keep them accessible for the American people. You don't fire a third of the National Park Service to save a few bucks. You do it because a crippled, understaffed agency is infinitely easier to break apart and sell to the highest bidder. The backdoor deal they are trying to force through in Yosemite right now is just the test run. If they successfully hand over the birthplace of our national park system to a private developer while simultaneously firing the rangers who protect it, no wild space in this country is safe. At Public Land Warriors, we are building a massive, targeted digital ad blitz to expose this exact scam. We are going to make sure every voter knows exactly who is firing our park rangers and auctioning off our national parks to corporate developers. They think they can quietly sell us out to the highest bidder. Let's make sure it costs them their jobs. You take our land—we take your seat. body:

| | Tomorrow, the Michigan House Select Oversight Committee will hold a hearing examining the petition process surrounding the Citizen Only Voting Amendment.
The hearing begins at **10:00 a.m. on Wednesday, October 14** , and will include testimony about the petition process and the outrageous circumstances surroundingthe Bureau of Elections and the Board of State Canvassers blocking the amendment from the November ballot.
More than 700,000 Michiganders signed petitions supporting the proposed amendment. The committee hearing offers an opportunity for the public to hear testimony, examine questions about the review and certification process, and learn more about what happened.
**WATCH THE HEARING LIVE****Wednesday, October 14 | 10:00 a.m.**[CLICK HERE TO WATCH THE HOUSE OVERSIGHT COMMITTEE HEARING](https://us.list-manage.com/g9GfcPvpO3g?e=ecf60db114&c2id=b020b7081f44f277164dc2a0d73e83a2)

Our work to bring attention to the unfair petition process and the disparate treatment given the Citizen Only Voting Amendment continues.
We encourage you to stay informed, follow the testimony, and especially to learn where your elected representatives stand on citizenship verification, voter ID, and election administration.
You can also visit [**EveryVoteEveryVoter.com**](https://us.list-manage.com/bhSomdaws9h?e=ecf60db114&c2id=b020b7081f44f277164dc2a0d73e83a2) for updates and information about legislators who support the Citizen Only Voting Amendment's goals.
Thank you for remaining engaged and following this important discussion. Public participation and government accountability matter, and tomorrow's hearing is another opportunity for Michiganders to hear directly about the process.
**Every Voter. Every Vote.**
Thank you for your continued support,Americans for Citizen Voting – Michigan

subject: Announcing our $1.2 million investment
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
We meant it when we said we’re going all in to elect the next generation of young, bold leaders.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20261013-1&t=1&akid=4136%2E587540%2E_6uk1p)
Peter, I wanted you to hear this directly from me:
**Leaders We Deserve is investing $1.2 million in 11 states with must-win legislative races!**
We meant it when we said we’re going all in to elect the next generation of young, bold, progressive leaders. Thank you for everything you’ve done to support our mission and our candidates. This investment is only possible because of supporters like you chipping in what you can when you can.
We’re putting that support to work across 11 states where our candidates are running to flip chambers, break GOP supermajorities, and build the Democratic bench.
**Katrina Manetta** in Michigan is running to flip a critical seat to get Democrats within striking distance of a majority in the statehouse. Democrats are only four seats away from taking back the Michigan House.
The Wisconsin Senate has been deemed the “most flippable” state legislative body in the country. **Trevor Jung** is running in a must-win seat that can finally flip the chamber blue and stop the GOP from making Wisconsin the next stop on their map-rigging campaign.
**Ken McCool** in North Carolina is running against a Democrat-turned-Republican who only won her seat by 206 votes. With margins this tight, a win is critical. Republicans in NC are one seat away from a veto-proof majority.
**[If you’re ready to help our candidates win, please rush a $5 contribution now.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261013_1_state.jJjvuM&refcode=em20261013-4136&amount=5&t=2&akid=4136%2E587540%2E_6uk1p)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261013_1_state.jJjvuM&amount=5&refcode=em20261013-4136&t=3&akid=4136%2E587540%2E_6uk1p)**
**State legislatures don’t always make the headlines, but these are the arenas where our daily lives are shaped.**
They’re where we can stop abortion bans, throw out racist Republican gerrymandered maps, pass stricter gun laws, and expand Medicaid. They decide whether corporate landlords keep jacking up the rent with zero accountability and whether states will protect their water and land from data center encroachment.
These are some of the most pressing issues facing Americans right now — we need fighters in statehouses across the country who are ready to deliver. Leaders who aren’t afraid to challenge the status quo.
We’re making this historic investment because we believe deeply in our candidates — **we _know_ they can win with the right resources behind them.** But because their races could come down to a handful of votes, we need to have their backs and keep them competitive all the way to Election Day.
**[We can only sustain investments like this one if grassroots supporters like you step up to power them. Will you pitch in $5 today to help us elect the next generation of leaders?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261013_1_state.jJjvuM&refcode=em20261013-4136&amount=5&t=4&akid=4136%2E587540%2E_6uk1p)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

Tom Shattuck, Graham Pollard, Joe Sokol and Jon Fetherston break down Sanford's crackdown on the mill encampment. Fetherston says police searched the building with Old Orchard Beach police and the York County Sheriff's Office, and that the city council was meeting Tuesday night on extending its emergency street closure past five days. He also plays his interview with two women at the mill who say police told them to go to Portland. The panel then covers a Westbrook woman charged with drug OUI after crashing into a Bonny Eagle school bus, Joe Sokol's latest Bangor videos, the Boston Globe's scrutiny of an independent Massachusetts news site, and this fall's races, including Susan Collins's.

As permitted by law, TPPAC, Inc. maintains a non-contribution account for the purpose of influencing federal, state, and local elections. Federal law requires us to use our best efforts to collect and report the name, address, occupation, and employer of individuals whose contribution exceeds $200 in an election cycle. For contributions from federal committees, corporations, and labor unions - regardless of contribution amount - federal law requires us to use our best efforts to collect and report the committee’s name and address. State and local law may require us to collect and report additional information.

Contributions to this account may be used to influence federal elections by making independent expenditures in support of or in opposition to federal candidates. Additionally, in state and local jurisdictions that permit non-individual type (e.g., corporate) contributions directly to candidates and/or committees, contributions to this account may be used for both independent expenditures and direct contributions to candidates and/or committees, as permitted by state and local law.

Individuals, federal committees, corporations, and labor unions may contribute to TPPAC, Inc.’s non-contribution account without limit. Contributions by national banks, foreign nationals (without lawful permanent resident status), and other foreign entities (e.g., foreign corporations) are prohibited. Contributions to TPPAC, Inc.’s non-contribution account are not tax-deductible for federal income tax purposes.

Hey folks,
Donald Trump is using the federal government to go after Ilhan Omar, and Katie Miller may have just given away the whole game.
Federal agents reportedly raided Omar's home over immigration fraud allegations, and Katie Miller celebrated with a now-deleted post saying, "Promise made, promise kept." That tells you everything you need to know about what I believe is really happening here. This isn't about justice. It's about political intimidation, racism, and using the power of government to punish people Trump doesn't like.
Here's what we get into:
* [**00:01:43**] Katie Miller celebrates the reported raid on Ilhan Omar's home, then quickly deletes her post. Why that little mistake could become a massive problem for the Trump administration.
* [**00:04:24**] The deleted tweet, the desperate cleanup, and how Trump's team turns right-wing conspiracy theories into federal investigations.
* [**00:07:25**] JD Vance openly discusses targeting Omar over alleged immigration fraud. Are they investigating a crime, or working backward to manufacture a case?
* [**00:10:16**] CNN raises serious questions about federal investigations this close to an election, and why this sets a dangerous precedent for our democracy.
* [**00:13:10**] The incredible hypocrisy of Katie Miller complaining about political retaliation while celebrating the targeting of a Democratic congresswoman.

This is bigger than Ilhan Omar. It's about what happens when people in power decide the federal government is their personal weapon against political opponents. I've experienced this kind of targeting myself, and I know how devastating it can be. We cannot normalize it. We cannot look away. And we cannot let fear silence us. If you believe in accountability, democracy, and independent media willing to call this out, help me keep these conversations going.

Peter, How do you fight a captured and corrupt Supreme Court that’s chaotic and unpredictable? **By watching the state courts. Today’s state court case is tomorrow’s Supreme Court case, and what the states do now affects what will happen at the Supreme Court in the future.** Take this fall’s elections. Anti-choice judges are on the ballot in Alabama, Arizona, Florida, North Dakota, Oklahoma, and Texas. Extremist elites are working on breaking down pro-choice majorities on courts in Michigan, Ohio, North Carolina, and Montana.1 **That’s at least ten states where the balance and makeup of the courts could fundamentally change which cases are decided and how.** If extremist forces are successful, we could see attacks on our rights, pro-billionaire and corporate litigation, and anti-democracy cases vie for Supreme Court blessing for years to come. **Many of the cases on the extremist agenda? clean_body: Today’s state court case is tomorrow’s Supreme Court case. | | Peter, How do you fight a captured and corrupt Supreme Court that’s chaotic and unpredictable? By watching the state courts. Today’s state court case is tomorrow’s Supreme Court case, and what the states do now affects what will happen at the Supreme Court in the future. Take this fall’s elections. Anti-choice judges are on the ballot in Alabama, Arizona, Florida, North Dakota, Oklahoma, and Texas. Extremist elites are working on breaking down pro-choice majorities on courts in Michigan, Ohio, North Carolina, and Montana.1 That’s at least ten states where the balance and makeup of the courts could fundamentally change which cases are decided and how. If extremist forces are successful, we could see attacks on our rights, pro-billionaire and corporate litigation, and anti-democracy cases vie for Supreme Court blessing for years to come. Many of the cases on the extremist agenda? Abortion and trans rights. When the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade, the fight over reproductive rights was sent down to the states. Years later, all those state cases are coming due. Cases in Idaho and Indiana could open the issue back up at the Supreme Court soon. The Supreme Court also allowed discrimination against trans folks in a major case last year, and state courts have begun fielding these cases as well. The way these courts decide to rule on the issue means we could be fighting discrimination and bans for years to come. United for Democracy is ready to fight any battle that comes next. The corrupt, captured Supreme Court and the shadowy network of wealthy elites behind them won’t rest until they’ve stolen all of our power. That means we can’t rest either. We’re building the people-powered coalition it will take to not only fight back against the worst Supreme Court rulings, but to demand huge, fundamental changes to unrig the system. We the People are fed up, and United for Democracy is channeling the anger and energy into building a democracy where the people come first, not wealthy elites. name: Swing Left
subject: Get ready to take action this weekend
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
This weekend, No Kings events are planned in cities across the country.
#
Hi there,
This weekend, No Kings events are planned in cities across the country. Thousands of people will turn out with one clear message: we will not give up our democracy, our rights, and our freedoms without fierce grassroots resistance.
That message matters. **And the strongest answer to a would-be king is a Democratic Congress and Democratic governors across the country who can put a real check on his power.**
That’s why, with just 3 weeks left until Election Day, the Swing Left community has canvasses and phone banks planned in dozens of swing districts and states this weekend.
**So if you’re getting ready to attend a No Kings event this weekend, and you want to do even more when it’s over, there’s an easy next step.[Click here to use Swing Left’s Take Action Tool now to find the best volunteer opportunity for you during Swing Left’s upcoming Weekend of Action on October 17th and 18th.](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2654?t=1&akid=3134%2E1562180%2ETAmy1D)**
**[Take Action Now](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2654?t=2&akid=3134%2E1562180%2ETAmy1D)**
3 weeks from now, the outcome of the closest races in the country could come down to just a few hundred votes. And this weekend, thousands of Swing Left volunteers will go out to have what we hope to be the highest number of Ground Truth conversations yet with voters on the doors and on the phones.
Those conversations we have with voters are how we make sure Democrats secure the votes they need to win—and we need your help to make it happen.
So whether or not you live in one of our target districts or states, there are plenty of opportunities to get involved. You can join an in-person canvass near you, or you can join a virtual phonebank from the comfort of your own home.
Thank you for showing up for our democracy this weekend and every day until Election Day and beyond.
— The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. name: Kailee Buller
subject: Peter, I need you on my side
body:
We're 21 days out, and every moment counts now.

| | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Peter,
We are now 21 days away from Election Day.
When I started this campaign, I said it would be built from the ground up by the people of Central New York. You've been part of that from the start, and I'm grateful.
**But these final weeks are when races like ours are won or lost.**
Every conversation with a neighbor, every reminder to a friend, and every yard sign in a front lawn matters more now than at any point in this campaign.
That is why I'm asking you to become an official VICTORY CAPTAIN for Kailee Buller for Congress.
[**YES, I'LL BE A VICTORY CAPTAIN >>**](https://us.list-manage.com/SLm_L0JefyW?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
Here's what being a Victory Captain means...
Victory Captains are the people I'll count on most in the home stretch. You'll be the first to hear our closing plan, the first to get our final campaign updates, and the person your friends and family turn to when they want to know what's really at stake in this race.
_**We'll be counting on you to help make sure the people in your life have a plan to vote, to let us know who could use a yard sign, and to keep us in touch with what's happening in your corner of NY-22.**_
_**You'll be the reason voters who might have stayed home show up instead.**_
I'm running to lower costs, protect our communities, defend our farmers and small businesses, and make Central New York a place where our kids can build their futures. And I need people like you standing with me now, more than ever.
[ _So, Peter, will you be there?_](https://us.list-manage.com/VJoi9RyupRV?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
---

---

The clock is running, and I want my strongest supporters in place before the final push begins.
Thank you for being on this team. Let's finish this together.
Kailee BullerRepublican Candidate for Congress, NY-22

We'll be counting on you to help make sure the people in your life have a plan to vote, to let us know who could use a yard sign, and to keep us in touch with what's happening in your corner of NY-22. You'll be the reason voters who might have stayed home show up instead. I'm running to lower costs, protect our communities, defend our farmers and small businesses, and make Central New York a place where our kids can build their futures. And I need people like you standing with me now, more than ever. | | | The clock is running, and I want my strongest supporters in place before the final push begins. Thank you for being on this team. Let's finish this together. Just before the 2022 midterm elections, as polling showed Democrats were performing well with women voters, another conservative pastor and YouTuber, Joel Webbon, tweeted that “ the 19th Amendment was a bad idea.” He’s since used his large platform for misogynistic rants where he regularly advocates for revoking women’s rights. “ A woman as a mother is a precious gift, but a woman as a civil magistrate is the death of the nation ,” Webbon posted on social media this year. In 2024, Dale Partridge, another Christian nationalist pastor, posted on social media that “i n a Christian marriage, a wife should vote according to her husband’s direction.” In January 2025, Partridge said Congress should repeal the 19th Amendment because he thinks women are too empathetic. Even the powerful venture capitalist and conservative activist Peter Thiel once wrote that he thought the women’s suffrage movement was bad for democracy. One of Thiel's best friends in politics? Vice President J.D. Vance.The examples go on, but these extreme ideas need to be stopped before its too late. = | | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country. **TOP NEWS**
**“In a rare move, Gov. Greg Abbott defends Medicaid funding for Texas”** via [The Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Terri Langford** – Texas Gov. **Greg Abbott** is doubling down on the state’s fight to recover nearly $10 billion in Medicaid funding that the Trump administration is withholding from Texas hospitals.

“Texas is working with the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services to protect funding that helps hospitals serve Medicaid patients and keeps critical emergency care available,” **Andrew Mahaleris** , Abbott’s spokesman, said in a statement.

The statement comes two days after The Texas Tribune reported that the governor’s office had stepped into a nearly year-long impasse between the Texas Health and Human Services Commission and Washington over the funding. The money helps hospitals close the gap between their Medicaid reimbursements and the actual costs they incur for treating low-income Texans. _(__[TX TRIB](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“New polling on data centers shows how the issue could impact the midterms in Texas”** via [CBS News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s**Jack Fink** – With the midterm elections approaching, new polling data shows that data centers could play an important role in competitive elections this year.

A poll released by the Texas Politics Project at the University of Texas at Austin found that a majority of Texans oppose the construction of data centers in their communities. In a sample of 1,200 voters, 30% of respondents strongly or somewhat supported the construction of data centers in their community, while 57% strongly or somewhat opposed.

The poll also found that respondents are worried about the potential impact of data centers on their water supply, energy bills, environment and quality of life. However, they did feel data centers could have a positive impact on the economy locally, statewide and nationally.

**Jim Henson** spoke with **Jack Fink** for “Eye On Politics” this week about the results and what they could mean for November. Jack Fink and Jim Henson discussed the issue of data centers, with Henson noting that the issue has become a lightning rod for discontent about the data centers themselves and their impacts on communities, as well as discontent around AI and anti-corporate feelings. Jack Fink also mentioned **Gov. Abbott** ‘s focus on data centers during a property tax relief rally in the Tyler area, which Fink believed was a sign that Republicans are feeling the issue from rural areas. _(__[CBS News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Over 1.2 million Texans are on the voter “suspense list”. Here’s how to check your status.”** via [CBS News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.) – More than 1.2 million Texans, including 410,812 from North Texas counties, currently have a “suspensed”; voter status, according to the Texas Secretary of State’s office.

The good news? Being on the suspense list does not mean you lose your right to vote, but you will need to take a few quick steps to make sure your ballot counts.

County voter registrars place voters on the suspense list when official county mail is returned as undeliverable. Common triggers include:

Voters have until Oct. 5 to update their status. This is the deadline to register to vote. You can do this by visiting the Secretary of State’s website. You’ll need your current driver’s license or ID card, Social Security number and the Voter Unique Identifier Number from your Voter Registration Card. _(__[CBS News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Texas Governor Hits the Brakes on Flock Camera Funding”** via [Governing](https://link.mail.beehiiv.) – Gov. **Greg Abbott** has ordered all state agencies to pause funding for Flock cameras as scrutiny over the AI-powered surveillance devices has mounted.

The order came as The Texas Tribune was preparing to publish an investigation detailing how a state agency has devoted at least $30 million to building up the state’s Flock surveillance network by providing grants to local police departments.

Abbott gave the order on Aug. 26, 2026, to halt state funding for Flock cameras, his spokesman confirmed. “To the extent that cities get any funding for those cameras, most of it comes from the federal government. To the extent any funding comes from Texas agencies, those agencies are clarifying that those funds cannot be used for Flock cameras,” **Andrew Mahaleris** said in a statement shared first with the Tribune. _(__[Governing](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Texas hospitals expect to lose $27 million a day in Medicaid funding starting Tuesday”** via [The Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Terri Langford** – When the state’s new fiscal year begins on Tuesday, Texas hospitals expect to lose $27 million a day in additional Medicaid funding.

The shortfall is the result of a decision by the Trump administration to withhold approval from Texas for about $9.8 billion in the next year from three programs, the bulk of which affects the Comprehensive Hospital Increase Reimbursement Program (CHIRP). This program gives hospitals additional funding to cover the difference between Medicaid rate payments and the actual costs that hospitals incur to provide services to Medicaid patients. Essentially, hospitals, which often are paid less than what they can spend on Medicaid patients due to outdated payment rates set by the state, are losing out on their additional reimbursement for 2027.

Local governmental entities collect taxes from hospitals — about $4 billion a year, according to the Texas Hospital Association — and under CHIRP, the federal government matches those funds so that Texas hospitals can then use them to cover the actual costs of providing Medicaid services. Hospitals say those CHIRP dollars are critical and if they lose that funding, they will likely have to cut services to patients.

“It is impossible for a hospital to take a huge loss on a Medicaid side of their portfolio and not have that impact services across the board, regardless of what type of insurance a patient has,” said **Sara González** , a THA vice president of advocacy, public policy and political strategy. Four million low-income Texans are enrolled in Medicaid, most of them children. Dr. **Esmaeil Porsa** , president and CEO of Harris Health, said “The impacts would be catastrophic for Texas’ safety-net healthcare system,” **Robert Fries** , the chief financial officer for Children’s Health in Dallas said in a statement that this type of funding is crucial for children’s hospitals like Children’s Medical Center. Gov. **Greg Abbott** sent a pointed letter Aug. 7 to U.S. Health Secretary **Robert F. Kennedy Jr.** in which he stated that there’s nothing wrong with the way Texas hospitals’ local taxes are collected. **Anna Stelter** , the THA’s vice president of policy and **Carrie Kroll** , THA’s senior vice president of advocacy and public policy, also commented on the issue. _(__[TX TRIB](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“A Texas Banking Billionaire and His Children Are Locked in a Bitter Succession Drama”** via [WSJ](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s**Ben Glickman** – A family battle over a billionaire’s fortune, from boats and a jet to Dallas Cowboys tickets, is rankling the board of a small regional bank in Texas.

Texas banking veteran **Gerald J. Ford** is ensnarled in a legal fight with some of his adult children over a large stake in Hilltop Holdings, the $2.2 billion financial-services holding company he forged.

Four of Gerald J. Ford’s children—including son **Jeremy Ford** , who took over as chair from Gerald J. Ford in 2025—are suing to wrest away control of their father’s more-than-26% stake in Hilltop, worth some $600 million.

The battle is over the control of Gerald J. Ford’s stake in Hilltop Holdings, which is a significant portion of the company, and the outcome is still uncertain. _(__[WSJ](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“UT Arlington president stepping down to return to teaching”** via [Fort Worth Star-Telegram](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Maven Navarro** – University of Texas at Arlington President**Jennifer Cowley** announced Monday, Aug. 31, that she would step down from her role to teaching at the university.

Cowley was the first woman to serve as president of the university, a role she has held since 2022. The change is effective immediately.

“As I conclude my service as president, I do so with tremendous gratitude for what we have accomplished together, deep affection for this community, and great optimism for UTA’s future. I will never lose sight of what a privilege it is to help shape the lives of our students,” Cowley said in a statement.

UTA Chancellor **John Zerwas** said that when he learned of Cowley’s decision, he felt gratitude for her commitment to stay at the university. _(__[FWST](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_
