**2026**
**“Talarico Is Out-Fundraising Paxton and Flooding the Airwaves in Texas Senate Race”** via [WSJ](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Maggie Severns** and **Elizabeth Findell** – Senate candidate**James Talarico** began August in Massachusetts, standing beside a swimming pool on tony Nantucket, where more than 100 curious islanders gathered in sunglasses and sports coats to see what the bright-eyed Democrat on a hot streak in Texas was all about.

The event, held at the cedar-shingled home of a former Biden administration ambassador, came as James Talarico made a private East Coast swing that included August stops in Martha’s Vineyard, another Massachusetts vacation spot, and New York City, according to invitations that priced tickets between $500 and $13,500. _(__[WSJ](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Talarico needs to cut Paxton’s edge with rural Texans to win Senate race. Can he?”** via [Fort Worth Star-Telegram](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Eleanor Dearman** – In 2018, Texas’ Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate sought to run a different type of campaign. For years, liberal candidates had focused on Texas’ most populous areas — cities where Democrats largely resided. It was just a matter of getting them to turn out, the theory went.

But **Beto O’Rourke** wanted to try something new. He would famously stump in all of Texas’ 254 counties in his 2018 race against Sen. **Ted Cruz** , zigzagging to communities across Texas, small and large. He lost a close race. However, in some ways, the strategy worked.

**James Talarico** , the party’s nominee, needs votes from everywhere. He doesn’t have to win rural Texas; that’s practically impossible. But if he reduces **Ken Paxton** ’s advantage in counties concerned about water and private school vouchers, irritated over energy and grocery costs and angry about data centers, he improves his odds.

“We’re determined not to make those [campaign] mistakes of the past,” Talarico said recently, acknowledging Texas Democrats have sometimes neglected areas beyond the cities and suburbs. “It’s why we’re constantly showing up in rural communities, in our small towns. Why are we speaking” to the concerns of voters there. _(__[FWST](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Dark money in Texas Senate race spurs Talarico complaint to FEC against Paxton”** via [CBS News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Gabe Kaminsky** – Earlier this year, a super PAC supporting Texas Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton received four checks totaling over $1 million from an organization called Preserve Texas, Inc.

Preserve Texas is not registered as a political committee and has not filed paperwork with the Federal Election Commission that could reveal where the money came from. Instead, it is a Virginia-based nonprofit, incorporated by **John Plishka** , the treasurer for Paxton’s Senate campaign, according to corporate documents filed in Virginia.

The arrangement, part of the dramatic uptick in American politics of anonymous, big-dollar giving, has now drawn a complaint from the campaign of Paxton’s Democratic opponent, **James Talarico** , which accused Paxton and his treasurer of violating federal campaign finance rules. _(__[CBS News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Affordability crisis takes center stage in Texas races”** via [The Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Joshua Fechter** ,**Paul Cobler** , **Dan Keemahill** , **Terri Langford** and **Kayla Guo** – In a state once considered one of the most affordable places in the country, candidates have popped up at barbershops and in voters’ homes vowing to tackle a new problem for Texas: its cost-of-living woes.

“Affordability has become the defining issue of this cycle and the voters want candidates to speak on it,” said **Michael Adams** , a professor and director of the Master of Public Affairs Graduate Program at Texas Southern University.

From housing to groceries and gas, Texans’ regular expenses have risen considerably in the past several years. As those costs have grown, Texans have increasingly said the higher cost of living is one of the biggest problems facing the state.

In the state’s marquee Senate race, Republican **Ken Paxton** has floated tax breaks for families to help pay for health care and housing costs, and more ideas. Among the proposals from state Rep. **James Talarico** , his Democratic foe from Austin: abolishing the gas tax to help Texans’ transportation costs and expanding tax benefits for parents with kids. _(__[TX TRIB](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Gina Hinojosa focuses on kitchen table issues as polls show the Texas Governor’s race within five percentage points”** via [CBS News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s**Jack Fink** – Statewide polls show the top concern among Texans is inflation and higher prices, and Democratic gubernatorial candidate Gina Hinojosa said her campaign reflects that.

“Everyone’s done with the culture wars. Nobody has, really, the luxury to be focused on this. It’s about kitchen table issues. That’s what this campaign is about,” she said.

A new poll released last week by the Texas Politics Project at UT Austin shows Gina Hinojosa trailing three-term Republican incumbent **Greg Abbott** by five percentage points, 45-40 percent. 10% are undecided, while 38% of Independents said they’re undecided. Two months ago, the same poll had Abbott leading Hinojosa by seven percentage points. In the Real Clear Politics average of polls between June 3 and August 24, Abbott leads by 4.7 percentage points, 48.6 percent to 43.9 percent.

Last week, Abbott’s campaign began advertising on TV, and the Governor maintains a sizable campaign war chest with about $67 million cash on hand as of June 30th. In an interview, Hinojosa was asked how she is going to keep this a tight race as the Governor starts spending on advertising. _(__[CBS News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Former GOP Texas Supreme Court justices back Democrat for attorney general”** via [The Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Eleanor Klibanoff** – Two former Texas Supreme Court justices appointed by Republican governors are endorsing Democratic attorney general nominee Nathan Johnson over their party’s pick, **Mayes Middleton**.

The race to replace outgoing Attorney General **Ken Paxton** as Texas’ top lawyer is, like many races this cycle, running tighter than usual. While Republicans have held the seat since **John Cornyn** was elected in 1998, several polls have **Nathan Johnson** within five points of Middleton.

**Tom Phillips** , who broke the Democrats’ stranglehold on the high court with his appointment as chief justice in 1987, and **Deborah Hankinson** , an appointee of then-Gov. **George W. Bush** , say they support Nathan Johnson’s nonpartisan approach to the agency. The attorney general’s office, which defends state agencies and statutes against legal challenges, frequently intersects with the state’s highest civil court, which has the final say on such cases.

“For attorney general, I look at who will follow the law and who will operate the office efficiently,” Phillips said. “That’s been Nathan Johnson’s emphasis, and Mayes Middleton’s has been more about using the office as a political tool to advance certain agendas.” _(__[TX TRIB](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Despite outrage, Tarrant County approves 30% reduction in voting sites for November”** via [Fort Worth Star-Telegram](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Rachel Royster** – Tarrant County will have 224 Election Day and 47 early voting polling locations for the November midterm election after numerous calls for more to be added to the original list.

Last month, Elections Administrator **Clint Ludwig** presented a suggested list of polling locations that offered to use roughly half the number of sites that were used in the 2022 midterm election. The Commissioners Court entirely opposed the slash, saying it was far too drastic.

In their marathon 10-hour meeting Tuesday, the commissioners voted along party lines to approve 29% fewer Election Day and 6% fewer early voting centers compared to the November 2022 lists.

Democrat Commissioner **Alisa Simmons** requested several sites be added to the early voting list and almost 150 be added to Election Day. The amendment was turned down because many of the early voting sites were unavailable or gave the southern precincts more locations than the northern precincts had. _(__[FWST](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_
|
---
**STATE GOVERNMENT**
**“Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick targets schools over 2,000 books he says are ‘vulgar’”** via [Spectrum News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.) – Texas Lt. Gov. **Dan Patrick** announced last month that he will try to remove what he deems inappropriate books from school libraries.

His message was clear and simple at an Aug. 19 news conference. “We’re coming for the books,” Dan Patrick said.

Dan Patrick said this latest effort comes after school districts were not following the law — Senate Bill 13 — which called for districts to create more transparency over what books are in their schools’ catalogs. Dan Patrick said over 2,000 titles are subject to removal. If the districts choose not to remove the books, Dan Patrick said he will urge the Legislature to consider another law that, if passed, could mean some districts could be taken over by the Texas Education Agency (TEA).

Among the 2,000 titles was “Let’s Talk About It ” by **Erika Moen** and **Matthew Nolan** , a sex education book created for teenagers. “So filthy, so dirty, so vulgar, so pornographic, and for the ladies here, I wouldn’t even want to show you,” Dan Patrick said. **Bonnie Wallace** of the religious values-based group Recover America provided a list of 14 school districts in Texas that have the book. Spectrum News was able to independently verify that at least 12 of the districts have the book, including in some of the state’s major metro areas like Austin, San Antonio, El Paso, as well as McAllen, Killeen and Galveston. _(__[Spectrum News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“At least 14 Texas districts at risk of school takeovers next year”** via [The Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Megan Menchaca** – More than a dozen Texas public school districts are at risk of triggering a potential state takeover if they do not improve student academic performance before the next year’s A-F accountability ratings, data shows.

At least 14 districts had at least one campus with a fourth consecutive failing grade, according to the preliminary 2026 ratings. That includes the Clarksville, Cleveland, Coldspring-Oakhurst, Elgin, Judson, Kingsville, Manor, Nacogdoches, Poteet, Runge, San Angelo, San Antonio, Spring and Waco school districts.

The majority of the at-risk districts are concentrated in the Austin, Houston or San Antonio metro areas, with an average enrollment of about 11,700 students. Nearly every school eligible to trigger future state action has a larger percentage of low-income students than the state average, as well as higher rates of Black and Hispanic students. _(__[TX TRIB](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Texas’ divisive overhaul of high school social studies lessons set to conclude this week”** via [The Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s**Jaden Edison** – A rewrite of what Texas high schoolers learn in history, government and geography is expected to receive final approval this week.

The Texas State Board of Education will decide, for example, whether public school students must learn how “biblical imagery and founding principles of equality and justice from the Declaration of Independence” connect to **Martin Luther King Jr.** ’s “I Have a Dream” speech.

The board members will debate a recommendation that students learn about early Islam through the lens of “the Prophet Mohammed’s brutal military campaigns against Jewish and Christian tribes, the normalization of slavery, and the taking of female captives as harem slaves.”

Another proposal would ensure students graduate with the ability to describe arguments against “the modern welfare state that emerged from continued expansion of Great Society programs.” The Great Society refers to President **Lyndon B. Johnson** ’s 1960s policy agenda that sought to abolish poverty and inequality. _(__[TX TRIB](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

Abbott announces $138B investment in Texas transportation”** via [Community Impact](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Ashton Yeaman** – The office of Gov. **Greg Abbott** announced a $138 billion investment in Texas transportation infrastructure, including projects in the Greater Houston region, according to an Aug. 27 news release from the Texas Department of Transportation.

The Unified Transportation Program was approved during an August meeting of the Texas Transportation Commission.

The program’s funding is divided into two portions, $95 billion for transportation projects across the state, and $43 billion which is reserved for routine maintenance and development. The total of $138 billion is intended to be spent on projects and maintenance over the next 10 years, according to the news release. _(__[COMMUNITY IMPACT](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Lawmakers added $1 to Texans’ car insurance policies. The money paid for thousands of Flock cameras.”** via [The Washington Post](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Ayden Runnels** – In 2023, the Texas Legislature unanimously passed a law raising auto insurance costs for Texans by $1 to combat rampant catalytic converter theft. Three years later, a little-known state agency has devoted at least $30 million of that fee toward supercharging the state’s Flock surveillance network, placing cameras along highways and streets from El Paso to the Louisiana border, an analysis by The Texas Tribune found.

The Motor Vehicle Crime Prevention Authority, led by a board mostly appointed by Gov. **Greg Abbott** , has turned the $1 fee hike into at least 3,200 Flock cameras. The agency has awarded no fewer than 95 grants to help law enforcement agencies purchase and maintain about 2,000 Flock cameras. Another $15.9 million is helping the Texas Department of Public Safety add almost 1,200 more.

**Miguel Rodriguez** , chair of the Motor Vehicle Crime Prevention Authority, said during an August 2023 meeting that he hoped to use proceeds from the fee increase to “cover the entire state” with cameras. Rodriguez, who is also the Laredo Police Chief, sees the cameras as a powerful law enforcement tool, particularly to combat criminal organizations.

But on Friday evening, after multiple requests for comment from the Tribune about its findings, Abbott’s office said the governor was pausing all state funding for local grants to be used for Flock cameras. “To the extent that cities get any funding for those cameras, most of it comes from the federal government. To the extent any funding comes from Texas agencies, those agencies are clarifying that those funds cannot be used for Flock cameras,” **Andrew Mahaleris** , Abbott spokesperson, said in a statement shared first with the Tribune. _(__[WAPO](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Comptroller requests doubling Texas school voucher program to $2 billion”** via [Houston Public Media](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Kyle McClenagan** – Texas’ chief financial officer requested that lawmakers double the amount of money available for the state’s private school voucher program, resulting in a total of more than $2 billion.

In the appropriations request for 2028–29 biennium, Texas Comptroller **Don Huffines** asked the Legislature to raise the program’s base funding by $1 billion so more families can use taxpayer money to cover private school or home schooling costs.

Officials from the comptroller’s office noted Thursday that the request was based on the number of current participants and students on the waitlist, as required by state law. Huffines also wants for an additional $226 million to accommodate funding increases for families currently participating in the program, which launched this school year.

The Texas State Teachers Association on Thursday criticized the budget request, saying taxpayers need more information on who has signed up to receive voucher funding before raising the program’s price tag. Recent state data shows that 70% of families who joined or have pending invites to the program already attended a private school or home-school. _(__[Houston Public Media](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“4 in 10 Texas homeowners pay no school taxes. State leaders want to go further.”** via [Houston Chronicle](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s**Sam González Kelly** – Nearly 40% of Texas homeowners paid nothing in school property taxes last year after a decade of incremental increases to homestead exemptions, according to a analysis presented Tuesday by state Sen. **Paul Bettencourt** , R-Houston.

The finding foreshadows a key focus for lawmakers in the coming months, as Lt. Gov. **Dan Patrick** in March directed the Senate Local Government Committee , which Paul Bettencourt chairs, to assess the impact of the increased homestead exemptions with an eye toward raising them even further in the 2027 legislative session, which starts in January. Gov. **Greg Abbott** , meanwhile, has his own plan to eliminate homeowners’ school taxes , leaving only businesses to foot that bill.

The Legislature last year raised the homestead exemption — the amount a homeowner can deduct from the taxable value of their residence — to $140,000 for most homeowners and to $200,000 for those over age 65 or with disabilities. It was the fourth time lawmakers have raised the homestead exemption since 2015, when it was just $15,000 for standard homeowners and $25,000 for seniors.

Paul Bettencourt’s committee staff found that 39% of all homeowners did not pay any school property taxes following the latest hike to the homestead exemption, up from 28% in 2024. Among seniors and disabled Texans, 61% of homeowners paid no school taxes. These homeowners’ school tax bills also have long been frozen at the amount they paid in the first year they qualified for either exemption. State Sen. **Molly Cook** said renters don’t benefit from the higher homestead exemptions, and argued the state cannot always rely on hefty surpluses to fill in the gaps left by lost tax revenue. _(__[HOU CHRON](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

The proposed desalination plant was intended to provide a drought-proof source of drinking water, but opponents questioned its high cost and the environmental impact of its salty discharge on Corpus Christi Bay.

The vote was being watched by Gov. **Greg Abbott** , who criticized the City Council after it rejected the plant one year ago, saying the state might have to “micromanage” the city to protect the region’s water supply.

Outreach teams visited some sites multiple times, and most of the costs came from staff salaries and contractor payments.

That was one of the key takeaways from a presentation Austin’s Homeless Strategies and Operations office gave the city council’s public health committee Wednesday.

That increase represents a $44 annual increase in property taxes for a median home value of $372,638.

The highest the tax rate could be is 13.5195 cents per $100 home value. The current rate is 11.8023 with an annual bill of $460 for a home with the median value. If an 8% increase is approved by the hospital district’s board of managers on Sept. 9 and then by the Travis County commissioners on Sept. 15, Central Health’s budget will hit the $1 billion mark for the first time. Central Health is tasked with caring for people making less than 200% of the federal poverty level. That 200% is $31,920 for a single person and $66,000 for a family of four. Each year, the hospital district has been offering more direct care through its specialty care clinics, which began in 2022; a medical respite center that opened in 2025 and its CommUnityCare federally qualified health centers, which grew out of the city and county clinics. _(__[AAS](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Brownsville faces higher tax bills as SpaceX presence grows”** via [The Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Berenice Garcia** – Home values in Cameron County more than doubled over a six-year period, and property tax bills are going up along with it, according to research from the Texas Real Estate Research Center at Texas A&M; University.

SpaceX’s arrival in 2014 has led to the area’s rapid rise in wealth, which researchers suspect also contributed to the rise in property values. And with the expansion of SpaceX and other industries in the Brownsville area, researchers expect home values to go up even further.

For longtime residents of Brownsville, the largest city in the county, rising property values could mean rising tax bills. And for some, that means being priced out of their homes, one local real estate agent warns.

Krebs** , an economist with the Texas Real Estate Research Center at Texas A&M; University, said the increase in property taxes could similarly be attributed to newer, more expensive homes built during that time. _(__[TX TRIB](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

The rollout of the gold-colored Teslas, which give passengers no way to take control in an emergency, comes as the company prepares to launch the service in other cities. Tesla shares have suffered amid a slump in vehicle sales, but they rose more than 5% Thursday on hopes that the futuristic-looking taxis will catch on quickly.

Tesla trails self-driving taxi leader Waymo in the number of cabs deployed and trips completed. The PUC, the state agency responsible for economic regulation of the state’s electric and water utilities, voted unanimously on Friday, August 28 to amend Dallas-based electric company Oncor’s certificates of convenience and necessity — a permit that authorizes a company to provide a public service — for two of the five 765-kilovolt (kV) transmission lines that make up the drafted Permian Basin Reliability Plan network. body:
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3988%2E21716%2E9DJKEI)
I hope you’re well! I’m reaching out because I know how much you care about helping Democrats take back the House Majority.
Democratic candidates across the country are hitting the ground in their districts and working tirelessly to communicate their message to voters in order to win in November and deliver for the American people in Congress.
Through the Red Alert program, the DCCC is highlighting Frontline Members and Red to Blue candidates in some of the tightest races in the country. With less than 30 days until Election Day, [_**they need your help.**_](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1588?t=2&akid=3988%2E21716%2E9DJKEI)
**DCCC Red Alert Round #3**
**Frontline Members:**
Rep. Susie Lee (NV-03)
Rep. Tom Suozzi (NY-03)
Rep. Marcy Kaptur (OH-09)
**Red to Blue Candidates:**
Chris Jones (AR-02)
Amish Shah (AZ-01)
Manny Rutinel (CO-08)
Pia Dandiya (FL-22)
Cait Conley (NY-17)
Bob Harvie (PA-01)
Nancy Lacore (SC-01)
Mitchell Berman (WI-01)
Republicans know that **Susie Lee (NV-03), Tom Suozzi (NY-03)** **and Marcy Kaptur (OH-09)** won’t be easy to beat, so Donald Trump and Republican super PACs are spending millions against them. They need the resources to continue fighting back and communicating with voters in their districts.
**Chris Jones (AR-02)** was just added to the DCCC Red to Blue list, because he has put this traditionally Republican seat on the map. Chris is a 7th-generation Arkansan raised by parents who were both ministers. He has what it takes to win in November and flip this seat blue.
**Dr. Amish Shah (AZ-01)** is an emergency room physician who came within just 4% of flipping this district in 2024 – one of the closest margins of the cycle. Now an open seat, this is one of Democrats’ top pick up opportunities in 2026.
**Manny Rutinel (CO-08)** is running in one of the most competitive House districts in the country. The son of a single mom who immigrated from Latin America, Manny is running hard through the finish line as everyday Coloradans grow even more sour on Gabe Evans and Donald Trump’s disastrous agenda.
A working mom, educator and Palm Beach native, **Pia Dandiya (FL-22)** represents the people-first values that Congress needs while her self-funder opponent has endorsed Trump’s cost-spiking tariffs and One Big Ugly Bill. This district was redrawn by corrupt Florida Republicans to benefit the GOP, but Pia is putting the seat in reach.
**Cait Conley (NY-17)** is running against one of only _three_ Republicans in a Congressional district that Kamala Harris won in 2024. Cait is a combat veteran who is ready to win this seat in November and retire MAGA extremist Mike Lawler.
In another seat that Kamala Harris won last cycle, Republicans have spent over _$3 million dollars_ attacking **Bob Harvie (PA-01)** , but poll after poll shows that this race is in a dead heat.
**Nancy Lacore (SC-01)** served our nation for 35 years in the Navy, a career that began as a helicopter pilot and culminated as a three star admiral and the Chief of Navy Reserve where she was entrusted to lead more than 60,000 sailors. Now, Nancy is running for Congress in SC-01, in a race she can win if she has the resources to communicate and get out the vote.
**Mitchell Berman (WI-01)** is uniquely positioned to flip this district in November. As an ER nurse who has seen firsthand how patients struggle to get care because of Republican policies, Mitch is committed to standing up to corruption and special interests in Washington.
[**Could you donate now to support these 11 candidates and help take back the House?**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1588?t=3&akid=3988%2E21716%2E9DJKEI)
Thank you for all you do to help House Democrats. Together, we can take back the House Majority, and continue our fight to improve the lives of all Americans.
All my best,
Sarah McBride

body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTQwMjI4NjcS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjU2MDA3MzMxNQS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
Tell the U.S. Census Bureau: Hands Off Our Census!

While you’re busy voting, the Trump administration is trying to rig future
elections with changes to the 2030 Census rules. They think we won’t notice. But we’re paying attention, and we won’t be silenced.

The proposed changes to the 2030 Census would exclude large groups of people —
people who matter and who need to be counted. When our communities aren’t
represented in the data, we lose out on our fair share of resources and
political representation. An accurate census count is critical to protecting our
communities, our environment, and our democracy.

The comment period closes November 2 — we all need to speak up today. Add your name and urge the Census Bureau to extend the comment deadline and
reject these dangerous exclusionary rules.

Tell the U.S. Census Bureau: Hands Off Our Census! https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/KybpT- ADD YOUR NAME https://links.messages.lcv. Peter, While communities are focused on protecting voting rights this election season,
Trump is sneakily seeking to rig future elections — by changing the 2030 Census rules. They think we won’t notice. But we’re paying attention, and we won’t be silenced. Tell the Census Bureau: hands off our census! https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/_4bqMEpZyDh- TAKE ACTION NOW https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/3Z0ec- An accurate census count is critical to protecting our communities and
environment. Census data determines how billions of dollars of environmental
funding is distributed across the country. This includes funding for water and
waste disposal systems, public transportation infrastructure, and disaster
relief on which we all rely. The data collected will also inform research to
identify and address environmental injustices. When our communities aren’t represented in the data, we lose out on our fair
share of resources and political representation. The proposed changes would
exclude or skew data for large groups of people — people who matter and who need
to be counted. The changes would impact U.S. residents, including visa-holders,
refugees, and asylum seekers; people who are currently incarcerated; seasonal
workers; children in foster care; and military families, among many others. We
can’t let this happen. Urge the Census Bureau today: extend the comment deadline and reject these proposed rules >> https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/8wqzCjkLz~ Thank you for helping build a more equitable America, for all people and the
planet. Yours in the movement, Justin Kwasa

| | THIS PAST WEEK...
# **MY FIRST TV ADS WILL BE ON AIR!**
In my previous campaigns, I never had enough money to run a single TV ad. This year, thanks to YOU, my grassroots supporters, we finally did it!

This is a big milestone for me.

Watch ["American Dream"](https://us.list-manage.com/16d2gqOoLz_?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c) and ["Complaints Department"](https://us.list-manage.com/an1M9HlEYkO?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c), and please share them with your friends and family. How do you think they turned out?
# **ASK ME ANYTHING IN JAFFREY & THE UNH CARSEY FORUM**
Where I grew up, we weren't allowed to question the people in power.

That's why I love my [Ask Me Anything town halls](https://us.list-manage.com/1Ao9IaKBjYZ?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c) so much. Thank you, Jaffrey, for your tough and thoughtful questions!

The next night, I made my case at the [UNH Carsey Candidate Policy Forum in Concord](https://us.list-manage.com/t8EioCT681I?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c) to keep the American Dream affordable for every Granite Stater.

# 23 DAYS TO GO...
**A PACKED WEEK AHEAD**

---
|
**COME JOIN ME @ THESE UPCOMING EVENTS**

SWEENEY AUDITORIUM, NHTI – CONCORD'S COMMUNITY COLLEGE
31 COLLEGE DRIVE
Concord, NH
Free and open to the public. The mic is yours. Bring your questions.
# **WEDNESDAY 10/14, 5:30 PM - FIRESIDE CHAT WITH LILY - DARTMOUTH**
Rockefeller Center for Public Policy, Dartmouth College, Hanover
A moderated conversation about my background and policy priorities, followed by audience Q&A. Watch the livestream on Dartmouth's YouTube channel.
# **THURSDAY 10/15, 6:00 PM - NHPR CANDIDATE FORUM - KEENE**
Brewbaker Cafe, Keene (doors open at 5:00 PM)
A forum with a panel of New Hampshire journalists asking questions submitted by voters. Free and open to the public, but please register in advance [here](https://us.list-manage.com/7Yl7oegxUeX?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c).
It will stream on NHPR on Friday 10/16 at 9:00 AM or 7:00 PM.
# **SATURDAY 10/17 - TEAM LILY AT THE KEENE PUMPKIN FESTIVAL & BERLIN RIVERFIRE**
Keene Pumpkin Festival: Central Square, Downtown Keene, 2:00 PM - 7:30 PM. Free.
RiverFire: Heritage Park, 942 Main Street, Berlin, all day. $5 admission (kids 5 and under free).
Help Team Lily meet voters in Cheshire and Coös counties!

If you are able to participate, please email CM@lily4congress.com to confirm meeting up with Team Lily.
# **SUNDAY 10/18, 1:30 PM - 3PM "ASK ME ANYTHING" TOWN HALL - LITTLETON**
LITTLETON COMMUNITY CENTER
120 MAIN STREET
Littleton, NH
Free and open to the public. Bring your questions. North Country friends, I hope to see you there!

| **Hi Friends!**

We’re in the home stretch, and **Election Day is just three weeks away!** Thank you to everyone who has donated, volunteered, shared our posts, and helped spread the word about our campaign.

**There’s one more important way you can help: volunteer at the polls. We need volunteers across NC-08 to greet voters and share our campaign literature during early voting and on Election Day.**

Early voting begins Thursday, October 15, and runs through Saturday, October 31. Election Day is Tuesday, November 3. Poll locations and early-voting hours vary by county.

Reply to this email if you’re interested and we’ll get you plugged in!

We’re so close to the finish line. Let’s make these final weeks count!

**Onward to Victory.**

body:
[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=partner_em261013ke_demandjusticepac.cdVo-V&refcode=em20261013-61902&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1001&akid=61902%2E1407376%2EK891QQ ]A picture of Keith Ellison.

Republican megadonors are pouring millions into attack ads against me, and
I want to be honest with you about where things stand.

Earlier this summer, public polling had me up eight points. Then our race
was tied. Now, for the first time this year, a poll shows my Republican
opponent, Ron Schutz, ahead.

This is exactly what those millions were meant to do. And you can bet
Trump’s MAGA allies are looking at these numbers and deciding how much
more to pour into Minnesota.

They want an Attorney General who will look the other way when powerful
interests put profits, politics, and power ahead of people. They know I
won’t.

I have never backed down from those fights, and I’m not starting now. But
I need your help to fight back.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=partner_em261013ke_demandjusticepac.cdVo-V&refcode=em20261013-61902&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=61902%2E1407376%2EK891QQ ]Will you split a donation between Demand Justice PAC and my campaign so
we can answer these attacks and reach the voters who will decide this
race?

As the People’s Lawyer, it’s my job to help people afford their lives and
live with safety, dignity, and respect. That’s why I’ve taken on Big
Pharma, stood up for workers who were cheated, and fought back when Donald
Trump abused his power.

That’s the record I’m proud to run on—and the work I’m asking you to help
me continue.

But with Republican megadonors spending millions to distort that record,
we have to make sure voters hear the truth. Your support helps us run our
own ads and keep our organizers in the field, talking directly with
Minnesotans who are still making up their minds.

We can’t match MAGA megadonors dollar for dollar—and we don’t need to. But
we cannot let them spend the rest of this race telling voters who I am
without hearing from us.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=partner_em261013ke_demandjusticepac.cdVo-V&refcode=em20261013-61902&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=61902%2E1407376%2EK891QQ ]Team,
will you chip in whatever works for you, split between Demand Justice PAC
and my campaign, to help us turn this around, win, and keep fighting for
justice?

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=partner_em261013ke_demandjusticepac.cdVo-V&amount=5&refcode=em20261013-61902&t=1022&akid=61902%2E1407376%2EK891QQ ]Donate $5 ››

Thank you for standing with me,

Keith Ellison
